6.9.5 Target IBI Credit Counting
2947 If field IBI_CREDIT_COUNT_EN in register HC_CAPABILITIES (Section 7.4.4) has a value of 1'b1, then the
2948 Host Controller also supports an Target IBI credit counting mechanism, which allows the Driver to manage
2949 the credits for each Target. Target IBI credit counting is intended for use on I3C Buses where I3C Targets
2950 send frequent IBI Requests with data payloads, and when the Driver needs to manage incoming IBI
2951 Requests and ensure that it has sufficient memory to handle the IBI payload data.
2952 When this mechanism is enabled, the Host Controller shall conditionally ACK or NACK a Target’s IBI
2953 Request, based on the available credits for that Target in the Target IBI Credit Counters Extended
2954 Capability structure (see Section 7.7.5). If the Host Controller supports this mechanism, then it shall also
2955 include this Extended Capability structure. Each Target’s credit counter is stored in a register within the
2956 Extended Capability structure, and the Host Controller shall consume credits (i.e., shall decrement the
2957 counter) as data bytes are received. All Target credit counters shall be cleared when the Host Controller is
2958 reset, or when the Target IBI credit counting mechanism is disabled (i.e., when the Driver clears field R/S in
2959 register TARGET_CREDIT_CONFIG, see Section 7.7.5.2).
2960 Note:
2961 The Extended Capability structure has an array of registers, with one register for each Target. The
2962 size of the array is the same as the number of DAT entries (see Section 8.1), and each register for
2963 a Target corresponds to its DAT entry (i.e., has the same positional index).
2964 When this mechanism is enabled, the Host Controller shall ignore field IBI_REJECT in the Target’s
2965 DAT entry. Conversely, when this mechanism is disabled, the Host Controller shall use field
2966 IBI_REJECT in the DAT entry to determine whether to accept or reject the IBI Request.
2967 As each IBI Request arrives, the Host Controller checks the credit counter for that Target, to see whether
2968 the IBI Request is allowed. If there is not sufficient credit, then the Host Controller shall NACK the IBI
2969 Request, and shall then immediately send the DISEC Direct CCC with the ‘DISINT’ bit set, to tell the Target
2970 to disable subsequent IBI Requests.
2971 Note:
2972 Per the I3C Specification [MIPI05] at Section 5.1.6.2, the Controller may NACK an IBI Request
2973 and also send the DISEC CCC to disable sending subsequent IBI Requests. I3C Targets are
2974 allowed to send IBI Requests by default, unless configured to not send them via the DISEC CCC
2975 (per [MIPI05] Section 5.1.9.3.1). However, as noted in I3C FAQ [MIPI08] entry Q18.20, disabling
2976 IBI Requests only affects an I3C Target’s ability to send IBI Requests, it does not prevent an I3C
2977 Target from enqueueing new IBI Requests that would be sent a later time, as and when the
2978 Controller sends the ENEC CCC to re-enable sending IBI Requests.
2979 However, if there is sufficient credit when the IBI Request is received, then the Host Controller shall ACK
2980 the IBI Request, and shall prepare to receive the IBI data payload and optional Auto-Command data (e.g.,
2981 Pending Read). As the data arrives, the Host Controller shall automatically decrement the credit counter
2982 based on the length of the data received, per the value of field CREDIT_BYTE_COUNT in register
2983 TARGET_CREDIT_CONFIG. One credit shall be consumed for the IBI Request and its Mandatory Data Byte,
2984 followed by one credit for every K bytes of additional IBI payload data or subsequent Pending Read
2985 payload data, where the value K is determined by 2 to the power of (1 plus the value in field
2986 CREDIT_BYTE_COUNT).
2987 Note:
2988 If the IBI data payload or Pending Read data payload is not exactly aligned to the byte count for a
2989 credit, then the Host Controller shall decrement the credit counter by 1 for the last portion of the
2990 data payload, i.e., the partial byte count. If an IBI Request has a data payload of either zero bytes
2991 (i.e., no MDB) or one byte (i.e., MDB only), then the Host Controller shall decrement the credit
2992 counter by 1.
2993 If the Target’s credit counter reaches zero during (or at the very end of) an IBI Request or a subsequent
2994 Pending Read, then the Host Controller shall automatically send the DISEC Direct CCC with the ‘DISINT’
106 Copyright © 2018–2023 MIPI Alliance, Inc.
Public Release Edition

Version 1.2 Specification for I3C HCI
15-Feb-2023
2995 bit set after the end of the data payload, to tell the Target to disable subsequent IBI Requests. The Host
2996 Controller shall conditionally terminate the read if the credit counter reaches zero, per the value of field
2997 TERM_READ_ZERO_CREDIT in register TARGET_CREDIT_N (where N is the index of both the register array
2998 and the Target’s DAT entry).
2999 Note:
3000 If field TERM_READ_ZERO_CREDIT is set to 1’b0, then the Host Controller shall continue reading
3001 data bytes from the Target even if the credit counter reaches zero during the read. The Driver
3002 should prepare to read up to the maximum expected length of the IBI data payload (or subsequent
3003 Pending Read data payload); in most cases, this requires the Driver to have sufficient memory to
3004 handle the data payload that would exceed the allotted credit count.
3005 If field TERM_READ_ZERO_CREDIT is set to 1’b1, then the Host Controller shall terminate the read
3006 of the data payload when the credit counter reaches zero (i.e., if the Target did not use the T-Bit to
3007 indicate the end of the payload). The Host Controller shall indicate this condition by setting field
3008 ERROR to 1'b1 in the last IBI Status Descriptor.
3009 After the credit reaches zero, the Driver should subsequently increment the credit counter if it wishes the
3010 Host Controller to accept subsequent IBI Requests from that Target. The Driver may update the available
3011 credit by writing to register TARGET_CREDIT_N in one of two ways:
3012 • Incrementing the credit counter, when field CREDIT_INCR is set to 1’b1, and field CREDIT_COUNT holds
3013 the number of credits to increment.
3014 • If the value written to field CREDIT_COUNT would cause the Target’s credit counter to exceed the
3015 maximum value, then the Host Controller shall constrain this to the maximum value. The maximum
3016 value is a function of the value of field CREDIT_MAX_SIZE in register TARGET_CREDIT_TABLE (see
3017 Section 7.7.5.1).
3018 • If the Target’s credit counter was previously zero when the Host Controller applied the update, then the
3019 Host Controller shall automatically send the ENEC Direct CCC with the ‘ENINT’ bit set, to tell the
3020 Target to enable IBI Requests.
3021 • Decrementing the credit counter, when field CREDIT_DECR is set to 1’b1, and field CREDIT_COUNT holds
3022 the number of credits to decrement.
3023 • If the Target’s credit counter is already zero, then the Host Controller shall discard the update.
3024 • If the value written to field CREDIT_COUNT would cause the Target’s credit counter to go below zero,
3025 then the Host Controller shall constrain this to zero. The Host Controller shall also automatically send
3026 the DISEC Direct CCC with the ‘DISINT’ bit set, to tell the Target to disable IBI Requests.
3027 Note:
3028 The Driver shall not set both bits CREDIT_INCR and CREDIT_DECR to 1’b1 when writing to register
3029 TARGET_CREDIT_N. If the Host Controller sees both of these bits set during a register write, then it
3030 shall discard the update.
3031 If fields CREDIT_INCR and CREDIT_DECR are both set to 1’b0, then the Host Controller shall not
3032 update the Target’s IBI credit counter, and shall generate an IBI credit acknowledgement report that
3033 contains the current value of the credit counter.
3034 As the Host Controller processes the credit update request, it will first wait for the IBI credit update FSM to
3035 reach an idle state (i.e., no IBI Request is being received; see Figure 26 below), ensure there is space in the
3036 IBI Queue/Ring to enqueue the acknowledgement report (see below), and then apply the increment or
3037 decrement operation to the current value in the Target’s credit counter. After applying the update, the Host
3038 Controller shall generate an IBI credit acknowledgement report that is a special form of an IBI Status
3039 Descriptor (see Section 8.6.4) that contains the status of the update.
3040 Note:
3041 If the IBI Queue (for PIO Mode) or IBI Ring (for DMA Mode) is full when the Host Controller sees
3042 the register write to update the credit, then the Host Controller shall delay applying the update until
3043 there is sufficient space to enqueue the IBI Status Descriptor and the single DWORD. When
3044 sufficient space is available, the report shall be enqueued into the IBI Queue/Ring with highest
3045 priority.

3050  eventually generate an IBI Status Descriptor with a value of 1’b1 in field IBI_STS, to report that the new
3051  request was dropped.
3052  The Host Controller shall use the FSM shown in Figure 26, to manage updates to a Target’s credit counter.

6.10 Managed CCC Transfer Framing Model
3069 The Host Controller supports the Managed CCC Transfer Framing model defined in Section 6.3 of the I3C
3070 TCRI Specification [MIPI06] and its sub-sections. Additional specifications in this section address details
3071 particular to specific HCI operating modes.
6.10.1 Direct CCCs and NACK Retry
3072 The DAT allows the Driver to configure the NACK retry count for typical Transfer Commands to particular
3073 I3C Targets. However, this is handled differently for Direct CCCs.
3074 When processing a Transfer Command that is a Direct CCC:
3075 If the indicated Device NACKs its Dynamic Address along with the RnW bit, then:
3076 • The Host Controller shall attempt to retry the Direct CCC at least once following the first NACK, per
3077 the following conditions:
3078 • If the value of the appropriate field DEV_NACK_RETRY_CNT (i.e., from the indicated Device’s DAT
3079 entry) indicates no retries for NACKed transfers, then the Host Controller shall always attempt one
3080 retry for a NACKed Direct CCC, per the I3C Specification’s mandatory single-retry model (see the
3081 I3C Specification at Section 5.1.9.2.3 [MIPI02]).
3082 • However, if the value of the appropriate field DEV_NACK_RETRY_CNT indicates any additional
3083 retries, then the Host Controller shall retry according to that field’s setting.
3084 • If the indicated Device NACKs its Dynamic Address repeatedly, beyond the retry count determined by
3085 the above conditions, then this shall be reported as an error per Section 6.10.3.
6.10.2 Providing Data for Broadcast/Direct Write CCCs
3086 When enqueueing Transfer Commands for CCCs that write data to a Target, the software shall observe the
3087 following requirements.
3088 For PIO Mode: The Data bytes for Broadcast, Direct Write, or Direct SET CCC segments shall be
3089 populated on the Data Queue as a sequence of DWORD writes, in an appropriate order for each Command
3090 Descriptor not using Immediate Data Bytes. Software should generally attempt to write all the Data to the
3091 Data Queue before writing any Command Descriptors to the Command Queue (see Section 6.8.1). All such
3092 Command Descriptors should be written to the Command Queue in sequential order.
3093 For DMA Mode: Each Command Descriptor shall be contained in a Transfer Descriptor structure (see
3094 Section 8.3). For Direct Write or Direct SET CCC segments, the relevant Data pointer for each Transfer
3095 Descriptor structure shall point to the Data buffer for the corresponding Target Device. If using multiple
3096 Transfer Commands for CCCs sent in continuous framing, then the first Transfer Descriptor shall point to
3097 the Data for the first Target, the second Transfer Descriptor structure shall point to the Data for the second
3098 Target, etc. If using Broadcast CCCs, then each Transfer Descriptor structure shall point to the data for that
3099 Broadcast CCC; these may optionally be mixed with other Direct CCC segments, or be mixed with other
3100 Broadcast CCCs, or be sent individually. All of the Transfer Descriptors that form such a CCC transfer shall
3101 be posted to same Ring Bundle, and shall be contiguous (i.e., shall not be interleaved with other Command
3102 Descriptors). Software should generally prepare and enqueue these Transfer Descriptors in one operation,
3103 before updating the Enqueue Pointer (see Section 6.8.2).
3104 For additional details, refer to Section 6.3.1.1 of the I3C TCRI Specification.

6.10.3 Error Handling for CCC Flows
3105 As the Host Controller processes each Command Descriptor, it shall generate and provide Response
3106 Descriptors appropriately, as indicated in field WROC for each Command Descriptor, and each Response
3107 Descriptor shall provide status information for the related transfer phase.
3108 • For PIO Mode: Response Descriptor structures shall be generated for all Command Descriptors with
3109 field WROC having a value of 1'b1, for all Direct Read or Direct GET CCCs (i.e., as with any Read-type
3110 transfer), or when the transfer phase encountered an error for any Command Descriptor (see Section 6.5).
3111 • For DMA Mode: Multiple Response Descriptor structures are generated in the Response Ring, one for
3112 each Command Descriptor, with status in each descriptor (see Section 6.6.2).

3113  The Host Controller supports an option to automatically generate a Read transfer after receiving a specified
3114  IBI event on a per-Device (per-Target) basis. If enabled, this option requires setting what value of the IBI
3115  Mandatory Byte will trigger this Auto-Command.

3121  is enabled, the Host Controller shall inspect IBI Mandatory Byte coming from the indicated Device
3122  (Target). The IBI Mandatory Data Byte is masked with the value set by the Driver.

3124  When the Host Controller receives an IBI that is accepted from the indicated Device (i.e., the Target
3125  Address in the IBI matches the DYNAMIC_ADDRESS field in the DAT entry) and whose IBI Mandatory
3126  Byte, after masking with the AUTOCMD_CMD field of the DAT entry for this Device, matches the indicated
3127  AUTOCMD_VALUE, the Host Controller shall immediately initiate a Read-type transfer to this Device (i.e.,
3128  before allowing another IBI or another Transfer/Command to proceed). The Read-type transfer shall have
3129  the parameters indicated by fields in the DAT entry: field AUTOCMD_MODE shall specify the I3C Mode, and
3130  field AUTOCMD_HDR_CODE shall specify the Command Code for HDR Modes (e.g., HDR-DDR, HDR-
3131  TSP, and HDR-TSL). The Device is expected to know the internal offset (if any) and data length for the
3132  Read data, and shall handle proper termination of the transfer.
3133  After the termination of the transfer, the Host Controller shall store the received data into the IBI Payload
3134  Buffer, and the Driver shall process the IBI only once all the Data becomes ready. The Driver shall process
3135  the request in exactly the same manner as though the data had been received via a regular IBI event (i.e., as
3136  the IBI Data Payload).

6.11.2 Configuration with DAT
3137 In order to enable the Auto-Command feature, the software shall:
3138 1. For all Devices for which Auto-Command behavior is desired, follow the DAT entry and:
3139 A. Set field IBI_PAYLOAD to 1'b1 to allow reception of IBI Mandatory Byte
3140 B. Set field AUTOCMD_MASK to the desired value
3141 C. Set field AUTOCMD_VALUE to the desired value
3142 D. Set field AUTOCMD_MODE to the desired value
3143 E. Set field AUTOCMD_HDR_CMD to the desired value
3144 Every time an IBI occurs for an Auto-Command enabled Device, the IBI’s received Mandatory Data Byte
3145 is masked with the value of AUTOCMD_MASK and the result is logically compared to the value of
3146 AUTOCMD_VALUE. If the compare result is True, then the Host Controller automatically performs a Read-
3147 type transfer to the indicated Device after the completion of the IBI, using the provided parameters and in
3148 the I3C Mode described with field AUTOCMD_MODE. The read transfer is unbounded in length, and thus
3149 ends when terminated by the Target Device, or when terminated by the Controller in case of an end-of-
3150 buffer condition (i.e., for an IBI Data Ring or an IBI FIFO).
3151 Example: Assume that AUTOCMD_MASK contains 0xF and that AUTOCMD_VALUE contains 0xC. IBIs
3152 with the following Mandatory Data Byte values will trigger the Auto-Command: 0x0C, 0x1C, …,
3153 0xFC.
3154 Note:
3155 The default values of AUTOCMD_MASK and AUTOCMD_VALUE are both 0x00, and when
3156 IBI_PAYLOAD is set to 1 in the DAT, an Auto-Command shall be triggered for all incoming IBIs from
3157 the indicated Dynamic Address. If Auto-Command is not intended, then the software must update
3158 field AUTOCMD_VALUE to a non-zero value in order to disable the Auto-Command function.
3159 The Read command in HDR Mode shall use 0x80 as the default Command Code, in case the value
3160 in AUTOCMD_HDR_CODE is lower than 0x80, or the value defined with AUTOCMD_HDR_CODE. See
3161 Table 65 of the I3C Specification [MIPI02] for details.
6.11.3 Data Reporting to IBI Payload Buffer
3162 Field AUTOCMD_DATA_RPT in register HC_CONTROL (see Section 7.4.2) determines how the data received
3163 from this Read transfer will be reported:
3164 • Coalesced Reporting: If field AUTOCMD_DATA_RPT is set to 1'b0, then data received from this Auto-
3165 Command’s Read transfer is coalesced together with the IBI Data Payload, and must be described using
3166 the same IBI Status Descriptor structure(s), per Section 8.6.2.
3167 In this case, the Read transfer data byte(s) from the Auto-Command read will immediately follow the
3168 last data byte from the IBI Data Payload. The Driver must know the length of the IBI Data Payload,
3169 which may vary per the I3C content protocol. For all IBI Status Descriptors, field STATUS_TYPE will
3170 contain the value 3'b000 (REGULAR_IBI).
3171 • Separated Reporting: If field AUTOCMD_DATA_RPT is set to 1'b1, then data received from this Auto-
3172 Command’s Read transfer is described in separate IBI Status Descriptor structure(s) that immediately
3173 follow the IBI Status Descriptor(s) and IBI Data for the IBI Data Payload, per Section 8.6.6.
3174 In this case, the initial IBI Status Descriptor(s) for the IBI Data Payload will have field
3175 STATUS_TYPE with a value of 3'b000 (REGULAR_IBI). For the subsequent IBI Status Descriptor(s) for
3176 the Auto-Command Read transfer data, field STATUS_TYPE will contain the value 3'b100
3177 (AUTOCMD_READ).
3178 Note:
3179 Field AUTOCMD_DATA_RPT is new for version 1.2 of this I3C HCI Specification, and the IBI
3180 Descriptor’s field STATUS_TYPE has been expanded to allow more status types, including the

6.12 Request Handling
3183 In general, software shall not initiate a transfer request to an I3C Target Device until and unless the Target
3184 has been assigned a Dynamic Address per Section 6.4.
3185 • The Address Assignment Command type of the Command Descriptor (see Section 8.4.1) shall be used to
3186 perform Dynamic Address Assignment using either ENTDAA or SETDASA.
3187 • A standard Transfer Command (such as an Immediate Transfer Command) shall be used to perform
3188 Dynamic Address Assignment using SETAASA.
3189 Once a Target Device has received its Dynamic Address, the software may initiate transfer requests for any
3190 supported Transfer Command types. This includes Transfer Commands that are CCCs using managed CCC
3191 transfer framing (per Section 6.3 of the I3C TCRI Specification [MIPI06]) in SDR Mode. Each Command
3192 Descriptor shall indicate the Target Device to which the Transfer Command is directed.
3193 Note:
3194 Per Section 6.3 and Section 6.4, the Driver must first populate a DAT entry containing the
3195 Dynamic Address for a Device (or an assigned Group Address, if supported) before sending any
3196 transfer requests using the index for that DAT entry.
3197 The Speed and Mode of the transfer is set via the MODE field in the Command Descriptor structure for a
3198 Transfer Command type (for more details, see Section 6.2.5 of the I3C TCRI Specification [MIPI06]).
3199 Per Section 6.2.4 of the I3C TCRI Specification [MIPI06], Software may enqueue individual transfers,
3200 where each Command Descriptor’s field TOC has a value of 1'b1; or a number of transfers in a given order,
3201 comprising a transaction sequence:
3202 • The first and subsequent Command Descriptors (except for last in the sequence) indicate the start and
3203 continuation of the sequence, with field TOC having a value of 1'b0; and
3204 • The last Command Descriptor indicates the end of the sequence, with field TOC having a value of 1'b1.
3205 Within such a sequence, field TOC roughly corresponds with the framing elements in the I3C Modes, as
3206 defined in I3C TCRI Specification Section 6.2.4.
3207 Note:
3208 Unless otherwise noted in this I3C HCI Specification, software should generally not mix Transfer
3209 Commands (as defined in the I3C TCRI Specification) with other such Command Descriptors that
3210 are not Transfer Commands, especially in the same sequence. Specifically, other such Command
3211 Descriptor(s) should not be inserted in the middle of a valid sequence of Transfer Commands with
3212 field TOC set to 1'b0, because the results would be undefined. Instead, software should ensure that
3213 the last Transfer Command has field TOC set to 1'b1, or else ensure that the Bus has otherwise
3214 reached an idle state (i.e., due to transfer abort or some other error) before enqueueing a
3215 Command Descriptor that is not a Transfer Command. However, certain Atomic transaction
3216 sequences that are defined in this I3C HCI Specification will require an Internal Control Command
3217 at the start and end of such a sequence, in order to inform the I3C Bus Controller Logic of special
3218 handling of such Transfer Commands.
3219 Whenever possible, the software should attempt to enqueue all Command Descriptors comprising a
3220 sequence of transfers as a single continuous operation or uninterrupted stream of actions, in order to
3221 prevent a command sequence stall condition or timeout (as defined in the I3C TCRI Specification at
3222 Section 6.4.2 [MIPI06]). If the Command Queue (for PIO Mode) or the active Command Ring (for DMA
3223 Mode) is unable to contain or accept all such Command Descriptors for this sequence, or if the sequence is
3224 longer than the maximum size of the Command Queue/Ring, then software must first enqueue some
3225 Command Descriptors to start processing the sequence, and then actively monitor the status of the
3226 Command Queue/Ring to ensure that it is able to enqueue additional Command Descriptors when possible,
3227 while preventing a command sequence stall condition or timeout.
3228 For more detail, refer to Section 6.4.2 of the I3C TCRI Specification [MIPI06].
114 Copyright © 2018–2023 MIPI Alliance, Inc.

Version 1.2 Specification for I3C HCI
15-Feb-2023
3229 The Host Controller shall monitor the active Command Queue/Ring and attempt to detect situations of
3230 possible command sequence stall conditions or timeouts, reporting them as warnings or errors per
3231 Section 6.13.2. The Host Controller shall also monitor the specific execution status of the operating mode,
3232 for other mode-specific conditions that might cause an interruption of transfer processing.
3233 Whenever possible, the Host Controller and its I3C Bus Controller Logic should attempt to mitigate or
3234 prevent such underflow situations that might become imminent as the Command Queue drains to approach
3235 an empty state, using the following methods as examples:
3236 • Stalling the I3C Bus, using any methods that might be defined and enabled for the I3C Mode;
3237 • Using any available I3C-Mode-specific methods to defer a transaction, or any upcoming actions that
3238 might be expected in the near future; or
3239 • Reducing the clock speed at which transfers are driven on the Bus.
3240 In other cases, the Host Controller and its I3C Bus Controller Logic would not be able to prevent an
3241 underflow situation or other interruption of transfer processing, and would be required to cancel the
3242 sequence. In this case, the I3C Bus Controller Logic would be required to end the framing using either a
3243 STOP condition or HDR Exit Pattern, as appropriate for the I3C Mode. As a result, the I3C Bus Controller
3244 Logic would act as though the last executed Command Descriptor had been provided the value 1'b1 in field
3245 TOC (instead of its actual value of 1'b0).
3246 If the Host Controller is instructed to cancel a transaction sequence for any reason (including a command
3247 sequence timeout) then it shall assert an interrupt via field HC_SEQ_CANCEL_STAT in register INTR_STATUS
3248 (see Section 7.4.7) to inform the Host that the sequence was terminated before receiving a Command
3249 Descriptor having field TOC=1. The specific warning and error conditions relating to a command sequence
3250 stall condition or timeout shall also be reported as interrupts, as defined in Section 6.13.2.
3251 Note:
3252 Since some I3C content protocols might not tolerate a forced STOP condition between two
3253 transfers that would otherwise need to be executed in a continuous sequence (i.e., with a Repeated
3254 START or HDR Restart Pattern), the Driver shall determine whether enqueueing the next
3255 Command Descriptor after a cancelled sequence due to a timeout is a correct course of action, or
3256 whether the command sequence must be restarted from an earlier transfer. The Driver shall
3257 determine whether to resume transfers after the STOP condition, or to restart from a prior Transfer
3258 Command, by enqueueing new Transfer Commands appropriately for the I3C content protocol after
3259 detecting the forced STOP condition. Alternatively, the Driver may configure automatic halting if a
3260 command sequence timeout occurs, by writing to field HALT_ON_CMD_SEQ_TIMEOUT in register
3261 HC_CONTROL (see Section 6.13.2 and Section 7.4.2).
3262 Refer to Section 6.7 and Section 8.4 for usage of Transfer Commands.
3263 A Host Controller may support alternate methods for handling a transition between two Transfer
3264 Commands with different Speeds (i.e., different transfer rates) or different I3C Modes (see Section 6.2.5 of
3265 the I3C TCRI Specification [MIPI06]), or for optimizing the handling of Transfer Commands in HDR
3266 Modes with field TOC set to 1'b1. If such optional alternate methods are supported, then they shall be
3267 disabled by default, and shall be explicitly enabled by software via register control. Such a register should
3268 be part of an Extended Capability structure, that might be enabled or disabled by software, having a default
3269 configuration setting to use the standard behavior.
3270 If the Host Controller processes either a Host Controller Abort operation (see Section 6.8.4) or a Ring
3271 Abort Operation (see Section 6.6.6) at the request of the Driver, then it shall attempt to either complete or
3272 abort any in-progress transfers that the I3C Bus Controller Logic is currently driving, and if possible it shall
3273 abort such transfers at the earliest opportunity, even if the associated Command Descriptor(s) have field
3274 TOC set to 1'b0 (i.e., are not the intended end of a sequence).

6.12.1 PIO Mode
3275 In PIO Mode, the Driver prepares the Command Descriptor structure with the Request, and optionally the
3276 associated data buffer (see Section 6.8.1). The Data is sent to the Tx Data Port register 32 bits (one
3277 DWORD) at a time (see the PIO section of the Register Map, Section 7.4.21). The Data is transmitted on
3278 the I3C Bus for each DWORD entry in the Tx Data Queue, using the current byte ordering mode (per
3279 Section 6.8.3). Each Data byte is transmitted on the I3C Bus according to the I3C Mode signaling. The
3280 Driver shall provide data payload and write the Command Descriptor to the Command Queue Port, starting
3281 with the first DWORD entry.
3282 The order in which the data and the Command Descriptor are provided may be arbitrary (i.e., Command
3283 Descriptor first, or Command Descriptor last). Once the last DWORD of the Command Descriptor is put
3284 into the Command Queue, the Host Controller shall start processing the Transfer Command. In PIO Mode,
3285 the data can be sent either as an Immediate transfer payload (i.e., in a Command Descriptor structure), or
3286 else through the Transfer Data Port.
3287 Per Section 6.5, once the transaction has taken place on the Bus, the Host Controller shall conditionally
3288 populate the Response Queue with a Response Descriptor (see Section 8.5) describing the status of this
3289 transaction. For Read-Type transfer requests, the data for the transaction is available through the Transfer
3290 Data Port. Each Data byte is populated from the Bus based on the I3C Mode signaling. The software shall
3291 populate the data into the Rx Data Queue as one or more DWORD entries, using the current byte ordering
3292 mode (per Section 6.8.3). If the received data length is not DWORD-aligned, then the next Bus transaction
3293 shall be populated starting on a DWORD boundary.
3294 If any error is detected, then the PIO processing shall be halted and the Response Descriptor shall indicate
3295 the particular error. After reporting the error, status shall be cleared (PIO_INTR_STATUS) and written to the
3296 Command Queue Port (COMMAND_QUEUE_PORT).
3297 If the software is still enqueueing Command Descriptors that are part of a sequence of transfers (as defined
3298 in Section 6.12) but has not yet enqueued the last such Command Descriptor for the end of this sequence
3299 (i.e., where field TOC would have a value of 1'b1) for any reason, this might cause a command sequence
3300 stall condition or timeout, if the Host Controller is able to process all previously enqueued Command
3301 Descriptors before the software is able to enqueue a subsequent Command Descriptor into the Command
3302 Queue Port. Such a stall condition shall initially be indicated as a warning, per the I3C Mode. This stall
3303 condition would be mitigated if the Host Controller were to receive a subsequent Command Descriptor in
3304 time, i.e., if software were able to enqueue a subsequent Command Descriptor via the Command Queue
3305 Port (see Section 6.8.1) before the stall becomes a timeout. However, if the Host Controller were forced to
3306 cancel the transaction sequence due to a timeout caused by an empty Command Queue, then it must report
3307 this timeout error as an interrupt, as defined in Section 6.13.2; and it must also indicate the cancellation of
3308 the transaction sequence, via field HC_SEQ_CANCEL_STAT of register INTR_STATUS (see Section 7.4.7).
3309 Note:
3310 If the Host Controller is required to cancel a transaction sequence due to other PIO error conditions
3311 such as the Tx Data Queue draining to empty during a Write-Type transfer, or the Rx Data Queue
3312 becoming completely full during a Read-Type transfer, and this causes the transfer to be aborted by
3313 the I3C Bus Controller Logic, then this shall also be reported as a cancelled transaction sequence,
3314 in addition to an aborted transfer (i.e., field TRANSFER_ABORT_STAT in register PIO_INTR_STATUS;
3315 see Section 7.5.9).
3316 For each Command Descriptor in a sequence, if field TOC has a value of 1'b1, then the Bus transaction shall
3317 end with a STOP condition, in order to allow subsequent IBI reception. If field TOC has a value of 1'b0,
3318 then the Bus transaction shall end with a Repeated START condition, and the next Command shall be
3319 processed.

6.12.2 DMA Mode
3320 In DMA Mode, the Driver prepares pointers to one or more contiguous buffers of physical memory,
3321 depending on whether Scatter-Gather capability is supported (per Section 6.2.1). The Command Descriptor
3322 structure is contained in a Transfer Descriptor structure at a given index on the Command Ring. The
3323 Transfer Descriptor also indicates whether to store the data in a single contiguous block of physical
3324 memory, or in a list of memory blocks (i.e., an array of Memory Descriptor structures) using Scatter-Gather
3325 capability (if supported). The flow for preparing a Transfer Descriptor is defined in Section 6.8.2, and the
3326 data structure formats are defined in Section 8.3.
3327 Once software has written the Transfer Descriptor’s pointer into the Command Ring and has updated the
3328 Enqueue Pointer, the Transfer Descriptor is ready to be processed. Software may enqueue one or more
3329 Transfer Descriptors with a single update of the Enqueue pointer.
3330 The I3C Bus Controller Logic shall use the current byte ordering mode (per Section 6.8.3) for all Transfer
3331 Commands. For Write-Type transfers, the Memory Access Interface shall read the indicated DWORDs
3332 automatically from Host system memory and apply the current byte ordering mode to each DWORD, to
3333 ensure that the Data bytes enter the Tx Data Buffer in the correct order. Similarly, for Read-Type transfers,
3334 the Memory Access Interface shall consume bytes from the Rx Data Buffer and collect these the Data bytes
3335 into DWORDs accordingly, to ensure that every DWORD written to Host system memory uses the current
3336 byte ordering mode.
3337 The byte ordering shall apply to Transfer Commands that use a single physical memory buffer, as well as
3338 Transfer Commands that use Scatter-Gather (i.e., to each single buffer described by a Buffer List Pointer
3339 list entry; see Section 8.3.1).
3340 The Memory Access Interface logic shall drive all Host system memory access for Transfer Commands
3341 using the DMA engines (i.e., Memory Access Engines, as shown in Figure 3), using the Base Address
3342 pointers that are provided by the Host for each Ring, as well as the buffer pointer for each Transfer
3343 Descriptor. The Ring Controller shall monitor the fill levels of the Tx Data Buffer and Rx Data Buffer, and
3344 also monitor the operation of the Memory Access Interface for all outstanding memory requests. The Ring
3345 Controller shall detect situations where the Host system bus is unable to respond to memory requests with
3346 sufficient performance to maintain correct operation of the I3C Bus Controller Logic during a transfer, and
3347 where the I3C Bus Controller Logic might be required to terminate a transfer.
3348 For each transaction, the index into the Command Ring and Response Ring shall be the same. That is, at the
3349 same Ring index for both the Command Ring and the Response Ring, the Host Controller shall
3350 conditionally generate a Response Descriptor for each Transfer Descriptor that is processed and executed,
3351 and the Response Descriptor at that index shall indicate the status of processing that transaction, per
3352 Section 6.6.2. Response Descriptors shall be generated as transactions are processed, according to the Ring
3353 Controller’s arbitration logic, which might service individual Ring Bundles in any desired order or priority.
3354 Additionally, the Ring Bundle must be enabled and running, and not in a halted or aborted state.
3355 If the software is still enqueueing Transfer Descriptors that are part of a sequence of transfers (as defined in
3356 Section 6.12) but has not yet enqueued the last such Transfer Descriptor for the end of this sequence (i.e.,
3357 where the Command Descriptor’s field TOC would have a value of 1'b1) for any reason, then this might
3358 cause a command sequence stall condition or timeout if the Host Controller is able to process all previously
3359 enqueued Transfer Descriptors in this Ring Bundle before the software is able to enqueue a subsequent
3360 Transfer Descriptor into the Command Ring of this same Ring Bundle. Such a condition shall initially be
3361 indicated as a warning, per the I3C Mode. This situation would be mitigated if the Host Controller receives
3362 a “doorbell” notification that one or more subsequent Transfer Descriptors were written into Command
3363 Ring (see Section 6.8.2) before the stall becomes a timeout. However, if the Host Controller must cancel
3364 the transaction sequence due to an “empty” Command Ring (i.e., when the Enqueue Pointer and Dequeue
3365 Pointer are equal), then it would have to report this timeout error as an interrupt, as defined in
3366 Section 6.13.2; and it would also indicate the cancellation of the transaction sequence, via field
3367 HC_SEQ_CANCEL_STAT of register INTR_STATUS (see Section 7.4.7).

6.13 Error Handling
3368 The general approach to error handling in I3C HCI is as follows:
3369 • Any detectable error on a transaction will result in an error code in the Response Descriptor structure.
3370 Reception of the Response triggers an interrupt to Host Controller Driver.
3371 In addition, the Host Controller shall halt processing to allow the Driver to handle the error.
3372 • The specific error code will be returned in field ERR_STATUS of the Response Director, as defined in
3373 Section 8.5. Section 6.4 of the I3C TCRI Specification [MIPI06] contains additional details on the
3374 defined error codes in field ERR_STATUS.
3375 • In PIO Mode, the Command/Response Queue shall halt its operation (indicated via the RESUME field in
3376 register HC_CONTROL, Section 7.4.2). The Driver shall take any necessary measures to recover from
3377 this situation, and then resume normal operation of the queues.
3378 • In DMA Mode, the Ring Bundle that processed the failed request shall halt its operation (indicated via
3379 the RS field in register RH_CONTROL, Section 7.6.10.9). The Driver shall take any necessary measures
3380 to recover from this situation, and then resume normal operation of that Ring Bundle.
3381 In some error situations, the Host Controller might halt operations of all enabled Ring Bundles,
3382 indicated via the RESUME field in register HC_CONTROL. The Driver shall take any necessary
3383 measures to recover from this situation, and then resume normal operations of applicable Ring
3384 Bundles.
3385 • For Write requests, the Driver should issue a Transfer Command with the GETSTATUS Direct CCC to
3386 determine the Device’s overall error status.
3387 • IBIs (Target-initiated interrupts) are natively supported via the IBI Ring and triggering interrupt (i.e., the
3388 same as for the Response Descriptor). Any errors in IBI reception are flagged in the IBI Status Descriptor
3389 structure.
3390 The Host Controller shall not autonomously issue the GETSTATUS Direct CCC, nor any other command to
3391 determine Device state/health. The Driver shall issue GETSTATUS Direct CCC when required, and shall
3392 subsequently take appropriate measures to recover the Bus or the Host Controller.
3393 If the Host Controller exposes Debug-specific registers via the Debug Specific Extended Capability
3394 structure (see Section 7.7.7), the Host Controller may optionally provide a counter for CE2 errors via field
3395 CE2_ERROR_COUNT in register MX_ERROR_COUNTERS (Section 7.7.7.4). Such error counters may
3396 optionally be used by software to indicate the type of the errors occurring on the Bus. Any such registers
3397 shall zero their values upon being read; as a result, any cumulative counter must be implemented in
3398 software.
3399 Upon any non-recoverable internal error, the Host Controller shall stop, interrupt the software, and indicate
3400 an internal error via field HC_INTERNAL_ERR_STAT in register INTR_STATUS (Section 7.4.7).

6.13.1 Error Status Codes in Response Descriptor
3401 General error codes for Response Desciptors are defined in Section 6.4.1 of the I3C TCRI Specification
3402 [MIPI06]. This I3C HCI Specification defines the specific conditions under which reporting of some of
3403 those error codes is required. Some of these conditions depend upon the HCI operating mode or condition.
3404 As a result, the following sub-sections should be read in conjunction with the I3C TCRI Specification’s
3405 error code definitions.
6.13.1.1 Address Header Error
3406 For field ERR_STATUS having a value of 0x4 (ADDR_HEADER):
3407 • In SDR Mode:
3408 If no Target Devices acknowledge the Broadcast Address before the start of a private Transfer
3409 Command that was driven automatically by the I3C Bus Controller Logic:
3410 • Because field IBA_INCLUDE in register HC_CONTROL (Section 7.4.2) was set to 1'b1,
3411 • Or because software had previously used an Internal Control Command to enable automatic
3412 transmission of the I3C Broadcast Header on the Bus (per Section 8.4.2 and Table 137),
3413 then this is an Address Header error.
3414 For additional details, see the I3C TCRI Specification at Section 6.4.1.4 [MIPI06].
6.13.1.2 Overflow/Underflow Error
3415 For field ERR_STATUS having a value of 0x6 (OVL):
3416 • In PIO Mode:
3417 If the Host Controller’s Tx Data Buffer experiences an underflow condition for any Write-Type
3418 transfer, then this is an Underflow error (see Section 6.8.1).
3419 If the Host Controller’s Rx Data Buffer experiences an overflow condition for any Read-Type
3420 transfer, then this is an Overflow error.
3421 Note:
3422 This scenario does not apply to DMA Mode, since the Host would allocate memory for the
3423 Tx/Rx Data Buffer; therefore, the Host does not use PIO registers to fill the Tx Data Queue or
3424 consume from the Rx Data Queue during a transfer.
3425 • While processing a sequence of Command Descriptors for an Atomic transaction for a Target
3426 Reset Action:
3427 The Host Controller shall report this error code for the special Internal Control Command that
3428 indicates the end of the sequence, if the Atomic transaction was only partially successful.
3429 “Only partially successful” means that the Command Queue/Ring had an underflow condition before
3430 the end of the sequence (i.e., that software could not enqueue all such Command Descriptors in a
3431 timely manner, to maintain continuous framing and avoid a timeout), and that some of the Transfer
3432 Commands in the sequence were successfully processed and driven on the I3C Bus.
3433 In this scenario, the Host Controller would have determined that it could safely allow the partial
3434 sequence of Transfer Commands to be followed by the Target Reset Pattern, instead of allowing the
3435 stall to become a timeout, as defined in Section 6.15.1.2.
3436 If the Command Queue/Ring underflow condition occurs and individual Transfer Commands in the
3437 sequence were rejected (i.e., were not driven on the I3C Bus due to underflow), then the Response
3438 Descriptors for each such rejected Transfer Command shall report error code 0x8 (HC_ABORTED).

6.13.1.3 Host Controller Aborted
3439 For field ERR_STATUS having a value of 0x8 (HC_ABORTED):
3440 • In PIO Mode:
3441 The Host Controller shall report this error code for a transaction that was aborted due to the Host
3442 Controller Abort operation per Section 6.8.4.
3443 • In DMA Mode:
3444 The Host Controller shall report this error code for a transaction that was aborted due to either the
3445 Host Controller Abort operation per Section 6.8.4, or a Ring Abort operation per Section 6.6.6.
6.13.1.4 Bus Aborted
3446 For field ERR_STATUS having a value of 0x9 (BUS_ABORTED), the Host Controller shall report this error
3447 code if an I3C transaction was aborted due to Early Termination (i.e., by another I3C Device). This can
3448 occur when a Monitoring Device on the I3C Bus aborts a transfer, or when the intended Target uses an
3449 Early Termination Pattern to end a Write-Type transfer. For more details, see Section 6.8.6.
6.13.1.5 Aborted with CRC
3450 The Host Controller does not support field ERR_STATUS having a value of 0xB (ABORTED_WITH_CRC)
3451 because HDR-BT Mode transfers are not currently supported.
6.13.1.6 Transfer Type Specific
3452 For field ERR_STATUS having a value of 0xC–0xF (Transfer Type Specific):
3453 These error codes are used for special variants of Transfer Commands, or in other operating modes.
3454 • While processing a Combo Transfer Command:
3455 For details that apply to Combo Transfer Commands, see the I3C TCRI Specification at
3456 Section 6.4.1.2 [MIPI06].
3457 • While processing a sequence of Command Descriptors for an Atomic transaction for a Target
3458 Reset Action:
3459 The Host Controller shall report error code 0xC or error code 0xD for the special Internal Control
3460 Command that indicates the end of the sequence:
3461 • If the Atomic Target Reset transaction failed due to early cancellation by software, or
3462 • If the Command Queue/Ring had an underflow condition before the end of the sequence (i.e., if
3463 software could not enqueue all such Command Descriptors in a timely manner, to maintain continuous
3464 framing and avoid a timeout), as defined in Section 6.15.1.2.
3465 In both cases, the Target Reset Action would not be performed as requested.
3466 If the Command Queue/Ring underflow condition occurs, then any individual Transfer Commands
3467 that were rejected (i.e., that were not driven on the I3C Bus due to underflow) shall report error code
3468 0x8 (HC_ABORTED). For other transfer errors, the usual error codes shall apply to each individual
3469 Transfer Command within the sequence.
3470 For other general guidance on Atomic transaction sequences, see the I3C TCRI Specification at
3471 Section 6.4.1.2 [MIPI06].
3472 • While attempting to pass the Controller Role to a Secondary Controller Device:
3473 The Host Controller shall report error code 0xC or error code 0xD, depending on which error
3474 condition the I3C Bus Controller Logic encountered while attempting to pass the Controller Role
3475 with the GETACCCR CCC. For additional details, see Section 6.17.2. Note that a NACK error with
3476 the GETACCCR CCC is reported via error code 0x5 (NACK).

6.13.2 Errors Due to Command Sequence Stall or Timeout
3477 In some situations, the Host Controller might fully drain the Command Queue (in PIO Mode) or active
3478 Command Ring (in DMA Mode) while processing a command sequence where one or more Command
3479 Descriptors were enqueued and the last Command Descriptor was a Transfer Command with field TOC set
3480 to 1'b0. As the I3C Bus Controller Logic started processing these enqueued Transfer Commands, the Host
3481 might not enqueue another suitable Command Descriptor with field TOC set to 1'b1 in a timely manner, and
3482 as a result the I3C Bus Controller Logic would be forced to terminate the sequence.
3483 • In SDR Mode, the I3C Bus Controller Logic might stall the Bus at certain points in SDR framing,
3484 according to the maximum allowed stall times defined for SCL Low (see the I3C Specification [MIPI02]
3485 at Section 5.1.2.5).
3486 • In HDR Modes, the I3C Bus Controller Logic might use a stall method that is specific to that HDR
3487 Mode, if supported and previously enabled for use.
3488 • If the stall method was not previously enabled or no stall method is supported, then the I3C Controller
3489 must terminate the transaction with the HDR Exit Pattern.
3490 Section 6.4.2 of the I3C TCRI Specification [MIPI06] defines handling requirements for Command
3491 Sequence Stall and Timeout.
3492 In addition, this I3C HCI Specification defines the following Host Controller requirements:
3493 • When a Stall is Detected: If the I3C Bus Controller Logic detects such a condition that it has
3494 temporarily mitigated by stalling the clock, then the Host Controller shall report this as a warning event,
3495 via field HC_WARN_CMD_SEQ_STALL_STAT in register INTR_STATUS (see Section 7.4.7).
3496 If the condition is not resolved, and the stall turns into a timeout, then the Host Controller shall
3497 report this as a possible error, via field HC_ERR_CMD_SEQ_TIMEOUT_STAT in register INTR_STATUS
3498 (see Section 7.4.7). Software may configure the Host Controller to also assert an interrupt via field
3499 HC_SEQ_CANCEL_STAT in register INTR_STATUS (see Section 7.4.7) to inform the Host that the
3500 command sequence was terminated before receiving a Command Descriptor having field TOC = 1.
3501 • After a Timeout: Software may subsequently resume sending valid Command Descriptors after the
3502 timeout, and the Host Controller shall attempt to restart a new transaction in the indicated I3C Mode,
3503 starting with the next Transfer Command in the sequence, unless any of the following conditions are true:
3504 • The Response Descriptor for the previous transfer (i.e., the last one processed before the stall turned
3505 into a timeout) indicated a transfer error in field ERR_STATUS;
3506 • The Host Controller was processing Transfer Commands in an Atomic Target Reset transaction that
3507 had a timeout per Section 6.15.1.2, and would reject any subsequent Transfer Commands after a
3508 timeout, until software sends a special Internal Control Command to end this transaction mode;
3509 • Field HALT_CMD_SEQ_TIMEOUT in register HC_CONTROL (see Section 7.4.2) was set to 1'b1; or
3510 • Any other transfer error, operating mode-specific error or Host Controller interrupt was asserted.

3511 Field HALT_ON_CMD_SEQ_TIMEOUT in register HC_CONTROL shall determine whether the Host Controller
3512 must halt processing of further Command Descriptors in the active Command Queue/Ring, when the I3C
3513 Bus Controller Logic encounters a command sequence timeout condition that it cannot avoid or mitigate.
3514 • If this field is set to 1'b1, then the Host Controller must halt processing and wait for software to resolve
3515 the condition using an error recovery procedure. Software may set this field to 1'b1 if it knows that it is
3516 sending sequences of Command Descriptors that must be run in sequence using continuous framing in
3517 order to be successful, i.e., for a particular I3C content protocol that does not tolerate a disruption (i.e.,
3518 forced end of the framing) if certain successive transfers are to be successful.
3519 For example, in cases where an unresolved stall becomes a timeout that causes a STOP condition or
3520 HDR Exit Pattern, this would disrupt the operation of the addressed Target(s), or have other side
3521 effects on the operation of addressed Target(s) that require subsequent commands to be continuously
3522 executed with any preceding commands. As instructed by field HALT_ON_CMD_SEQ_TIMEOUT, the
3523 Host Controller must not execute any subsequent commands after the forced STOP condition or
3524 HDR Exit Pattern.
3525 • If this field is set to 1'b0, the Host Controller may generally resume processing without waiting for
3526 software to resolve the condition. Software may set this field to 1'b0 if it is sending standard Transfer
3527 Commands that may be executed separately or together, with the use of continuous framing as a
3528 performance optimization.
3529 In this case, an unresolved stall that becomes a timeout shall still be reported as an error, but the Host
3530 Controller shall resume operation upon receiving the next enqueued Command Descriptor, unless the
3531 Host Controller was processing a special sequence of Transfer Commands that did not allow
3532 automatic resume of operations, such as an Atomic Target Reset transaction.
3533 Note:
3534 The Atomic Target Reset transaction using the RSTACT CCC and Target Reset Pattern (as defined
3535 in Section 6.15.1.2) is a special exception with pre-defined behavior that always applies,
3536 regardless of the current setting of field HALT_ON_CMD_SEQ_TIMEOUT.

3544 Within each such Register Set, the corresponding bit fields for the four registers shall control the status and
3545 signaling of each interrupt condition. The bit fields in each of the four registers shall interact and provide
3546 fine-grained control over the reporting of interrupts to the Host system.
3547 • The Interrupt Status Enable Mask bit field controls whether either of the following events might be
3548 logged in the Interrupt Status Register bit field:
3549 • The interrupt condition in logic, caused by the underlying event or assertion; or
3550 • Software writing a 1 to the Force Interrupt bit field (i.e., in the Interrupt Force register).
3551 • If the bit field in the Interrupt Status Register has a value of 1, then it may be cleared either by taking
3552 some other action from software (i.e., by writing 1 to clear the same bit field), or by consuming the
3553 results of the specific Queue or FIFO that caused the underlying interrupt condition to trigger.
3554 • The Interrupt Signal Enable Mask bit field controls whether the Interrupt Status Register bit field
3555 transitioning from 0 to 1 would cause the Host Controller to assert an interrupt to the Host.
3556 In order to receive interrupt assertions for desired interrupt conditions, software must enable the bit fields in
3557 both the Interrupt Status Enable Mask and the Interrupt Signal Enable Mask. Alternatively, software might
3558 only enable bit fields in the Interrupt Status Enable Mask, and use polling of the Interrupt Status Register to
3559 test for an interrupt condition (i.e., without using an interrupt service routine).

6.15 Target Reset and Bus Recovery
3570 The Host Controller shall support several methods of sending a Target Reset Pattern, or recovering the I3C
3571 Bus from various conditions.
3572 Note:
3573 The reset and recovery methods described in this section are required in order to comply with
3574 version 1.1.1+ of the I3C Specification [MIPI05]. These methods rely on new sub-commands for
3575 the Internal Control Command (see Section 8.4.2). Implementers are required to support these
3576 sub-commands as well as the flows defined in sub-sections of this section.
6.15.1 Target Reset Pattern
3577 I3C version 1.1.1 supports several flows for the Target Reset mechanism (see the I3C Specification
3578 [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.11). The Host Controller shall support these flows using Command Descriptors of
3579 type Internal Control Command (see Section 8.4.2) with value 0x4 in the MIPI_CMD field (see Table 135
3580 and Table 139). In this section and its subsections, such a Command Descriptor is referred to as a Target
3581 Reset Command Descriptor.
6.15.1.1 Reset I3C Peripheral or Reset Whole Chip
3582 Software may choose to send the target Reset Pattern at any appropriate time by enqueuing a Target Reset
3583 Command Descriptor with a value of 0x0 in field RESET_OP_TYPE (i.e., Bits[13:12], see Table 139).
3584 Software may issue a single Target Reset Pattern to initiate the Reset I3C Peripheral action, by sending one
3585 such Command Descriptor. Software may also issue two Target Reset Patterns to initiate the Reset Whole
3586 Chip action, by sending two such Command Descriptors in succession (i.e., without any intervening
3587 CCCs).
3588 The Host Controller shall schedule the Target Reset Pattern to be sent once the Command Descriptor is
3589 processed, and once the I3C Bus is not active (i.e., a Bus Free Condition). The I3C Bus Controller Logic
3590 shall drive a START condition and set up the Bus properly, then drive the Target Reset Pattern, followed by
3591 a Repeated START and then a STOP.
6.15.1.2 Configure Target for Target Reset Action
3592 Software may choose to configure one or more Target Devices to take any valid Target Reset actions, using
3593 the Broadcast or Direct SET forms of the RSTACT CCC (see the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at
3594 Section 5.1.11.2 and Section 5.1.9.3.26). Software shall send a sequence of Command Descriptors to the
3595 Host Controller as an Atomic Target Reset transaction:
3596 • Software shall first prepare the Host Controller to start the Atomic Target Reset transaction, by enqueuing
3597 a Target Reset Command Descriptor with field RESET_OP_TYPE (i.e., Bits[13:12]) set to a value of 0x2
3598 (see Table 139).
3599 • This operation instructs the Host Controller to enter a Critical Section, such that it must perform
3600 special handling of subsequent Command Descriptors, until this is ended by a subsequent operation.
3601 • Software shall then send one or more subsequent Command Descriptors in SDR Mode, with continuous
3602 framing. Each Command Descriptor shall be a Transfer Command:
3603 • A Broadcast CCC, addressed to the I3C Bus, to configure all Target Devices; or
3604 • A Direct SET CCC, addressed to a specific Target Device, for the Target Reset action that will be
3605 configured with the RSTACT CCC.

3606 • The last of these Command Descriptors shall contain the value 1'b1 in the TOC field, to indicate the end
3607 of the Atomic transaction.
3608 • To prepare a single Target Reset action, software shall send one such Command Descriptor with value
3609 1'b1 in the TOC field. The Host Controller shall conditionally drive the Target Reset Pattern at the end
3610 of the frame.
3611 • To prepare multiple Target Reset actions, software shall send multiple consecutive Command
3612 Descriptors in a sequence. Each Command Descriptor in the sequence except the last one shall contain
3613 the value 1'b0 in the TOC field, and the last one shall contain 1'b1 in the TOC field. The Host Controller
3614 shall use Direct CCC Framing (see Section 6.10) as indicated by the field values of the Command
3615 Descriptors, and shall conditionally drive the Target Reset Pattern at the end of the frame (i.e., at the
3616 end of the last such Command Descriptor, when TOC=1).
3617 • After sending all such Command Descriptors for the RSTACT CCC, software shall enqueue a Target
3618 Reset Command Descriptor with field RESET_OP_TYPE (i.e., Bits[13:12]) set to a value of 0x3 (see Table
3619 139).
3620 • This operation instructs the Host Controller to leave the Critical Section and resume normal handling
3621 of subsequent Command Descriptors.
3622 While the Host Controller is processing the Atomic transaction in the Critical Section, all other operations
3623 shall be suspended. If the Host Controller is operating in DMA Mode, then any other active Ring Bundles
3624 shall be temporarily suspended once the Host Controller starts processing the initial Target Reset Command
3625 Descriptor, and then resumed once the entire transaction is finished (i.e., after the final Target Reset
3626 Command Descriptor is received).
3627 The Host Controller shall observe the following requirements while operating in the Critical Section:
3628 • All Transfer Commands shall be in SDR Mode, at any supported data rate per Section 7.1.1.1 of the I3C
3629 TCRI Specification [MIPI06].
3630 • The Host Controller shall reject any Transfer Commands in any HDR Modes.
3631 • The Host Controller shall reject any other Internal Control Commands other than the Target Reset
3632 Command Descriptor to leave the Critical Section.
3633 • If the Host Controller receives the Target Reset Command Descriptor to leave the Critical Section, and it
3634 has not yet received a valid Transfer Command for a RSTACT CCC with TOC=0, then:
3635 • If this is intentional from software (i.e., is not due to a stall that turns into a timeout) then the Host
3636 Controller shall cancel the Critical Section, and the I3C Bus Controller Logic shall not drive the Target
3637 Reset Pattern.
3638 • The Host Controller shall resume processing any subsequent Command Descriptors as normal, and
3639 then generate a Response Descriptor with error code 0xD (Transfer Type Specific: SEQ_CANCELLED) in
3640 field ERR_STATUS to signal that the Target Reset was cancelled by software request.
3641 • The Transfer Commands allowed in the Critical Section shall be a sequence comprised of Broadcast
3642 CCCs and/or Direct SET CCCs, for the RSTACT CCC.
3643 • For certain sequences that begin with a single Broadcast RSTACT CCC (with Defining Byte of 0x0)
3644 followed by one or more Direct SET RSTACT CCCs (with non-zero Defining Byte values), a ‘partial
3645 success’ sequence is a truncated portion of the sequence, starting with the first (i.e., Broadcast with
3646 Defining Byte 0x00) followed by one or more of the subsequent Direct SET RSTACT CCCs.
3647 • The Host Controller shall inspect each Transfer Command received, after entering the Critical Section:
3648 • If a Broadcast CCC is received as the first Transfer Command, then:
3649 • If the Defining Byte is zero, then the Host Controller shall set a flag that indicates it may allow a
3650 “partial success”.
3651 • If the Defining Byte is not zero, then the Host Controller shall not allow a “partial success”.
3652 • If no Broadcast CCC is received, then the Host Controller shall not allow a “partial success”.
3653 • If a subsequent Broadcast CCC is received with a non-zero Defining Byte, and the “partial success”
3654 flag was set earlier, then the “partial success” flag is cleared and shall not be set again during this
3655 Critical Section.

3656 • If any Transfer Command fails during the sequence, then:
3657 • For failures due to a Target Device not acknowledging its Dynamic Address (i.e., ERR_STATUS having
3658 a value of 0x5 for NACK), the Host Controller shall stop processing subsequent Command Descriptors,
3659 per normal processing, after attempting an appropriate number of retries. For Direct CCCs, the retry
3660 model is specified in Section 6.10.
3661 • For failure due to any other reason, the Host Controller shall stop processing subsequent Command
3662 Descriptors, per normal Transfer Command processing. The I3C Bus Controller Logic shall drive a
3663 STOP condition, and the Target Reset Action shall be cancelled.
3664 • The Host Controller shall not drive the Target Reset Pattern, and shall leave the Critical Section due to
3665 the error.
3666 • Software should subsequently run an error recovery procedure.
3667 • If the Host Controller processes all Command Descriptors that were enqueued into the Command
3668 Queue/Ring, and the Host does not enqueue additional Command Descriptors in time to prevent a stall
3669 from turning into a timeout, then:
3670 • If the “partial success” flag was set earlier, then the last processed Command Descriptor had field
3671 TOC=0, and the Host Controller was able to drive the initial Broadcast CCC followed by at least one
3672 subsequent Direct CCC (with TOC=0) in continuous framing, then the Host Controller shall assume it
3673 could achieve success with a partially successful transaction.
3674 • For such a condition: before allowing the stall to turn into a timeout, the I3C Bus Controller Logic
3675 shall drive the target Reset Pattern after the last successful Direct SET CCC Segment (i.e., the one
3676 with the last processed Command Descriptor with TOC=0) followed by a Repeated START and then
3677 a STOP.
3678 • The Host Controller shall report the warning via field HC_WARN_CMD_SEQ_STALL_STAT of register
3679 INTR_STATUS (Section 7.4.7) to inform the Host that the I3C Bus Controller Logic was forced to
3680 stall the clock (per Section 6.13.2) but prevented the command sequence stall condition from
3681 becoming a timeout by driving the Target Reset Pattern before the end of the sequence.
3682 • The Host Controller shall set a flag indicating that all subsequent Command Descriptors in the
3683 sequence would be rejected, until it receives the final Target Reset Command Descriptor with field
3684 RESET_OP_TYPE set to the value 0x3.
3685 • Any Command Descriptor that is rejected (i.e., one that arrived after the I3C Bus Controller Logic
3686 was forced to drive the Target Reset Pattern instead of allowing a stall to turn into a timeout) shall
3687 cause a Response Descriptor to be generated, with error code 0x8 (HC_ABORTED) in field
3688 ERR_STATUS.
3689 • When the Host Controller receives the final Target Reset Command Descriptor to leave the Critical
3690 Section, it shall resume processing any subsequent Command Descriptors as normal, and then
3691 generate a Response Descriptor with error code 0xC (Transfer Type Specific: CMD_UNDERFLOW) in
3692 field ERR_STATUS to signal underflow of the Command Queue/Ring with partial success.

3693 • If the “partial success” flag was not set earlier, then the Host Controller shall not drive the Target
3694 Reset Pattern, and shall allow the stall to turn into a timeout.
3695 • The I3C Bus Controller Logic shall drive a STOP condition.
3696 • The Host Controller shall assert an interrupt via the HC_SEQ_CANCEL_STAT field of register
3697 INTR_STATUS (Section 7.4.7) to inform the Host that the RSTACT CCC and Target Reset command
3698 sequence was cancelled (i.e., as a specific example of a transaction sequence).
3699 • The Host Controller shall report the error via field HC_ERR_CMD_SEQ_TIMEOUT_STAT of register
3700 INTR_STATUS (Section 7.4.7) to inform the Host that the Target Reset action was cancelled due to an
3701 unresolved stall condition that became a timeout, per Section 6.13.2.
3702 • The Host Controller shall set a flag indicating that all subsequent Command Descriptors in the
3703 sequence would be rejected, until it receives the final Target Reset Command Descriptor with field
3704 RESET_OP_TYPE set to the value 0x3.
3705 • Any Command Descriptor that is rejected (i.e., that arrived after the I3C Bus Controller Logic was
3706 forced to drive a STOP condition) shall cause a Response Descriptor to be generated, with error code
3707 0x8 (HC_ABORTED) in field ERR_STATUS.
3708 • When the Host Controller receives the final Target Reset Command Descriptor to leave the Critical
3709 Section, it shall resume processing any subsequent Command Descriptors as normal, and then
3710 generate a Response Descriptor with error code 0x6 (OVL) in field ERR_STATUS to signal failure to
3711 drive any Target Reset action due to underflow of the Command Queue/Ring.
3712 • If the Host Controller processes all the Command Descriptors in a sequence, without error due to
3713 underflow or NACK, and without cancellation or other issue, then:
3714 • Once the Host Controller receives the last Transfer Command for the RSTACT Direct SET CCC with
3715 TOC=1, the Host Controller shall drive the Target Reset Pattern after the end of that Direct SET CCC
3716 segment, followed by a Repeated START and then a STOP.
3717 • When the Host Controller receives the final Target Reset Command Descriptor to leave the Critical
3718 Section, it shall resume processing any subsequent Command Descriptors as normal, and then generate
3719 a Response Descriptor with error code 0x0 (SUCCESS).
3720 Note:
3721 The Host Controller shall always generate a Response Descriptor when it receives the Target
3722 Reset Command Descriptor to leave the Critical Section (i.e., when field RESET_OP_TYPE has a
3723 value of 0x3), either for a successful sequence or for any sequence-related error condition during
3724 the Critical Section.
3725 The Host Controller shall not generate a Response Descriptor for this Target Reset Command
3726 Descriptor, if an individual transfer within the sequence fails with error code 0x5 (NACK) or 0x4
3727 (ADDR_HEADER), as Transfer Command processing would be halted by this error.
3728 Software should follow these requirements and recommendations:
3729 • All Transfer Commands for the Atomic transaction should be a sequence comprised of Broadcast CCCs
3730 and Direct SET CCCs, for the RSTACT CCC, in continuous framing.
3731 • All Transfer Commands must be in SDR Mode, at any supported data rate. Transfer Commands in
3732 HDR Modes are not supported.
3733 • If the sequence has two or more Transfer Commands, the last such Command Descriptor must set field
3734 TOC to 1'b1, and all other Command Descriptors before the last must set field TOC to 1'b0.
3735 • All such Transfer Commands in the sequence should be Immediate Data Transfer Commands per
3736 Section 7.1.2.1 of the I3C TCRI Specification [MIPI06]. Other types of Transfer Commands are not
3737 recommended. Combo Transfer Commands shall not appear in such a sequence

3738 • The first Transfer Command should generally be a Broadcast CCC with a Defining Byte value of 0x00,
3739 to instruct all Target Devices to disable Reset on seeing the Target Reset Pattern.
3740 • If a Broadcast CCC is used, then it should be the first Transfer Command in the sequence (after the
3741 Target Reset Command Descriptor with field RESET_OP_TYPE set to a value of 0x2), and it should not
3742 be sent again at any later point in the sequence.
3743 • The Broadcast CCC with a Defining Byte value of 0x00 is recommended. Use of other Defining Byte
3744 values is not recommended, for most use cases of the RSTACT CCC with Target Reset Pattern.
3745 • Subsequent Transfer Commands should be Direct SET CCCs, to address individual Target Devices.
3746 The Host Controller shall generate Response Descriptors as normal for all Command Descriptors following
3747 the initial Target Reset Command Descriptor to enter the Critical Section. The Host Controller shall also
3748 monitor the transaction status of each Command Descriptor that uses the Direct SET form of the RSTACT
3749 CCC, to ensure that the indicated Target Device ACKs its Dynamic Address. If all such Target Devices
3750 respond properly to the RSTACT CCC for their respective Command Descriptor in the Atomic transaction,
3751 then the Host Controller will know that each addressed Target Device is ready to accept the indicated Target
3752 Reset action, and the Host Controller will drive a single Target Reset Pattern at the appropriate time, instead
3753 of simply driving the STOP (P) condition for TOC=1, as with normal SDR framing (see the I3C
3754 Specification [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.11.1).
3755 However, if any Target Device does not ACK its Dynamic Address, or fails to respond to the RSTACT
3756 CCC, then the Host Controller shall not drive the Target Reset Pattern. Instead, the Host Controller shall
3757 terminate the Atomic transaction and leave the Critical Section after the failed transaction, and immediately
3758 drive the STOP (P) condition, even if the Command Descriptor for that transaction indicated continuation
3759 of framing with field TOC=0. The Host Controller shall generate a Response Descriptor for the failed
3760 transfer, with an appropriate error code in field ERR_STATUS (see Section 6.13.1).
3761 Additionally, the Host Controller shall assert an interrupt via the HC_SEQ_CANCEL_STAT field of register
3762 INTR_STATUS (see Section 7.4.7) to inform the Host of this error. Software should perform an appropriate
3763 error recovery procedure to determine why any of the Target Devices did not respond to the RSTACT CCC
3764 as part of this Atomic transaction.
3765 Software should monitor this process to ensure a successful Target Reset Action, and to understand errors
3766 or other issues that might arise.
3767 • If software receives a Response Descriptor for the Target Reset Command Descriptor to leave the Critical
3768 Section, then it knows that the Host Controller has resumed normal command processing.
3769 • If this Response Descriptor contains any error code other than 0x0 (SUCCESS), then software should
3770 determine the appropriate action to take, based on the error code as well as the error codes in the
3771 Response Descriptors for the individual Transfer Commands in the sequence (i.e., the Broadcast CCC
3772 and the Direct SET CCCs).
3773 • If software receives an error that indicates Command/Response processing has halted due to failure i.e.,
3774 NACK) of an individual transfer in the sequence, then it shall run an error recovery procedure.

6.15.2 Controller SDA Recovery or Bus Reset Procedures
3775 The Host Controller shall support several new procedures added in version 1.1.1+ of the I3C Specification
3776 for recovering the I3C Bus after a Controller reset, or from a Target Device with a stuck SDA Line (see the
3777 I3C Specification [MIPI05] at Section 5.1.10.2.6 and Section 5.1.10.2.7). The Host Controller supports
3778 these flows using Command Descriptors of type Internal Control Command (see Section 8.4.2) with the
3779 value of 0x5 in field MIPI_CMD (see Table 135 and Table 140). In this section and its subsections, such a
3780 Command Descriptor is referred to as a “Recovery Reset Command Descriptor”.
6.15.2.1 Recovering from a Stuck SDA Lane
3781 Software may issue a procedure to recover from a stuck SDA Lane by issuing a Recovery Reset Command
3782 Descriptor with the appropriate options (see Table 140) in order to run the appropriate I3C recovery
3783 procedures (see the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.10.2.6). Field REC_RESET_PROC occupies
3784 Bits[15:12].
3785 • If reading from an I2C Device, then software should enqueue a Recovery Reset Command Descriptor
3786 with value 0x0 in field REC_RESET_PROC.
3787 • If reading from an I3C Device with SDR Mode, then software should enqueue a Recovery Reset
3788 Command Descriptor with value 0x1 in field REC_RESET_PROC.
3789 • If reading from an I3C Device with HDR-DDR Mode, then software should enqueue a Recovery Reset
3790 Command Descriptor with value 0x2 in field REC_RESET_PROC.
3791 The Recovery Reset Command Descriptor should also use an appropriate SCL speed value in field
3792 SCL_SPEED (i.e., Bits[19:16]). The SCL speed value is aligned with the values supported by the various
3793 types of Command Descriptor (Section 8.4) as used for the MODE field. Generally, software should choose
3794 an SCL speed value that is supported by the particular Target Device.
6.15.2.2 Forcing a STOP Condition
3795 If an I3C Target Device fails to respond to some transfers, or if there are other transmission errors, then
3796 forcing a STOP Condition may be used as part of an error recovery procedure. Software may force a STOP
3797 Condition by issuing a Recovery Reset Command Descriptor with the appropriate options (see Table 140)
3798 in order to run the appropriate recovery procedure for various error conditions (see the I3C Specification
3799 [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.10.2). This procedure causes the I3C Bus Controller Logic to force a STOP after
3800 the previous command transfer; however, if both the SDA and SCL Lanes are already High, then the I3C
3801 Bus Controller Logic shall drive a START, followed by the Broadcast Address (i.e., 7'h7E) and a STOP.
3802 This ensures that a STOP is always driven, even if there was no current continuation of the frame or if there
3803 was a Bus Free Condition of any duration from a previous transfer.
3804 Software should enqueue a Recovery Reset Command Descriptor with the value 0x4 in the
3805 REC_RESET_PROC field (i.e., Bits[15:12]), and an appropriate value in the SCL_SPEED field (i.e., Bits
3806 [9:16]). The SCL speed value is aligned with the values supported by the various types of Command
3807 Descriptor (see Section 8.4) used for the MODE field. Generally, software should choose an SCL speed
3808 value that is supported by any particular non-responsive Target Devices, or by the slowest Target Device
3809 present on the I3C Bus, depending on the nature of the transmission error.

6.15.2.3 CE2 Error Handling for a Non-Responsive I3C Target
3810 If an I3C Target Device does not respond to a Private read/write transaction, then the HDR Exit Pattern
3811 may be used as part of an error recovery procedure. Software may issue the HDR Exit Pattern by issuing a
3812 Recovery Reset Command Descriptor with the appropriate options (see Table 140) in order to run the
3813 appropriate recovery procedure (see the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.10.2.5). This procedure
3814 is supported even if the Host Controller does not implement support for any HDR Modes.
3815 Software should enqueue a Recovery Reset Command Descriptor with the value 0x5 in the
3816 REC_RESET_PROC field (i.e., Bits[15:12]), and an appropriate value in the SCL_SPEED field (i.e.,
3817 Bits[19:16]). The SCL speed value is aligned with the values supported by the various types of Command
3818 Descriptor (see Section 8.4) as used for the MODE field. Generally, software should choose an SCL speed
3819 value that is supported by the particular non-responsive Target Device.
6.15.2.4 Controller Recovery After Crash or Unexpected Reset
3820 If the Controller inside the Host Controller crashes, or is reset unexpectedly, and does not know the context
3821 of the Bus, then the Controller must determine the Bus’ state. Software may issue the Bus Reset procedure
3822 by issuing a Recovery Reset Command Descriptor with the appropriate options (see Table 140) in order to
3823 run the appropriate I3C recovery procedure (see the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.10.2.7).
3824 Software should enqueue a Recovery Reset Command Descriptor with value 0x7 in the REC_RESET_PROC
3825 field (i.e., Bits[15:12]), and an appropriate SCL speed value in the SCL_SPEED field (i.e., Bits[19:16]). The
3826 SCL speed value is aligned with the values supported by the various types of Command Descriptor (see
3827 Section 8.4) as used for the MODE field. Generally, software should choose an SCL speed value that is
3828 supported by the slowest Target Device present on the I3C Bus.

6.16  Scheduled Commands
3829  The Host Controller may optionally support Scheduled Commands. The Scheduled Commands capability
3830  allows for issuing certain types of Transfer Commands, according to a programmed schedule based on an
3831  internal timer. This allows Host software to offload frequent transfers to the Host Controller.

3840  In  Figure  29,  a  MUX  represents  the  mechanism  for  selecting  the  operating  context.  This
3841  mechanism allows the I3C Bus Controller Logic to use either the current operating mode (i.e., PIO
3842  vs. DMA) or the Scheduled Commands logic, as and when the Clock Logic determines that
3843  Scheduled Commands should be executed (i.e., at the soonest opportunity). The MUX should only
3844  switch to use Scheduled Commands logic when the current operating mode has finished sending a
3845  sequence of Command Descriptors (i.e., should not switch in the middle of a sequence, nor when
3846  other Command Descriptors are still enqueued). When the Scheduled Commands logic has

finished its execution, the MUX switches back to the current operating mode.

3873 Implementers may choose to support various combinations of the defined Handler Types, based on
3874 the specific use case for a Host Controller. If a Host Controller supports multiple Handler Types,
3875 then each shall have one or more instances of Extended Capability structures (as limited by Table
3876 8) with separate configuration registers in each structure. For each structure, field R/S in register
3877 SCHEDULE_CONFIG shall control whether that instance of Scheduled Commands logic is enabled
3878 or disabled for processing, such that each instance can be enabled or disabled separately from
3879 other instances.
