6.16.1 Common Aspects of Command Scheduling
3880 The defined Handler Types provide different models for preparing Transfer Commands to be executed at
3881 regular opportunities. However, all defined Handler Types share common aspects regarding their
3882 configuration, and also share some registers in their Scheduled Commands Extended Capability structures.
3883 The first few registers in the Scheduled Commands Extended Capability structure share similar key fields.
3884 For example:
3885 • The first such register (i.e., SCHEDULE_CAPABILITIES) defines the clock resolution of the Scheduled
3886 Commands logic, and whether the Scheduled Commands logic supports execution of the Transfer
3887 Command(s) at every N-th opportunity, for configurable values of N (where 1 ≤ N ≤ 256).
3888 • The second such register (i.e., after register SCHEDULE_CAPABILITIES) distinguishes the specific Handler
3889 Type for the structure, and also defines the layout of the remaining registers in the structure. The value of
3890 field SCHED_HANDLER in this register will indicate one of the defined Handler Types in this I3C HCI
3891 Specification; alternately, the value 0x0 indicates an implementer-defined Handler Type (i.e., one that is
3892 not defined in this I3C HCI Specification). For implementer-defined Handler Types, the registers in such
3893 an Extended Capability structure should use the same key fields (including field SCHED_HANDLER).
3894 • The third such register (SCHEDULE_CONFIG) provides control and configuration of the Handler Type
3895 instance, including whether Scheduled Commands processing is enabled for that instance.
3896 Additional registers (i.e., after register SCHEDULE_CONFIG) are specific to the Handler Type.
3897 The Scheduled Commands logic is configurable, and attempts to execute the desired Transfer Command(s)
3898 at specific clock ticks. The tick interval is configured by the Driver (i.e., in relation to the Host Controller’s
3899 clock) such that the Scheduled Commands logic can execute one or more scheduled entities in a Scheduled
3900 Commands Extended Capability structure. Each such entity can be scheduled to be executed within one or
3901 more specific tick intervals. The Scheduled Commands logic supports up to 32 unique tick intervals, and
3902 the total number of supported tick intervals comprises the tick horizon.
3903 Note:
3904 The Scheduled Commands logic iterates over the tick intervals in ascending order, starting with tick
3905 interval 0. Implementers may determine how many tick intervals are supported per tick horizon. The
3906 minimum number of tick intervals is 8, and the recommended number of tick intervals is 32. If the
3907 implementer supports fewer tick intervals per tick horizon, then the corresponding high bits in field
3908 SCHEDULE_MASK within an entity’s mask register shall be read-only, for tick interval numbers that
3909 are not part of the tick horizon. For example, if only 20 tick intervals are supported, then Bits[19:0]
3910 in field SCHEDULE_MASK shall be writeable, but Bits[31:20] in field SCHEDULE_MASK shall be read-
3911 only and fixed to 0x0.
3912 The configurability of each entity varies per the Handler Type:
3913 • For Handler Type 1, an entity is a specific Schedule Table Entry that contains one Transfer Command.
3914 The Driver shall configure the specific tick intervals where each entry can be executed.
3915 • This means that each entry’s single Transfer Command will be executed independently from the others,
3916 at the configured tick intervals, per the value of field SCHEDULE_MASK for that entry (i.e., in register
3917 SCHEDULE_TABLE_##_MASK).
3918 • To disable a particular entry from execution, the Driver should write a value of 0x0 into field
3919 SCHEDULE_MASK for that entry.
3920 • For Handler Type 2, the entire Schedule Sequence is the entity. The Driver shall configure the specific
3921 tick intervals where the entire sequence can be executed (i.e., for all configured Targets).
3922 • This means that the sequence of Transfer Commands will be executed only at the configured tick
3923 intervals, per the value of field SCHEDULE_MASK (i.e., in register SCHEDULE_SEQ_MASK). The
3924 Scheduled Commands logic will iterate over the configured Targets.
134 Copyright © 2018–2023 MIPI Alliance, Inc.
Public Release Edition

Version 1.2 Specification for I3C HCI
15-Feb-2023
3925 • For Handler Type 3, the entire Schedule Buffer is the entity. The Driver shall configure the specific tick
3926 intervals where the entire buffer can be executed.
3927 • This means that the buffer of Transfer Commands will be executed only at the configured tick
3928 intervals, per the value of field SCHEDULE_MASK (i.e., in register SCHEDULE_BUF_MASK).
3929 Each instance of Scheduled Commands logic will indicate the clock resolution in field
3930 CLOCK_RESOLUTION, a read-only field in register SCHEDULE_CAPABILITIES that is set by the implementer
3931 and indicates the number of clock ticks per 1 ms. This is typically derived from the Host Controller’s core
3932 clock, and is set at implementation time. The value in field CLOCK_RESOLUTION is read by the Driver, and
3933 this gives context for how to set field TICK_TIME in register SCHEDULE_CONFIG. For example:
3934 • If the Driver reads from field CLOCK_RESOLUTION and then writes that same value into field TICK_TIME,
3935 then the Scheduled Commands logic shall use a tick interval of 1 ms. (This is the default value for field
3936 TICK_TIME after a Host Controller reset.)
3937 • If the Driver reads from field CLOCK_RESOLUTION, divides that value by 2, and then writes the result into
3938 field TICK_TIME, then the Scheduled Commands logic shall use a tick interval of 500 µs (i.e., half a
3939 millisecond).
3940 • If the Driver reads from field CLOCK_RESOLUTION, multiplies that value by 3, and then writes the result
3941 into field TICK_TIME, then the Scheduled Commands logic shall use a tick interval of 3 ms.
3942 If an instance of Scheduled Commands logic is enabled (i.e., if field R/S in register SCHEDULE_CONFIG is
3943 set to 1'b1), then the Host Controller shall initiate its timer, counting from tick interval 0 to tick interval 31
3944 (or the last supported tick interval, if the Scheduled Commands logic supports fewer tick intervals) at the
3945 configured interval (per field TICK_TIME), and shall then attempt to execute the entities that are configured
3946 to execute at each particular tick interval (per field SCHEDULE_MASK). After the last tick interval in the tick
3947 horizon, the Host Controller shall repeat the cycle starting with tick interval 0. If the entity is configured to
3948 be executed at a particular tick interval (i.e., if the corresponding bit in field SCHEDULE_MASK is set to
3949 1'b1), then the Host Controller is able to execute that entity.
3950 It is possible for multiple entities to be scheduled to execute at the same time. This can happen within a
3951 single instance of Scheduled Commands logic (i.e., only one Handler Type) or across multiple such
3952 instances; however, for multiple instances, this can happen if either:
3953 • The instances have the same value in TICK_TIME, and are configured to execute in the same tick interval;
3954 or
3955 • The instances have different values in TICK_TIME in each instance, and the tick intervals happen to
3956 coincide or overlap.
3957 In either of the cases above, the execution happens according to the following priority based on the Handler
3958 Types that are supported and enabled:
3959 1. First: If an instance of Handler Type 1 exists and is enabled, then the Schedule Table Entries that are
3960 enabled for this tick interval are executed in ascending order (i.e., first entry 0 if enabled, then entry 1
3961 if enabled, etc.).
3962 2. Next: If one or more instances of Handler Type 2 or Handler Type 3 exist and are enabled, then the
3963 instances execute according to the instance ID value (which is unique for each entry) in ascending
3964 order, starting with instance 0, then instance 1, etc.
3965 A. For Handler Type 2, the instance ID is in field HT2_INST_ID in register SCHEDULE_LAYOUT (see
3966 Section 7.7.9.2).
3967 B. For Handler Type 3, the instance ID is in field HT3_INST_ID in register SCHEDULE_LAYOUT (see
3968 Section 7.7.10.2).
3969 The Scheduled Commands logic shall always attempt to complete execution of all scheduled entities for a
3970 particular tick interval. Execution begins as soon as possible when the tick interval begins. However, if the
3971 Bus Controller logic is currently busy executing a Transfer Command from the current execution context
3972 per the operating mode (i.e., Command Queue for PIO Mode, or Command Ring for DMA Mode) or
3973 handling an In-Band Interrupt, then execution of scheduled entities will be delayed. The Bus Controller
3974 logic shall not interrupt a sequence of enqueued Transfer Commands from the Command Queue/Ring (i.e.,
Copyright © 2018–2023 MIPI Alliance, Inc. 135
Public Release Edition

Specification for I3C HCI Version 1.2
15-Feb-2023
3975 as long as field TOC=0) or an ongoing In-Band Interrupt, in order to start execution of any scheduled
3976 entities.
3977 Assuming that the Scheduled Commands logic is able to start execution of scheduled entities for a given
3978 tick interval: if execution of all scheduled entities finishes before the next tick interval starts, and if there
3979 are Transfer Commands that are available for execution in the current execution context (i.e., the Command
3980 Queue/Ring), then the Host Controller shall move to execute the enqueued Transfer Commands in the
3981 current execution context.
3982 If a new tick interval starts before the Scheduled Commands logic is able to finish execution of all
3983 scheduled entities for the previous tick interval, then the Scheduled Commands logic must skip that new
3984 tick interval and generate an interrupt to the Host, to report the missed tick interval. This can occur with
3985 any or all of the following scenarios:
3986 • Scheduling a large number of Transfer Commands (i.e., across multiple entities) that cannot all execute
3987 within a short tick interval
3988 • Scheduling long Transfer Commands (i.e., many data bytes transferred to/from a Target)
3989 • Scheduling slow Transfer Commands (i.e., reduced data transfer rate on the I3C Bus)
3990 • Clock stalling due to overflow or underflow of the data buffer (for PIO Mode only)
3991 • IBI Queue/Ring overflowing, because Host does not drain the IBI Queue/Ring in time to prevent a stall
3992 • Longer sequences of enqueued Transfer Commands in a command sequence (i.e., with field TOC=0) in
3993 the current execution context
3994 The following example shows how the Host Controller determines that it must skip a new tick interval:
3995 1. One or more instances of Scheduled Commands logic are configured with TICK_TIME of 5 ms.
3996 2. At time T + 0, tick interval 1 begins. The Bus Controller logic is not busy, so the Scheduled Commands
3997 logic begins executing the scheduled entities for tick interval 1.
3998 3. The Bus Controller logic takes 3 ms to execute these entities for tick interval 1, and then the Bus goes
3999 idle.
4000 4. At time T + 5, tick interval 2 begins, but the Bus Controller logic is busy processing an In-Band
4001 Interrupt from an I3C Target and/or a sequence of Transfer Commands in the current execution
4002 context.
4003 5. After 3 ms (time T + 8), the Bus Controller logic finishes these actions and begins executing the
4004 scheduled entities for tick interval 2. The Host Controller does not assert an interrupt, since tick
4005 interval 2 was not missed.
4006 6. The Bus Controller logic takes 4 ms to fully execute all such scheduled entities for tick interval 2,
4007 before the I3C Bus becomes idle.
4008 7. At time T + 10, tick interval 3 begins. The Scheduled Commands logic sees the start of this new tick
4009 interval, but is unable to execute any scheduled entities for tick interval 3 (i.e., because the I3C Bus
4010 Controller logic was still busy processing scheduled entities for tick interval 2).
4011 8. The Host Controller asserts an interrupt that indicates that a tick interval was missed.
4012 9. The Bus Controller logic remains busy until time T + 12 and then goes idle.
4013 10. At time T + 15, tick interval 4 begins. The Scheduled Command logic sees the start of this new tick
4014 interval, and is able to execute the scheduled entities.
4015 Note:
4016 The example above is not an exhaustive definition of when a tick interval could be skipped. In this
4017 particular example, it would have been possible for the scheduled entities for tick interval 2 to fully
4018 execute within the 5 ms time window, if the I3C Bus was idle at the start of the tick interval.
4019 However, the ongoing I3C Bus activity at the start of tick interval 2 delayed the execution of the
4020 scheduled entities.
4021 For Handler Type 3 only: if the Schedule Buffer could not be executed because field EXECUTED in
4022 register SCHEDULE_BUF_CONFIG (see Section 7.7.10.5) was set to 1'b1, this does not mean that a
4023 tick interval was missed.

4024 The Host Controller shall report interrupts for missed tick intervals, by asserting field
4025 SCHED_CMD_MISSED_TICK_STAT in register INTR_STATUS (see Section 7.4.7). Implementers may
4026 also choose to support the debug register SCHED_CMDS_DEBUG for Scheduled Commands logic
4027 (see Section 7.7.7.5). If supported, then this debug register shall indicate the specific ID of the
4028 missed tick interval, for such situations where a tick interval is missed.

6.16.2 Handler Type 1: Simple Table
4029 In order to support the Scheduled Commands capability with Handler Type 1, the Host Controller shall
4030 expose a Schedule Table with up to 16 unique entries. Each entry in the Schedule Table may be
4031 programmed to be executed on specific schedule ticks across the schedule horizon. The Schedule Table
4032 shall be exposed as registers in an Extended Capability of type Scheduled Commands, per Section 7.7.8.
4033 The Schedule Table comprises an array of Schedule Table Entries, with each entry containing registers to
4034 hold the schedule tick configuration, as well as additional registers to hold one Command Descriptor. Each
4035 such Command Descriptor shall be a valid Transfer Command describing either a Read-Type transfer with
4036 certain restrictions (such as a Regular Data Transfer or a Combo Transfer), or a Write-Type Immediate Data
4037 Transfer (i.e., a write with Immediate Data Bytes in the Command Descriptor).
4038 • For Read-Type Transfers: The data for a specific transfer that is being read from a Target Device shall
4039 be provided on either the IBI Port (for PIO Mode) or an IBI Pair within a Ring Bundle (for DMA Mode).
4040 If the Host Controller is operating in DMA Mode, then Ring Bundle 0 will always be used for such
4041 notifications.
4042 • For Write-Type Transfers: Write data shall be provided in the Command Descriptor (i.e., only
4043 Immediate Writes are allowed for Scheduled Commands).
4044 The Host Controller shall execute each Scheduled Command either exactly at its programmed time, or at
4045 the earliest opportunity after the programmed time. The execution of Scheduled Commands for a given
4046 schedule tick (i.e., the scheduled event for a command execution) shall not be interleaved with regular
4047 Command Queue servicing (for PIO Mode) or Command Ring servicing for any Ring Bundle that is
4048 enabled and running (for DMA Mode).
4049 The schedule tick for each table entry is programmable, and the schedule horizon is set to 32 schedule ticks
4050 (unless limited by the implementer). Optionally, the Host Controller may support execution on every N-th
4051 opportunity (where N ≤ 256) to allow additional flexibility. For a 1 ms tick, this allows for an horizon of
4052 (32 × 256 =) 8160 ms.
4053 The specific registers defined in subsections of Section 7.7.8 are arranged into an Extended Capability
4054 structure, which may exist within the chain of Extended Capability Structures. An instance of this Extended
4055 Capability structure includes the initial registers (i.e., registers SCHEDULE_CAPABILITIES,
4056 SCHEDULE_TABLE_LAYOUT, and SCHEDULE_CONFIG), which serve as a descriptor for the structure,
4057 followed by an array of Schedule Table Entries. Each Schedule Table Entry consists of registers to hold the
4058 schedule configuration and the Command Descriptor.
4059 Note:
4060 An implementer may define up to one Extended Capability structure of this type. Additionally, each
4061 Scheduled Table entry is limited to one Command Descriptor (i.e., only one Transfer Command).
4062 For applications that require longer sequences of Transfer Commands, the implementer must
4063 implement support for either Handler Type 2 (see Section 6.16.3) and/or Handler Type 3 (see
4064 Section 6.16.4).

6.16.3 Handler Type 2: Command Sequence
4071 In order to support the Scheduled Commands capability with Handler Type 2, the Host Controller shall
4072 expose a Schedule Sequence register set, to hold a single sequence of Command Descriptors, that can be
4073 executed for one or multiple unique Target Devices. The Schedule Sequence entry may hold up to 8
4074 Command Descriptors, as well as additional registers to select the unique Target Devices for which the
4075 sequence of Command Descriptors will be executed. Execution of the sequence may be programmed to be
4076 executed on specific schedule ticks across the schedule horizon. The Schedule Sequence registers shall be
4077 exposed in an Extended Capability of type Scheduled Commands per Section 7.7.9.
4078 Each Command Descriptor in the sequence shall be a valid Transfer Command that describes either a Read-
4079 Type transfer with certain restrictions (such as a Regular Data Transfer or a Combo Transfer), or a Write-
4080 Type Immediate Data Transfer (i.e., a write with Immediate Data Bytes in the Command Descriptor).
4081 • For Read-Type Transfers: The data for a specific transfer that is being read from a Target Device shall
4082 be provided on either the IBI Port (for PIO Mode) or an IBI Ring Pair within a Ring Bundle (for DMA
4083 Mode).
4084 • If the Host Controller is operating in DMA Mode, then the Driver shall choose which Ring Bundle will
4085 be used for such notifications.
4086 • For Write-Type Transfers: Write data shall be provided in the Command Descriptor (i.e., only
4087 Immediate Writes are allowed for Scheduled Commands).
4088 The Host Controller shall execute the sequence of Command Descriptors either exactly at its programmed
4089 time, or at the earliest opportunity after the programmed time. The execution of Scheduled Commands for a
4090 given schedule tick (i.e., the scheduled event for a command execution) shall not be interleaved with
4091 regular Command Queue servicing (for PIO Mode) or Command Ring servicing for any Ring Bundle that
4092 is enabled and running (for DMA Mode). If the configuration registers indicate multiple Targets, then the
4093 sequence shall be executed multiple times in succession, and the Host Controller shall iterate the sequence
4094 over each Target until all Targets have been processed.
4095 The schedule tick for the sequence is programmable, and the schedule horizon is set to 32 schedule ticks
4096 (unless limited by the implementer). Optionally, the Host Controller may support execution on every N-th
4097 opportunity (where N ≤ 256) to allow additional flexibility. For a 1 ms tick, this allows for an horizon of
4098 (32 × 256 =) 8160 ms.
4099 The specific registers defined in subsections of Section 7.7.9 are arranged into an Extended Capability
4100 structure, which may exist within the chain of Extended Capability Structures. Each instance of this
4101 Extended Capability structure includes the initial registers (i.e., registers SCHEDULE_CAPABILITIES,
4102 SCHEDULE_LAYOUT, and SCHEDULE_CONFIG), which serve as a descriptor for the structure, followed by
4103 arrays of registers for the indicated Target Devices as well as the sequence of Command Descriptors. The
4104 configuration registers are common to all indicated Targets.
4105 Note:
4106 Within each Extended Capability structure, an implementer may determine how many Command
4107 Descriptors will be supported for the command sequence, and the SCHEDULE_LAYOUT register
4108 shall indicate the size of the array. If any of the Command Descriptor registers in the array are not
4109 needed (i.e., the command sequence is shorter than the maximum number of Command
4110 Descriptors that could be used) then the Driver shall write a value of 0x7 to field CMD_ATTR for any
4111 unused Command Descriptors, so that the Host Controller knows when to end the sequence.
4112 An implementer may define one or multiple Extended Capability structures of this type, per the use
4113 case, in order to store multiple command sequences that are executed for unique sets of Targets.

6.16.4 Handler Type 3: Schedule Buffer
4120 In order to support the Scheduled Commands capability with Handler Type 3, the Host Controller shall
4121 expose a Schedule Buffer register set to describe a Schedule Buffer that can contain one or more Transfer
4122 Descriptors in Host system memory.
4123 Note:
4124 Handler Type 3 requires the Host Controller to implement support for DMA to access the Host’s
4125 system memory. Many aspects of Handler Type 3 are similar to the execution of Transfer
4126 Commands in a Command/Response Ring Pair for DMA Mode (see Section 6.6.2). However, DMA
4127 Mode is not required to be supported if Handler Type 3 is supported. If the Host Controller supports
4128 DMA Mode, then Handler Type 3 is the recommended option for Scheduled Commands
4129 capabilities.
4130 The Schedule Buffer is defined in Host system memory, and is an array of up to 255 Transfer Descriptors as
4131 defined in Section 8.3. Each Transfer Descriptor shall contain a Command Descriptor. The array of
4132 Transfer Descriptors shall be executed in sequence, and may be programmed to be executed on specific
4133 schedule ticks across the schedule horizon. The Schedule Buffer registers shall be exposed in an Extended
4134 Capability of type Scheduled Commands, per Section 7.7.10.
4135 Note:
4136 The Driver shall allocate sufficient Host system memory to store the Schedule Buffer, and this
4137 memory allocation must be large enough to hold enough Transfer Commands, based on the value
4138 written into field TRANSFER_COUNT in register SCHEDULE_BUF_CONFIG (see Section 7.7.10.5).
4139 Each such Command Descriptor in this array of Transfer Descriptors shall be a valid Transfer Command
4140 that describes either a Read-Type transfer with certain restrictions (such as a Regular Data Transfer or a
4141 Combo Transfer), or any Write-Type Transfer.
4142 • For Read-Type Transfers: The Host Controller can be configured to provide read data for a specific
4143 transfer (i.e., data being read from a Target Device) on either the IBI Queue (for PIO Mode), an IBI Ring
4144 Pair within a Ring Bundle (for DMA Mode), or the Data Buffer Descriptor within the specific Transfer
4145 Descriptor.
4146 • If the Host Controller is operating in DMA Mode, then the Driver shall choose which Ring Bundle will
4147 be used for such notifications.
4148 • Using the Data Buffer Descriptor for read data requires the Host to pre-allocate sufficient system
4149 memory for each expected Read-Type transfer, and then populate the Data Buffer Descriptor with a
4150 valid address for receiving that read data.
4151 • For Write-Type Transfers: Write data may be provided in either the Command Descriptor (i.e., an
4152 Immediate Write) or within the pre-allocated Host system memory described by the Data Buffer
4153 Descriptor within each Transfer Descriptor.
4154 The Host Controller shall execute the sequence of Command Descriptors either exactly at its programmed
4155 time, or at the earliest opportunity after the programmed time. The execution of Scheduled Commands for a
4156 given schedule tick (i.e., the scheduled event for a command execution) shall not be interleaved with
4157 regular Command Queue servicing (for PIO Mode) or Command Ring servicing for any Ring Bundle that
4158 is enabled and running (for DMA Mode). The Host Controller shall execute the sequence of Command
4159 Descriptors in sequential order until it either reaches the end of the Schedule Buffer, or else sees a
4160 Command Descriptor that denotes the end of the sequence.
4161 The schedule tick for the sequence is programmable, and the schedule horizon is set to 32 schedule ticks
4162 (unless limited by the implementer). Optionally, the Host Controller may support execution on every N-th
4163 opportunity (where N ≤ 256) to allow additional flexibility. For a 1 ms tick, this allows for an horizon of
4164 (32 × 256 =) 8160 ms.
4165 The specific registers defined in subsections of Section 7.7.10 are arranged into an Extended Capability
4166 structure, which may exist within the chain of Extended Capability Structures. Each instance of this
4167 Extended Capability structure includes the initial registers (i.e., registers SCHEDULE_CAPABILITIES,

4168  SCHEDULE_LAYOUT, and SCHEDULE_CONFIG), which serve as a descriptor for the structure, followed by
4169  other registers that describe and point to the Schedule Buffer.
4170  Note:
4171  Within  the  allocated  Schedule  Buffer,  an  implementer  may  determine  how  many  Transfer
4172  Descriptors will be executed, up to the maximum limit of 255. If the number of Transfer Descriptors
4173
is short (i.e., is less than the amount of system memory allocated by the Host), then the Driver shall
4174  write a value of 0x7 to field CMD_ATTR for any unused Command Descriptors, so that the Host
4175  Controller knows when to end the sequence.
4176
An implementer may define one or multiple Extended Capability structures of this type, per the use
4177  case, in order to describe multiple Schedule Buffers that are executed for unique sets of Targets.

6.17 Standby Controller Mode
4183 The Host Controller may optionally support Standby Controller mode, which includes Secondary
4184 Controller Logic and support for transitioning between Standby Controller mode (i.e., playing the Target
4185 role but also possessing Secondary Controller capabilities) and Active Controller mode (i.e., playing the
4186 Active Controller role).
4187 While operating in Standby Controller mode, the Host Controller shall support handling CCCs
4188 (Section 6.17.3.1) as though it were a limited-function I3C Target Device with additional I3C Secondary
4189 Controller capabilities.
4190 Minimum Requirements for Standby Controller Mode
4191 In order to support Standby Controller mode, the following capabilities, attributes, and logic are required
4192 (these are in addition to those required to support Active Controller mode):
4193 • Standby Controller Mode Extended Capability structure, with Extended Capability ID 0x12
4194 (Section 7.7.11)
4195 • Support for the mandatory registers in this Extended Capability structure
4196 • Minimal Secondary Controller Logic, including:
4197 • Minimum Bus Management Procedures, as defined by the I3C Specification at Section 5.1.7.3.2
4198 [MIPI02]
4199 • Support for the Standby Controller Interrupt logic, which allows additional interrupts to be routed to
4200 the Host via the System Bus
4201 • Support for autonomous response to standard CCCs that are required for the role of Secondary
4202 Controller on an I3C Bus (Section 6.17.3.1.1)
4203 • Controller Role FSM, including:
4204 • In Active Controller mode, sufficient checking of pre-Handoff readiness condition to ensure that all
4205 prerequisites for passing the Controller Role have been met, and that no other Command Descriptors
4206 would interfere with the Handoff process
4207 • Special command support for the sub-command that sends the GETACCCR CCC and initiates the
4208 Controller-to-Controller Handoff Procedure using the special Command Descriptor format, i.e., an
4209 Internal Control Command Type with field MIPI_CMD having a value of 0x7 (Section 8.4.2.7)
4210 • Support for transitioning from Active Controller mode to Standby Controller mode, where the Bus
4211 Controller Logic becomes idle after successfully passing the Controller Role to another Controller-
4212 capable Device (i.e., a Secondary Controller) and Secondary Controller Logic becomes active
4213 • Sufficient checking of pre-handoff acceptance condition in Standby Controller mode, to ensure that all
4214 necessary steps in receiving the most current Bus configuration from the Active Controller have been
4215 performed and have been handled by Host software (see Section 6.17.4)
4216 • Support for transitioning from Standby Controller mode to Active Controller mode, where the
4217 Secondary Controller Logic goes idle after successfully accepting the Controller Role from the Active
4218 Controller, and the Bus Controller Logic becomes active
4219 • Support for Error Type CE3 checking, to ensure that the new Active Controller successfully asserts its
4220 ownership of the Controller Role after the Controller-to-Controller Handoff Procedure
4221 Note:
4222 A Host Controller that only implements the minimum requirements specified above is also called a
4223 Minimal Standby Controller in this I3C HCI Specification. Such minimum requirements allow the
4224 Host Controller to pass the Controller Role to a Secondary Controller, and to receive the Controller
4225 Role again.

4226 Optional Standby Controller Mode Capabilities
4227 In addition to the minimum requirements, implementers may also choose to implement additional
4228 capabilities, attributes, and logic, in order to provide additional behavior or to enable use cases that depend
4229 on other actions required of the Host Controller while it is operating as a Standby Controller (i.e., while it is
4230 in the Secondary Controller role).
4231 • Support for Initialization as a Secondary Controller on the I3C Bus:
4232 • Standby Controller mode Bus connection logic, which allows the Host Controller to connect to the I3C
4233 Bus as an I3C Target with Secondary Controller capabilities;
4234 • Support for receiving a Dynamic Address from the Active Controller, using at least one supported
4235 method of Dynamic Address Assignment (i.e., any of the defined CCCs)
4236 • If Dynamic Address Assignment with ENTDAA is supported, then the Hot-Join Request shall also be
4237 generated, as and when the Driver indicates that the Host Controller should Join the I3C Bus
4238 • Support for receiving Bus Configuration changes from the Active Controller (i.e., via the DEFTGTS
4239 and DEFGRPA CCCs)
4240 • Additional Secondary Controller Logic, including:
4241 • Additional Secondary Controller functions, such as Bus Configuration Procedures, as defined at
4242 Section 5.1.7.3.3 of the I3C Specification [MIPI02]
4243 • Any other optional Secondary Controller capabilities deemed necessary by the implementer, listed in
4244 Section 5.1.7.3 (and relevant sub-sections) of the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.7.3
4245 • Support for autonomous response to additional CCCs. This may also include CCCs supported by
4246 extensions to Secondary Controller Logic per Section 6.17.3.1.2. The implementer may determine
4247 whether the Secondary Controller Logic supports responses for any additional CCCs, and if so, which
4248 additional CCCs will be supported.
4249 • Other optional capabilities and attributes, as defined by the implementer.

4258  If the Host Controller is configured as a Primary Controller on the I3C Bus, then it shall start operations in
4259  Active Controller mode, and it shall be responsible for initializing the I3C Bus as the Primary Controller
(see the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.7).
4260
4261  If the Host Controller is configured as a Secondary Controller on the I3C Bus, then it shall start operations
4262  in Standby Controller mode, and shall act as a Target on the I3C Bus, and shall report that it is a Controller-
capable Device (i.e., that it has Secondary Controller capabilities). The Device may request the Controller
4263
4264  Role from the Active Controller, and if it successfully receives the Controller Role from an Active
4265  Controller (e.g., the Primary Controller), then it will transition to Active Controller mode (see the I3C
Specification [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.6.3). While operating in Standby Controller mode, the functionality
4266
4267  and logic within the Host Controller that is active and that handles configuration and transactions as a
limited-capability I3C Target on the I3C Bus (i.e., in the Target role including Secondary Controller
4268
4269  capabilities) is called Secondary Controller Logic, to distinguish it from the Bus Controller Logic (which is
4270  active and handles configuration and transactions as an I3C Controller in Active Controller mode, fulfilling
4271  the Active Controller role).
4272  Additional Active Controller Requirements
4273  If the Host Controller supports Standby Controller mode and includes Secondary Controller logic, then the
Bus Controller Logic shall also support the following capabilities:
4274
4275  • If the Host Controller is a Secondary Controller and subsequently becomes the Active Controller (as
4276  described above), then it may subsequently pass the Controller Role to another Controller-capable
4277  Device, using the GETACCCR CCC (per Section 6.17.2).
4278  • If the Host Controller (as Active Controller) passes the Controller Role to another Secondary Controller,
4279  but that Secondary Controller does not respond in time or does not assert its Controller Role status (i.e.,
4280  according to Error Type CE3), then the Host Controller shall reclaim the Controller Role and become
4281  Active Controller again.

4282 Initialization and FSM
4283 The transitions between Active Controller mode and Standby Controller mode are handled by the
4284 Controller Role FSM. Field AC_CURRENT_OWN in register PRESENT_STATE (see Section 7.4.6) indicates
4285 whether or not the Bus Controller Logic is active, i.e., whether or not the Host Controller is the Active
4286 Controller and is responsible for driving the SCL (clock) line.
4287 Note:
4288 The operation and initial state of the Controller Role FSM will depend on whether the Host
4289 Controller also supports the optional Dead Bus Recovery Mechanism (see Section 6.18,
4290 Section 7.7.6, and Section 8.4.2.8). If this optional mechanism is supported, then the Host may
4291 choose whether to select the role on startup (i.e., based on Driver configuration), or else engage
4292 the Dead Bus Recovery mechanism to attempt to detect whether the I3C Bus already has an Active
4293 Controller. If the Host uses the Dead Bus Recovery Mechanism, then fields ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT
4294 and AC_CURRENT_OWN are automatically set based on the operation of the Dead Bus Recovery
4295 Mechanism, and the Driver should not write to these fields.
4296 However, if the Host Controller does not also support the Dead Bus Recovery Mechanism, then the
4297 Host shall choose to select the role on startup (i.e., based on Driver configuration) according to the
4298 initialization flow in this section. The remainder of this section generally assumes that the Dead Bus
4299 Recovery Mechanism is either not supported, or that the Driver has chosen not to use the Dead
4300 Bus Recovery Mechanism.
4301 In Standby Controller mode, field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1)
4302 is used to enable readiness to accept the Controller Role and to enable the Controller-to-Controller Handoff
4303 Procedure, thereby becoming the Active Controller; or to cancel such readiness and remain a Secondary
4304 Controller in Standby Controller mode. In Active Controller mode field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT is also used,
4305 but in this case to allow software to enqueue the special command to pass the Controller Role to another
4306 Controller-capable Device (i.e., a Secondary Controller) on the I3C Bus, initiating the Controller-to-
4307 Controller Handoff Procedure per Section 5.1.7.2 of the I3C Specification [MIPI02].
4308 The Controller Role FSM allows flexibility for an implementer to customize a Host Controller for various
4309 use cases:
4310 • Figure 34 shows a variant of the Controller Role FSM for a Host Controller that only supports
4311 initialization in Active Controller mode (i.e., as the Primary Controller of the I3C Bus) and supports the
4312 minimal Standby Controller mode capabilities. In this variant, the Host Controller would always be
4313 primed to accept the Controller Role after passing the Controller Role to another Secondary Controller
4314 Device.
4315 • Figure 35 shows a variant of the Controller Role FSM for a Host Controller that supports initialization in
4316 either Active Controller mode (i.e., as the Primary Controller of the I3C Bus) or Standby Controller mode
4317 (i.e., as a Secondary Controller with optional features and capabilities).

6.17.1 Configuration and Modes of Operation
4322 The Driver shall configure the Host Controller, along with its I3C Bus Controller Logic and I3C Secondary
4323 Controller Logic, in the appropriate manner and order. The order of the steps to configure a Host Controller
4324 must account for the supported capabilities, and should proceed according to the desired flow and mode of
4325 operation.
4326 Configuration of I3C Secondary Controller Logic
4327 The Driver shall determine which of the following configuration flow options to use to set the Host
4328 Controller’s initial role on the I3C Bus and its initial mode of operation.
4329 • Option 1: I3C Primary Controller Only (i.e., Active Controller mode) without support for Controller-
4330 to-Controller Handoff Procedure:
4331 A. The Driver initializes only the Host Controller’s I3C Bus Controller Logic.
4332 B. The Driver then enables only the Host Controller’s I3C Bus Controller Logic, by writing a value
4333 of 1'b1 to field BUS_ENABLE in register HC_CONTROL (Section 7.4.2).
4334 C. The Host Controller begins operation in Active Controller mode.
4335 D. Transitions from Active Controller mode to Standby Controller mode are not possible.
4336 • Option 2: I3C Primary Controller (i.e., Active Controller mode) with support for Controller-to-
4337 Controller Handoff Procedure:
4338 A. The Driver initializes both the Host Controller’s I3C Bus Controller Logic and its I3C Secondary
4339 Controller Logic (per Section 6.17.1.2).
4340 B. The Driver then enables the I3C Bus Controller Logic (see Option 1, step B above); sets the initial
4341 mode and role by writing a value of 1'b1 to field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT in register
4342 STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1); and then enables the I3C Secondary Controller Logic by
4343 writing a value of 2'b01 to field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL.
4344 C. The Host Controller begins operation in Active Controller mode. The Secondary Controller Logic
4345 remains in a standby state because the Bus Controller Logic is active (i.e., as the Primary
4346 Controller).
4347 D. Transitions from Active Controller mode to Standby Controller mode are possible, using the pre-
4348 Handoff steps followed by the special Command Descriptor (per Section 6.17.2).
4349 • Option 3: I3C Secondary Controller (i.e., Standby Controller mode) with support for accepting the
4350 Controller Role from the Active Controller:
4351 A. The Driver initializes both the Host Controller’s I3C Bus Controller Logic and its I3C Secondary
4352 Controller Logic (per Section 6.17.1.3).
4353 B. The then Driver sets the initial mode and role by writing a value of 1'b0 to field
4354 ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1); enables the I3C
4355 Secondary Controller Logic by writing a value of either 2'b10 or 2'b11 to field
4356 STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1); and then enables the
4357 I3C Bus Controller Logic (see Option 1, step B above).
4358 C. The Host Controller begins operation in Standby Controller mode. The Bus Controller Logic
4359 remains in a standby state, and the Secondary Controller Logic becomes ready to respond to
4360 Dynamic Address Assignment (see Section 6.17.1.3).
4361 D. Transitions from Standby Controller mode to Active Controller mode are possible, provided that
4362 the Host Controller has received a Dynamic Address, and that the Driver has primed the
4363 Secondary Controller Logic to automatically accept the GETACCCR CCC. This may be done
4364 either at the time of enabling, or at a subsequent time.

6.17.1.1 Secondary Controller Initialization
4392 To initialize the Host Controller to operate as a Secondary Controller, either at initialization time or in the
4393 future, the Driver must configure the Secondary Controller Logic by writing values to the appropriate
4394 registers in the Standby Controller Mode Extended Capability structure (see Section 7.7.11).
4395 In addition to the standard Host Controller initialization steps defined in Section 6.1, the Driver should also
4396 perform the following steps:
4397 1. Evaluate the Standby Controller Mode Extended Capability structure (see Section 7.7.11):
4398 A. Determine whether an I3C Target Transaction Interface to software is supported.
4399 If this interface is supported, then discover its capabilities and configure the interface
4400 appropriately (i.e., by using its vendor-specified Extended Capability structure). Then,
4401 enable the interface using field TARGET_XACT_ENABLE in register STBY_CR_CONTROL
4402 (Section 7.7.11.1).
4403 B. Determine which methods of Dynamic Address Assignment are implemented and supported, by
4404 reading register STBY_CR_CAPABILITIES (Section 7.7.11.3)
4405 C. Determine which other CCCs need to be supported and configured, either as registers in the
4406 Standby Controller Mode Extended Capability structure, or as registers in any instances of other
4407 vendor-specific Extended Capability structures that might be defined to provide control for such
4408 CCC handling.
4409 2. Set the BCR bits and the DCR value in register STBY_CR_DEVICE_CHAR (Section 7.7.11.5).
4410 3. Optionally, set the PID value in registers STBY_CR_DEVICE_CHAR and STBY_CR_DEVICE_PID_LO
4411 (Section 7.7.11.5 and Section 7.7.11.6) if required for the Dynamic Address Assignment with ENTDAA
4412 procedure, or if it is known that the GETPID CCC will be used by an Active Controller.
4413 4. Configure registers to set up autonomous responses for CCCs, for those CCCs that are defined for such
4414 handling in this specification (see Section 6.17.3.1).
4415 5. Enable Secondary Controller Interrupts:
4416 In register STBY_CR_INTR_SIGNAL_ENABLE (Section 7.7.11.8), set the mask of enabled
4417 interrupts.
4418 These steps might need to be done at different times, depending on the Host Controller’s role when it
4419 begins operation on the I3C Bus. Additionally, some steps might be omitted or delayed (i.e., might be
4420 executed after the steps that initialize and enable the Secondary Controller Logic), depending on the initial
4421 role and use case.
4422 After completing the initialization of the Secondary Controller Logic, the Driver may set field
4423 STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1) to enable the Secondary
4424 Controller Logic. Per Section 6.17.1, the value written to this field, and the order in which the Bus
4425 Controller Logic and the Secondary Controller Logic are enabled by the Driver, shall determine the Host
4426 Controller’s initial role on the I3C Bus, as well as the initial operating mode.

6.17.1.2 Configuration in Active Controller Mode
4427 If the Host Controller is initialized in Active Controller mode and, and if it wishes to control the I3C Bus as
4428 the Primary Controller, then the Driver should first perform all of the steps in the Host Controller
4429 initialization procedure as defined in Section 6.1.1, and then perform all the steps of the Secondary
4430 Controller Initialization procedure as defined in Section 6.17.1.1.
4431 Following that, the Driver must configure the Host Controller to have a Dynamic Address by writing to the
4432 appropriate fields of register CONTROLLER_DEVICE_ADDR (Section 7.4.3).
4433 Note:
4434 For this configuration, The Driver should not attempt to configure a Static Address in register
4435 STBY_CR_DEVICE_ADDR (Section 7.7.11.2) because the Driver assigns the initial Dynamic
4436 Address. However, after passing the Controller Role, another Controller-capable Device might
4437 change or reset this Dynamic Address, so the Driver should enable at least one supported mode for
4438 Dynamic Address Assignment in Standby Controller mode (per Section 6.17.1.3). For such
4439 situations, Dynamic Address Assignment with the ENTDAA procedure is recommended.
4440 The Driver should then:
4441 1. Start the Host Controller in Active Controller mode.
4442 2. Write a value of 1'b1 to field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1)
4443 to set the initial mode and role as Active Controller.
4444 3. Enable the Secondary Controller Logic by writing a value of 2'b01 to field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in
4445 register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1).
4446 Note:
4447 The Host Controller shall begin operation in Active Controller mode, since the I3C Bus Controller
4448 Logic was enabled first, and since field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT was set to 1'b1 when the Secondary
4449 Controller Logic was subsequently enabled. Because the Host Controller is initially operating in
4450 Active Controller mode, the Secondary Controller Logic must start in a standby state. The
4451 Secondary Controller Logic shall remain in standby (not in the transitional state per Section 6.17.2)
4452 until the Driver enters the transitional state and subsequently issues the special Command
4453 Descriptor to send the GETACCCR CCC, initiating the Controller-to-Controller Handoff Procedure.
4454 If those steps are successful, then the Controller Role will have been successfully passed to
4455 another Controller-capable Device on the I3C Bus; only then would the Secondary Controller Logic
4456 be active.

6.17.1.3 Initialization and Dynamic Address Assignment in Standby Controller Mode
4457 If the Host Controller is initialized in Standby Controller Mode and wishes to join the I3C Bus as a
4458 Secondary Controller, then the Driver must configure it to participate in Dynamic Address Assignment so
4459 that the I3C Bus’ Active Controller can assign a Dynamic Address (see the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at
4460 Section 5.1.4.2).
4461 For the initialization and process of joining the I3C Bus in Standby Controller mode, the Driver must
4462 perform the following steps:
4463 1. Perform steps 1–10 in the Host Controller Initialization procedure (per Section 6.1.1), but stop before
4464 enabling the Host Controller via register HC_CONTROL (i.e., stop before step 11). Refer to
4465 Section 6.17.1 for details on how the order in which the I3C Bus Controller Logic and I3C Secondary
4466 Controller Logic are enabled determines the Host Controller’s initial mode and role.
4467 2. Perform all of the steps in the Secondary Controller Initialization procedure per Section 6.17.1.1
4468 3. Enable at least one supported method for Dynamic Address Assignment, using register
4469 STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1).
4470 If using any of the methods that rely on Static Addresses (i.e., SETDASA or SETAASA), then
4471 also program the assigned Static Address into field STATIC_ADDR in register
4472 STBY_CR_DEVICE_ADDR (Section 7.7.11.1), and also set its field STATIC_ADDR_VALID to 1'b1.
4473 Note that knowledge of the Static Address must also be programmed into the Primary
4474 Controller.
4475 4. Write a value of 1'b0 to field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1)
4476 to set the initial mode and role as Secondary Controller.
4477 5. Enable the Secondary Controller Logic by writing to field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register
4478 STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1).
4479 A. If the Secondary Controller Logic supports sending a Hot-Join Request, then it shall also support
4480 Dynamic Address Assignment with the ENTDAA CCC. That is, fields DAA_ENTDAA_SUPPORT in
4481 register STBY_CR_CAPABILITIES (Section 7.7.11.3) and DAA_ENTDAA_ENABLE in register
4482 STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1) shall both have a value of 1'b1.
4483 To use Hot-Join, the Driver shall write a value of 2'b11 to field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in
4484 register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1). This shall enable the Secondary
4485 Controller Logic, and trigger it to emit the Hot-Join Request, once it has determined that
4486 it has met the conditions of eligibility as a Hot-Joining Target, as defined by the I3C
4487 Specification at Section 5.1.5 [MIPI02]. Note that the Driver must not assign a Dynamic
4488 Address to the Host Controller (i.e., field DYNAMIC_ADDR_VALID in register
4489 STBY_CR_DEVICE_ADDR must have a value of 1'b0).
4490 While the Secondary Controller Logic is still waiting to emit its first Hot-Join Request,
4491 field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1) shall
4492 return a value of 2'b11 on a subsequent read.
4493 Once the Secondary Controller Logic has successfully emitted its first Hot-Join Request
4494 (which the Active Controller might respond to with either an ACK a NACK), field
4495 STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT shall return a value of 2'b10 on a subsequent read. Additionally,
4496 field HJ_REQ_STATUS in register STBY_CR_STATUS (see Section 7.7.11.4) shall return a
4497 value of 1 on a subsequent read.
4498 Note:
4499 Since Dynamic Address Assignment may happen at some time after the Hot-Join Request,
4500 the Driver should watch for a subsequent interrupt that signals a successful assignment of
4501 a Dynamic Address, with interrupt STBY_CR_DYN_ADDR_STAT (see Section 7.7.11.7).
4502 B. If Hot-Join Requests are not supported, or if the Driver does not wish to use Hot-Join, then the
4503 Driver shall write 2'b10 to field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL
4504 (Section 7.7.11.1). This shall enable the Secondary Controller Logic, which will then wait

4505 passively for Dynamic Address Assignment, using any of the methods that are both supported in
4506 register STBY_CR_CAPABILITIES and enabled in register STBY_CR_CONTROL. Assigning a
4507 Dynamic Address from a Static Address requires the Driver to write a valid Static Address to field
4508 STATIC_ADDR in register STBY_CR_DEVICE_ADDR, and also requires the Active Controller (i.e., the
4509 Primary Controller) to know this Address via other means.
4510 Note:
4511 This I3C HCI Specification does not define a method to inform the Primary Controller of this
4512 Static Address.
4513 6. Subsequently, enable the Bus Controller Logic per steps 11 and higher (as applicable) of the Host
4514 Controller Initialization procedure defined in Section 6.1.1.
4515 Note:
4516 At the time that the Secondary Controller Logic was enabled, field BUS_ENABLE in register
4517 HC_CONTROL was not yet set to 1'b1 (per step 1 above) and field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT was
4518 set to 1'b0. As a result, the Host Controller shall begin operation in Standby Controller mode,
4519 with a Secondary Controller role on the I3C Bus.
4520 If the Driver does not subsequently enable the Bus Controller Logic, then the Host Controller
4521 will not be able to accept the Controller Role from the Active Controller, and will be unable to
4522 transition into Active Controller mode. In such a state, the Host Controller shall not allow the
4523 Secondary Controller Logic to be primed to accept the GETACCCR CCC.
4524 After the Driver writes to field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT, it shall wait for a subsequent
4525 STBY_CR_DYN_ADDR_STAT interrupt (read from register STBY_CR_INTR_STATUS [Section 7.7.11.3]) for
4526 notification that a Dynamic Address has been successfully assigned.
4527 At any time after initial Dynamic Address Assignment, the Active Controller may reconfigure the Dynamic
4528 Address using the SETNEWDA CCC, or reset the Dynamic Address using the RSTDAA CCC. Changes to
4529 the Dynamic Address will be reflected in field DYNAMIC_ADDR in register STBY_CR_DEVICE_ADDR
4530 (Section 7.7.11.2). If the Active Controller uses the RSTDAA CCC to reset the Dynamic Address, then the
4531 DYNAMIC_ADDR_VALID field will read as 1'b0 until the Active Controller sets a new Dynamic Address using
4532 a supported method. Any such changes of the Dynamic Address or its validity may generate subsequent
4533 STBY_CR_DYN_ADDR_STAT interrupts (read from register STBY_CR_INTR_STATUS) to notify the Host that
4534 configuration changes have been made.
4535 This shall also apply to a Host Controller that was formerly an Active Controller (e.g., the Primary
4536 Controller, as shown in Section 6.17.1.2) and subsequently passed the Controller Role to another
4537 Controller-capable Device on the I3C Bus.
4538 Note:
4539 Many of the fields for configuration registers in the Standby Controller Mode Extended Capability
4540 structure (Section 7.7.11) cannot be changed while the Host Controller is enabled in Standby
4541 Controller mode (i.e., if field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL is set to a non-
4542 zero value). In such a state, the Host Controller shall block writes to these fields. These fields may
4543 only be changed while the Host Controller is disabled, since such changes would not be known to
4544 the other Active Controller, and such a change might violate a private contract or create a mismatch
4545 in expectations.

6.17.2 Transition from Active Controller Mode to Standby Controller Mode
4546 To transition the Host Controller into Standby Controller mode, the Driver shall perform the following
4547 high-level procedures:
4548 1. Determine the appropriate steps to prepare the I3C Bus for the Controller-to-Controller Handoff
4549 Procedure, per Section 5.1.7.1 of the I3C Specification [MIPI02].
4550 2. Prepare the Host Controller for handoff (see Section 6.17.2.1).
4551 3. Once the Host Controller is ready to transition, enqueue the special Command Descriptor to transition
4552 to Standby Controller mode (see Section 6.17.2.2).
4553 This special Command Descriptor is a sub-command of the Internal Control Command, which
4554 may only be used in this transitional state. The sub-command sends the GETACCCR CCC and
4555 automatically initiates the Controller-to-Controller Handoff Procedure, using the I3C Bus
4556 Controller Logic and I3C Secondary Controller Logic within the Host Controller (see
4557 Section 8.4.2.7).
4558 4. Remain ready to receive the Controller Role again, if any of the following events occur:
4559 A. If the Secondary Controller Logic detects an Error Type CE3 failure and initiates an automatic
4560 return to Active Controller mode, due to the chosen Secondary Controller (i.e., the new Active
4561 Controller) failing to assert its Controller Role status, after a handoff that was initially presumed to
4562 be successful. See the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.10.2.4.
4563 B. If the new Active Controller subsequently sends the GETACCCR CCC. (If this Host Controller’s
4564 I3C Secondary Controller Logic is primed to automatically accept the CCC, then per
4565 Section 6.17.4 it shall do so.)
4566 In the Active Controller mode, the I3C Bus Controller Logic may be configured to accept a Controller Role
4567 Request (CRR) when the CRR_REJECT field in the relevant DAT entry for the Target is cleared. Once the
4568 Controller Role Request is accepted from a specific Secondary Controller Device, the Driver is then
4569 responsible for initiating the above high-level procedures for transitioning to Standby Controller mode. The
4570 Host Controller shall not automatically initiate the steps listed above to send the GETACCCR CCC in
4571 response to a Controller Role Request. The Driver may also use the above procedures to send the
4572 GETACCCR CCC using the special Command Descriptor without previously receiving any Controller Role
4573 Request from a Secondary Controller Device.
4574 Before passing the Controller Role to the chosen Secondary Controller Device, the Driver may announce
4575 the Bus configuration with the DEFTGTS Broadcast CCC (and other DEFGRPA Broadcast CCCs if
4576 applicable). If this configuration has not been announced since any changes to such Bus configuration, then
4577 this announcement before passing the Controller Role is mandatory, and the Driver must then verify that
4578 the chosen Secondary Controller Device has received and processed the data in the announced
4579 configuration data, and is ready to accept the Controller Role.
4580 Note:
4581 When sending the DEFTGTS Broadcast CCC, software is responsible for assembling the CCC’s
4582 data message in the correct format (see the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.9.3.7) and
4583 enqueueing the CCC as a Command Descriptor. The data message must include a descriptor for
4584 the Active Controller, including its Dynamic Address, DCR, BCR, and Static Address (i.e., 7'h7E) as
4585 defined for the DEFTGTS Broadcast CCC. The Host Controller and its Bus Controller Logic will not
4586 generate this Broadcast CCC automatically.

6.17.2.1 Preparing the Host Controller for Controller Role Handoff
4587 Before entering the special transitional state, the Driver shall either clear Rings/Queues from all commands,
4588 or else work to process any enqueued Transfer Commands while blocking new Transfer Commands. The
4589 Driver shall also disable In-Band Interrupt Requests, including Controller Role Requests and Hot-Join
4590 Requests from all Target Devices other than the chosen Secondary Controller Device. The Driver shall also
4591 take any other steps necessary to prepare the I3C Bus for passing the Controller Role, per Section 5.1.7.1 of
4592 the I3C Specification [MIPI02].
4593 The transition to Standby Controller mode is explicitly enabled by writing the value 1'b0 to field
4594 ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (see Section 7.7.11.1), however this is usually only
4595 the last step the Driver takes before sending the special Command Descriptor to transition to Standby
4596 Controller mode. Several other key requirements must be met before the Driver writes this value to prepare
4597 for the transition.
4598 The Host Controller shall ensure that all of the following necessary pre-Handoff conditions have been met:
4599 1. Secondary Controller Logic has been configured per Section 6.17.1.2.
4600 This includes setting field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL to a
4601 non-zero value (Section 7.7.11.1)
4602 2. The Host Controller has been configured with a valid Dynamic Address that has been broadcast to the
4603 chosen Secondary Controller Device, using the DEFTGTS CCC.
4604 A. In register CONTROLLER_DEVICE_ADDR (Section 7.4.3), field DYNAMIC_ADDR_VALID must be set
4605 to 1'b1 and field DYNAMIC_ADDR must be set to a Dynamic Address that is valid for an I3C
4606 Device. This Dynamic Address will become the Host Controller’s Dynamic Address once it
4607 successfully passes the Controller Role.
4608 Note:
4609 Software should have previously sent the DEFTGTS CCC to announce the list of all
4610 Devices (including the Dynamic Address of this Host Controller as the Active Controller) to
4611 any Secondary Controller Devices on the I3C Bus, to ensure that the chosen Secondary
4612 Controller Device knows the current configuration (see I3C Specification [MIPI02] at
4613 Section 5.1.9.3.7).
4614 3. The active Command Queue/Ring must be otherwise empty, and any other enabled Command
4615 Queues/Rings shall either be fully drained, quiesced or otherwise disabled, to prevent any
4616 interruptions.
4617 A. For DMA Mode: If the Host Controller supports multiple Ring Bundles (per Section 6.6.5), then
4618 the Command/Response Ring Pairs for such Ring Bundles that are enabled and running should be
4619 disabled or halted; or such Ring Pairs for all Ring Bundles except one (i.e., except for the Ring
4620 Pair that would be used in following steps) should be disabled, such that only one Ring Bundle’s
4621 Command/Response Ring Pair is both ENABLED and RUNNING. The Host Controller should also
4622 consume any enqueued Response Descriptors from such enabled Response Rings.
4623 B. For PIO Mode: The Host Controller should reset or empty the Command Queue, or allow it to
4624 drain to an empty state. The Host Controller should also consume any outstanding Response
4625 Descriptors along with any associated Rx Data from the Rx Data Buffer (per Section 6.8.1) until
4626 all such PIO Queues are empty.
4627 C. If the Host Controller supports Scheduled Commands (per Section 6.16), then this capability
4628 should be disabled to prevent any interruptions.
4629 D. If the Host Controller supports any other implementer-defined capability that could cause
4630 interrupts to the processing of I3C commands, if it were to be enabled, then such capability should
4631 also be disabled.
4632 Once all of these conditions are true, and as long as they remain true, the Driver may write a value of 1'b0
4633 to field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT. This signals readiness to transition into Standby Controller mode and
4634 allows the Driver to subsequently send the special Command Descriptor (per Section 6.17.2.2) that sends
4635 the GETACCCR CCC and initiates the Controller-to-Controller Handoff Procedure.

6.17.2.2 Sending the GETACCCR CCC and Initiating the Controller Role Handoff
Procedure
4647 In Active Controller mode, a value of 1'b0 read from field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT indicates that the Host
4648 Controller is ready to accept the special Command Descriptor on the Queue/Ring, which would send the
4649 GETACCCR CCC to the chosen Secondary Controller Device.
4650 To send the GETACCCR CCC and initiate the Controller Role Handoff Procedure, the Driver shall
4651 construct the Internal Control Command using the appropriate sub-command type as defined in
4652 Section 8.4.2.7, and then enqueue the Command Descriptor to the active Command Queue/Ring for
4653 processing.
4654 As noted in Section 6.17.2.1, the Host Controller shall only accept this special Command Descriptor while
4655 in this transitional state, and it shall not accept any other types of Command Descriptors (i.e., any other
4656 Transfer Commands).
4657 If the Driver enqueues this special Command Descriptor while the Host Controller is not in this transitional
4658 state, then the Host Controller shall reject the Command Descriptor as an error, and shall generate a
4659 Response Descriptor with the value 0xA (NOT_SUPPORTED) in field ERR_STATUS (per Table 143).
4660 If the Host Controller receives any other type of Command Descriptor while in this transitional state, then it
4661 shall reject the Command Descriptor as an error, and shall generate a Response Descriptor with the value
4662 0x8 (HC_TERMINATED) in field ERR_STATUS (per Table 143). The Host Controller shall also leave the
4663 transitional state, and field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT shall have a value of 1'b1.
4664 The Driver shall prepare such a Command Descriptor, and either:
4665 • For PIO Mode: Write the Command Descriptor into the Command Queue Port; or
4666 • For DMA Mode: Construct a Transfer Descriptor for the Command Descriptor, and enqueue it into the
4667 Ring Bundle that will be used for the transition. (In most cases, this will typically be the sole remaining
4668 Ring Bundle that is both ENABLED and RUNNING.)
4669 Once the Host Controller receives this special Command Descriptor, it shall ensure that the necessary
4670 conditions were met, and that the Host Controller is in the transitional state. If the conditions are met and
4671 the transitional state is still in effect, then the Host Controller shall latch the current value of field
4672 PRIME_ACCEPT_GETACCCR in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1). The latched value shall be
4673 used to determine whether the I3C Secondary Controller Logic will automatically be primed to accept the
4674 Controller Role after successfully transitioning to Standby Controller mode.
4675 • If field PRIME_ACCEPT_GETACCCR was set to 1'b0 when the Host Controller accepted the special
4676 Command Descriptor, then:
4677 • The Host Controller shall not prime the Secondary Controller Logic to automatically accept the
4678 Controller Role from the Active Controller after a successful transition to Standby Controller mode.
4679 • The Host Controller shall notify the Host upon successful transition, with an interrupt of type
4680 ACR_HANDOFF_OK_REMAIN_STAT.
4681 • However, the Driver may subsequently write a value of 1'b1 to field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT (per
4682 Section 6.17.4) after receiving notification of a successful transition.
4683 • If field PRIME_ACCEPT_GETACCCR was set to 1'b1 when the Host Controller accepted the special
4684 Command Descriptor, then:
4685 • The Host Controller shall prime the Secondary Controller Logic to automatically accept the Controller
4686 Role from the Active Controller (i.e., if the Active Controller sends the GETACCCR CCC to this Host
4687 Controller’s Dynamic Address).
4688 • This shall take effect only upon a successful transition into Standby Controller mode that is not
4689 otherwise cancelled (i.e., if the Secondary Controller Logic initiates an automatic return to Active
4690 Controller mode, due to an Error Type CE3 failure).
4691 • The Host Controller shall notify the Host upon successful transition, with an interrupt of type
4692 ACR_HANDOFF_OK_PRIMED_STAT to indicate that the Secondary Controller Logic is primed.

4693 • After this interrupt notification, field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT shall have a value of 1'b1 (i.e., as though
4694 the Driver had written a value of 1'b1 to field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT upon notification of successful
4695 transition). The Driver may subsequently revoke readiness (i.e., by writing a value of 1'b0 per
4696 Section 6.17.4) if this field is writeable while the Host Controller is operating in Standby Controller
4697 mode.
4698 After the Host Controller latches the primed state and finishes all preliminary checks, it shall prepare the
4699 Secondary Controller Logic for activation, and also drive the Bus Controller Logic to send the GETACCCR
4700 CCC to the chosen Secondary Controller Device using the Dynamic Address specified in the special
4701 Command Descriptor.
4702 Note:
4703 If the Host Controller rejects the Command Descriptor due to incorrect format, then field
4704 ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT shall revert to the value 1'b1. Before sending a subsequent Command
4705 Descriptor for the GETACCCR CCC, the software must first set this bit to 1'b0 again. However, field
4706 ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT shall not revert to the value 1'b1 as a result of the Host Controller rejecting
4707 a Command Descriptor for other reasons (i.e., necessary pre-Handoff conditions not being true).
4708 Because the Bus Controller Logic drives the GETACCCR CCC and manages the Controller-to-Controller
4709 Handoff Procedure, it shall monitor the I3C Bus to determine whether the Handoff is successful. The status
4710 of the Handoff Procedure shall be returned in the Response Descriptor.
4711 • If the chosen Secondary Controller does not ACK its Dynamic Address (i.e., passive NACK) during the
4712 Direct CCC framing, then the GETACCCR CCC will fail per the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at
4713 Section 5.1.9.3.16, Figure 63 (GETACCCR Format 2: Not Accepted).
4714 • If this occurs, then the Bus Controller Logic shall cancel the CCC by sending a Repeated START,
4715 followed by the I3C Broadcast Address, etc. The Response Descriptor would indicate this result with
4716 the value 0x5 (NACK) in field ERR_STATUS.
4717 • If the chosen Secondary Controller does ACK its Dynamic Address during the Direct CCC framing, but
4718 the Bus Controller Logic detects an incorrect response on the SDA Line for the returned Dynamic
4719 Address and Parity Bit, then the GETACCCR CCC must fail per the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at
4720 Section 5.1.9.3.16, Figure 64 (GETACCCR Format 3: Incorrect Cancel).
4721 • If this occurs, then the Bus Controller Logic shall cancel the CCC by sending a Repeated START,
4722 followed by the I3C Broadcast Address, etc. The specific status in the Response Descriptor shall
4723 depend on the mode of failure, based on the response on the SDA Line:
4724 • If the I3C Bus Controller Logic reads the correct Dynamic Address with an incorrect Parity Bit, then
4725 the Response Descriptor shall indicate this result with the value 0xC (Transfer Type Specific:
4726 GETACCCR_PARITY) in field ERR_STATUS.
4727 • If the I3C Bus Controller Logic reads an incorrect Dynamic Address (which might be caused by
4728 interference on the SDA Lane), then the Response Descriptor shall indicate this result with the value
4729 0xD (Transfer Type Specific: GETACCCR_DYNADDR) in field ERR_STATUS.
4730 • These error codes are defined in Section 6.13.1 and Table 143.
4731 • If the chosen Secondary Controller does ACK its Dynamic Address during the Direct CCC framing, and
4732 if the Bus Controller Logic detects a correct response on the SDA Line for the returned Dynamic Address
4733 and Parity Bit, then the GETACCCR CCC will be successful per the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at
4734 Section 5.1.9.3.16, Figure 62 (GETACCCR Format 1: Accepted).
4735 In this case, the I3C Bus Controller Logic shall drive a STOP condition at the end of the CCC, and
4736 follow with the Controller-to-Controller Handoff Procedure per the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at
4737 Section 5.1.7.2, as well as a test for Error Type CE3. The Response Descriptor shall indicate this
4738 result with the value 0x0 (SUCCESS) in field ERR_STATUS.
4739 If the transaction is successful, then software shall read the Response Descriptor as the last action in Active
4740 Controller mode. If the transaction is not successful, then field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT shall keep its value
4741 of 1'b0, and software may either leave it at this value (i.e., remaining in the transitional state, and possibly
4742 enqueuing another special Command Descriptor to try sending GETACCCR CCC again), or else write a

4746 Once the GETACCCR CCC is sent successfully and the Controller Role has been passed (which should
4747 occur on the subsequent STOP condition on the I3C Bus), the Bus Controller Logic shall stop driving the
4748 SCL clock, and the Secondary Controller Logic shall await either incoming requests or assertions of the
4749 Controller Role from the new Active Controller.
4750 After attempting to pass the Controller Role, the Host Controller shall report successful transitions or failed
4751 transition attempts from Active Controller mode to Standby Controller mode by triggering one or more of
4752 the interrupt events listed in Table 9 in register STBY_CR_INTR_STATUS (Section 7.7.11.7).

Interrupt Event Description

4754 Note:
4755 The interrupt events in Table 9 describe attempted transitions from Active Controller mode into
4756 Standby Controller mode. By contrast, the interrupt events in Table 10 describe attempted
4757 transitions in the other direction (i.e., from Standby Controller mode into Active Controller mode).
4758 In cases where a single Controller Role Handoff Procedure is quickly followed by another transition
4759 back into Active Controller Mode (i.e., if the Secondary Controller Logic was primed to accept the
4760 Controller Role and the new Active Controller subsequently passed the Controller Role back after it
4761 completed its tasks), software should expect to see at least one interrupt event from both Table 9
4762 and Table 10: one successful transition event for each direction. Depending on system interrupt
4763 latency and the timing of the two Controller Role Handoff Procedures on the I3C Bus, both such
4764 interrupt events might arrive within a very short time interval, and it’s possible that the software
4765 might read these events with a single read of register STBY_CR_INTR_STATUS, with no detectable
4766 change in the value of field AC_CURRENT_OWN between the two interrupt events.
4767 If interrupts ACR_HANDOFF_OK_REMAIN_STAT and ACR_HANDOFF_ERR_M3_STAT were both
4768 triggered, then that indicates that the Host Controller attempted to pass the Controller Role and
4769 remain in Standby Controller mode (i.e., with Secondary Controller Logic not in primed’ state per
4770 Section 6.17.4), but the Secondary Controller Logic subsequently detected an Error Type CE3
4771 condition after Handoff and was forced to return the Host Controller to Active Controller mode.
4772 If interrupts ACR_HANDOFF_OK_PRIMED_STAT and ACR_HANDOFF_ERR_M3_STAT were both
4773 triggered, then that indicates that the Host Controller attempted to pass the Controller Role and
4774 remain ready to accept the Controller Role (i.e., with Secondary Controller Logic in primed state per
4775 Section 6.17.4), but the Secondary Controller Logic subsequently detected an Error Type CE3
4776 condition after Handoff and was forced to return the Host Controller to Active Controller mode.
4777 Both of these situations should typically be considered errors (or exceptions to the standard flow),
4778 because the intended new Active Controller did not assert its Controller Role status, or failed to
4779 respond to a START Request in a timely manner. Note that in such situations the Response
4780 Descriptor for the special Command Descriptor will return a value of 0x0 in field ERR_STATUS
4781 because it only reports the initially successful handoff, not the subsequent Error Type CE3
4782 condition.
4783 The Driver should also watch for the transition status bus monitoring bit, AC_CURRENT_OWN, to change to
4784 1'b0. But an interrupt notification is the definitive method of determining whether a transition was
4785 successful or not successful, and (in some cases) whether it was also accompanied by a subsequent
4786 transition back into Active Controller mode.
4787 The transition shall trigger an interrupt notification to report the status:
4788 • An interrupt notification of either type ACR_HANDOFF_OK_PRIMED_STAT or type
4789 ACR_HANDOFF_OK_REMAIN_STAT signals that the Host Controller is now operating in Standby
4790 Controller mode, or was initially and transiently in that state:
4791 • If an interrupt notification of type ACR_HANDOFF_ERR_M3_STAT is also triggered, then this signals that
4792 the Host Controller was forced to return to Active Controller mode (see below).
4793 • However, if no interrupt notification of type ACR_HANDOFF_ERR_M3_STAT is triggered, and if the new
4794 Active Controller has asserted its Controller Role, then the Host Controller shall remain in Standby
4795 Controller mode per Section 6.17.3 (i.e., no Error Type CE3 condition is detected); and may also
4796 conditionally remain ready to accept the Controller Role per Section 6.17.4. The new Active Controller
4797 may subsequently attempt to pass back the Controller Role, at its discretion.
4798 • An interrupt notification of type ACR_HANDOFF_ERR_FAIL_STAT signals that the Controller Role
4799 Handoff Procedure was not successful (as noted in Table 9) and the Host Controller is still operating in
4800 Active Controller mode.
4801 In this case, the Host Controller would still be in the transitional state, and the AC_CURRENT_OWN
4802 bit would read as 1'b0. The Driver should read this status, attempt to determine why the Controller
4803 Role Handoff Procedure was not successful, and optionally initiate another attempt to send the
4804 GETACCCR CCC.

4805 • An interrupt notification of type ACR_HANDOFF_ERR_M3_STAT signals an error: the Secondary
4806 Controller Logic detected an Error Type CE3 condition per Section 5.1.10.2.4 of the I3C Specification
4807 [MIPI02].
4808 In this case, the Host Controller would have automatically returned to Active Controller mode and
4809 the AC_CURRENT_OWN bitfield in register STBY_CUR_STATUS (Section 7.7.11.4) would read as 1'b1.
4810 The Driver should read this status, then run an error recovery procedure to determine why the

4818 this by subsequently reading the register to verify that the value 1'b1 is read.) After writing this 1'b1,
4819 software may send regular Command Descriptors, but software shall not send the special
4820 Command Descriptor for the GETACCCR CCC.
