6.17.3 Operation in Standby Controller Mode
4825 In Standby Controller mode, the Host Controller supports a limited set of features and capabilities that are
4826 appropriate for the Secondary Controller role on the I3C Bus.
4827 The following features and capabilities are required, and shall be supported if Standby Controller mode is
4828 supported:
4829 • Secondary Controller Logic may receive the Controller Role from the Active Controller, subject to
4830 readiness conditions defined in Section 6.17.4.
4831 • Secondary Controller Logic may autonomously service certain standard CCCs sent by the Active
4832 Controller, per Section 6.17.3.1.
4833 Note:
4834 A Host Controller that only implements the Minimal Standby Controller definition in
4835 Section 6.17 is required to support the features and capabilities specified above. Such
4836 minimum requirements allow the Host Controller to receive the Controller Role from the Active
4837 Controller, as well as to comply with the essential requirements of the I3C Specification.
4838 The following features and capabilities are optional, and may be supported at the implementer’s discretion:
4839 • Support for generic Read-Type and Write-Type transactions sent by the Active Controller via an I3C
4840 Target Transaction Interface available to software, including support for CCCs that are not supported
4841 natively within the Secondary Controller Logic.
4842 • Support for sending Controller Role Requests, for the purpose of requesting or attempting to regain the
4843 Controller Role from the Active Controller, per Section 6.17.3.3.
4844 If implemented, then all such features and capabilities are part of the I3C Secondary Controller Logic, and
4845 shall be enabled in Standby Controller mode (i.e., if field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register
4846 STBY_CR_CONTROL has a non-zero value, see Section 7.7.8.1), if the Host Controller was initialized per the
4847 initialization steps defined in sub-sections of Section 6.17.1, specifically:
4848 • If initialized as a Secondary Controller on the I3C Bus, or
4849 • If initialized as an Active Controller (i.e., the Primary Controller of the I3C Bus) that subsequently
4850 passed the Controller Role to another Secondary Controller Device and became a Secondary Controller
4851 on the I3C Bus.
4852 A Host Controller may also support generic Read-Type and Write-Type transactions, via an I3C Target
4853 Transaction Interface to software as a separate capability that is linked with Standby Controller mode. If
4854 this Host Controller supports an I3C Target Transaction Interface for the I3C Secondary Controller Logic,
4855 then field TARGET_XACT_SUPPORT in register STBY_CR_CAPABILITIES (Section 7.7.11.3) shall have a
4856 value of 1'b1, and this interface shall be available for use by software. The Driver may choose to either
4857 enable this interface, or not enable it. To enable the I3C Target Transaction Interface, the Driver shall write
4858 a value of 1'b1 to field TARGET_XACT_ENABLE in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.8.1).
4859 Since the I3C Target Transaction Interface is not defined in this version of the I3C HCI Specification, it
4860 may be implemented as vendor-defined functionality, exposed via vendor-specific Extended Capabilties
4861 structures (per Section 7.3.2).
4862 Note:
4863 If an I3C Target Transaction Interface is supported, then it may be enabled or disabled only while
4864 field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL has a value of 2'b00.
4865 Autonomous servicing of standard CCCs that are required for Secondary Controller operation (per
4866 Section 6.17.3.1) shall not depend on whether the I3C Target Transaction Interface is enabled or
4867 disabled; these capabilities are independently configured.

6.17.3.1 Servicing CCCs Autonomously
4868 In Standby Controller mode, the Host Controller’s Secondary Controller Logic shall autonomously service
4869 certain Broadcast CCCs that are addressed to the I3C Bus, and certain Direct CCCs that are targeted to the
4870 Dynamic Address assigned to the Secondary Controller Logic.
4871 The Secondary Controller Logic shall autonomously service CCC (i.e., shall receive data and shall provide
4872 auto-response), and the specific support for these CCCs may be exposed or configured via certain registers
4873 in the Extended Capability structure for Standby Controller mode (Section 7.7.11).
4874 The implementer may choose which CCCs are supported, based on the use case; however, the minimum set
4875 of required CCCs specified in Section 6.17.3.1.1 must always be supported. A Host Controller
4876 implementation may also support additional standard CCCs (per Section 6.17.3.1.1), as well as other
4877 standard CCCs that might be supported either by extensions to the Secondary Controller Logic (per
4878 Section 6.17.3.1.2), or by interaction with the software via the I3C Target Transaction Interface, if that is
4879 also supported and enabled (per Section 6.17.3.1.3). This allows advanced configurability for vendor-
4880 defined CCCs, at the discretion of the implementer and with assistance from software that might be
4881 developed to support such vendor-defined CCCs, according to a custom content protocol.
4882 For Direct CCCs
4883 The Secondary Controller Logic shall track the CCC modality for the I3C Mode, and shall respond only to
4884 CCCs that it does support internally (i.e., either standard or via extensions), or that it has been programmed
4885 to respond to via an I3C Target Transaction Interface (if supported and enabled).
4886 For Direct CCCs that the Secondary Controller Logic does not support, or has not been programmed to
4887 respond to, the Secondary Controller Logic shall not acknowledge its address (i.e., equivalent to passive
4888 NACK in SDR Mode). If the Host Controller supports an I3C Target Transaction Interface to software, and
4889 if this interface is also enabled, then the Secondary Controller Logic shall pass notification of that Direct
4890 CCC to the Target Transaction Interface for handling. Otherwise, the Host Controller shall report this as an
4891 unhandled Direct CCC by reporting the CCC_UNHANDLED_NACK_STAT interrupt condition to the Driver.
4892 For Broadcast CCCs
4893 The Secondary Controller Logic shall track the CCC modality for the I3C Mode, and shall only capture and
4894 act on the Broadcast data messages for those CCCs that it supports internally. If the Host Controller
4895 supports the I3C Target Transaction Interface to software, and if this interface is also enabled, then any
4896 other Broadcast CCCs shall be forwarded to this Target Transaction Interface. Otherwise, any other
4897 Broadcast CCCs shall be discarded without notification.
4898 However, the RSTDAA CCC is a special case: if the Secondary Controller Logic does not support the
4899 RSTDAA CCC (i.e., because it does not support any of the CCCs used for Dynamic Address Assignment),
4900 then it shall treat this Broadcast CCC as a fatal error if it receives such a CCC from the Active Controller of
4901 the I3C Bus. Such a condition typically applies to a Host Controller implementation that closely aligns with
4902 configuration Option 1 or Option 2 (per Section 6.17.1); and does not support configuration Option 3,
4903 where the Host Controller joins the I3C Bus as a Secondary Controller and typically receives a Dynamic
4904 Address from another Controller-capable Device on the I3C Bus. However, in most cases the Secondary
4905 Controller Logic should support the RSTDAA CCC.
4906 Note:
4907 If the RSTDAA CCC is received but the Secondary Controller cannot successfully handle it (i.e.,
4908 because it does not support Dynamic Address Assignment) then the Host Controller shall report
4909 this situation as an error by reporting the CCC_FATAL_RSTDAA_ERR_STAT interrupt condition, to
4910 signal that the Host Controller cannot continue to operate without intervention from the Driver.

6.17.3.1.1 CCCs Serviced by Standard Secondary Controller Logic
4911 The standard Secondary Controller Logic shall support autonomous response to the following CCCs:
4912 Minimum Required CCCs for Standby Controller Mode:
4913 • GETACCCR (see Section 6.17.4).
4914 Readiness to accept the GETACCCR CCC is determined by the value of field
4915 ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1), and by
4916 additional logic within the Host Controller that determines readiness to accept this CCC
4917 and participate in the Controller Role Handoff Procedure (see Section 6.17.4).
4918 • GETSTATUS Format 1 (i.e., without a Defining Byte), and Format 2 with Defining Byte value PRECR
4919 (i.e., 0x91) shall be supported.
4920 A minimal Standby Controller implementation shall support this CCC, and shall either:
4921 (A) Omit any configuration register that would allow the Driver to provide custom values
4922 for the CCC response data (in this case, responses shall use appropriate values for
4923 mandatory fields); or
4924 (B) Implement a vendor-defined configuration register (i.e., in Extended Capabilities)
4925 that allows the Driver to provide custom values for the CCC response data (in this case,
4926 responses shall use values from this register’s fields).
4927 • GETCAPS
4928 These CCCs shall be handled automatically via register
4929 STBY_CR_CCC_CONFIG_GETCAPS (Section 7.7.11.10), and the responses shall indicate
4930 the capabilities of the Secondary Controller Logic. Since the Secondary Controller Logic
4931 (as defined in this I3C HCI Specification) only supports a subset of the possible I3C
4932 Target role’s capabilities, this register only exposes the capabilities that are supported.
4933 • ENEC and DISEC
4934 A minimal Standby Controller implementation shall support the ENEC and DISEC CCCs,
4935 with the ENCR and DISCR bits. However, a configuration register is not required for this
4936 use case.
4937 Note that support for additional event notification bits that are defined for these CCCs
4938 may be added at the discretion of the implementer, via Extended Capabilities.
4939 The Secondary Controller Logic may also support autonomous response to the following CCCs:

4940 Optional CCCs for Standby Controller Mode:
4941 • ENTDAA, RSTDAA, SETDASA, SETAASA, and SETNEWDA
4942 These CCCs shall be handled automatically via register STBY_CR_DEVICE_ADDR
4943 (Section 7.7.11.2). For the ENTDAA CCC, see also registers STBY_CR_DEVICE_CHAR
4944 (Section 7.7.11.5) and STBY_CR_DEVICE_PID_LO (Section 7.7.11.6).
4945 Note that Standby Controller support for each of the Dynamic Address Assignment CCCs
4946 (ENTDAA, SETDASA, and SETAASA) can be enabled or disabled by a bitfield in register
4947 STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1): DAA_ENTDAA_ENABLE, DAA_SETDASA_ENABLE,
4948 and DAA_SETAASA_ENABLE, respectively. The Driver shall enable or disable response for
4949 each of these CCCs, based on methods that might be implemented and supported in
4950 corresponding fields in register STBY_CR_CAPABILITIES (Section 7.7.11.3).
4951 • GETPID, GETBCR, and GETDCR
4952 These shall be handled automatically via registers STBY_CR_DEVICE_CHAR
4953 (Section 7.7.11.5) and STBY_CR_DEVICE_PID_LO (Section 7.7.11.6).
4954 Note that support for some or all of these CCCs shall be conditionally required,
4955 depending on which CCCs for Dynamic Address Assignment are also supported. For
4956 example, if the ENTDAA CCC is supported, then all of these CCCs must also be
4957 supported.
4958 • RSTACT
4959 These CCCs shall be handled automatically via register
4960 STBY_CR_CCC_CONFIG_RSTACT_PARAMS (Section 7.7.11.11).
4961 Additionally, the Secondary Controller Logic shall handle defined Target Reset action
4962 flows with the RSTACT CCC followed by the Target Reset Pattern, according to the
4963 configuration of registers STBY_CR_CCC_CONFIG_RSTACT_PARAMS and
4964 STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1). If the Active Controller sends a Target Reset
4965 action to reset the Secondary Controller Logic, then the Host Controller shall, at the
4966 discretion of the implementer, either assert interrupt STBY_CR_OP_RSTACT_STAT
4967 (Section 7.7.11.7), or else reset the Host Controller internally.
4968 • DEFTGTS and DEFGRPA
4969 These Broadcast CCCs shall be handled automatically and enqueued as Read data into
4970 the IBI Queue/Ring (see Section 6.17.3.2).
6.17.3.1.2 CCCs Serviced by Extensions to Secondary Controller Logic
4971 The Host Controller’s Secondary Controller Logic may support additional CCCs that are defined in the I3C
4972 Specification, implemented as standard extensions to Secondary Controller Logic that might be required for
4973 certain use cases or optional features of an I3C Device. Such extensions shall be exposed as instances of a
4974 vendor-specific Extended Capability structure that might be defined to control such CCC handling.
6.17.3.1.3 CCCs Serviced by Other Mechanisms
4975 Any CCCs (either Direct or Broadcast) that are not serviced autonomously by the Secondary Controller
4976 Logic shall either be treated as variants of either Read-Type or Write-Type transactions, and would
4977 typically be handled by software via the I3C Target Transaction Interface, or else treated as extensions to
4978 the Secondary Controller Logic that support autonomous handling of custom CCCs, with configuration
4979 registers exposed via one or more instances of a vendor-defined Extended Capability structure indicating
4980 custom CCC handling.

6.17.3.1.4 Implications for Minimal Standby Controller Use Case (Informative)
4981 In addition to Section 6.17.3.1.1’s list of CCCs that a minimal Standby Controller implementation is
4982 required to support, it is expected that such a minimal implementation will usually be the Active Controller
4983 of the I3C Bus, and will be responsible for most Bus Configuration functions. For many such use cases,
4984 such minimal Host Controllers are typically paired with other limited-function Secondary Controller
4985 Devices that are expected to only perform limited tasks while serving as the Active Controller, and only to
4986 hold the Controller Role for a limited time.
4987 Such other Secondary Controller Devices would be expected to support only the minimum I3C Bus
4988 Management procedures while acting as Active Controller (see the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at
4989 Section 5.1.7.3.2), and to not attempt to perform additional Bus Configuration procedures while acting as
4990 Active Controller. Since the Host Controller would only support the minimal Standby Controller mode
4991 functions and capabilities, and would only pass the Controller Role to such Secondary Controller Devices
4992 for a limited duration and purpose, this system configuration should present few integration issues for the
4993 Host Controller.
4994 It is also clear that such limited-purpose Secondary Controller Devices should typically pass the Controller
4995 Role back to the Host Controller when finished with the task for which the Controller Role was initially
4996 transferred. Additionally, such Secondary Controller Devices should support sending the Controller Role
4997 Request to initiate the process of handing the Controller Role back to the Host Controller (see
4998 Section 6.17.3.3). The I3C Specification recommends that such Secondary Controller Devices should
4999 advertise such capabilities using the GETCAPS Format 2 CCC with Defining Byte value CRCAPS (i.e.,
5000 0x91), which includes a field for the automatic pass-back capability (see the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at
5001 Section 5.1.9.3.19).
5002 However, if a more fully-featured Secondary Controller Device were to be paired with a minimal Standby
5003 Controller implementation of a Host Controller, then issues could arise due to a mismatch of expectations.
5004 Several error scenarios are possible:
5005 • The Secondary Controller Device attempting to perform Bus Configuration procedures, which the Host
5006 Controller would not be able to successfully track or understand due to its minimal capabilities.
5007 • The Secondary Controller Device attempting to send certain CCCs or other Private Read/Write
5008 transactions to the Host Controller, with the expectation of a particular response that would not be
5009 possible due to the Host Controller’s limited capabilities, or its lack of support for other CCCs.
5010 • The Secondary Controller Device attempting to assign a new Dynamic Address to the Host Controller,
5011 or to reset all Dynamic Addresses on the Bus via the RSTDAA CCC, which the Host Controller would
5012 not support (and might cause a fatal error, per Section 6.17.3.1).
5013 System designers should ensure that minimal Standby Controller implementations of Host Controllers are
5014 used for system integrations where other Secondary Controller Devices have carefully prescribed roles and
5015 capabilities, and where such other Devices will be known (or configured) to not exceed the boundaries of
5016 what the minimal Host Controller can support in Standby Controller mode. For use cases where that is not
5017 possible or where those limits cannot be ensured, a more fully-featured Host Controller with Standby
5018 Controller mode support is strongly recommended.
6.17.3.2 Receiving Broadcast DEFTGTS and DEFGRPA CCCs
5019 A Host Controller that supports Standby Controller mode shall monitor the I3C Bus for specific Broadcast
5020 CCCs relating to transferring Bus configuration (i.e., DEFTGTS and DEFGRPA) that can be sent by the
5021 Active Controller. The Secondary Controller Logic shall receive such Broadcast CCCs while enabled (i.e.,
5022 while field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL has a value of 2'b10, per
5023 Section 7.7.11.1).

5024 Note:
5025 If field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL does not have a value of 2'b10, then
5026 either the Secondary Controller Logic is disabled, or it will not receive and capture Broadcast
5027 CCCs.
5028 Any time the Active Controller sends either of these Broadcast CCCs (i.e., DEFTGTS or DEFGRPA), the
5029 Secondary Controller Logic shall capture each CCC and its subsequent data bytes, and make them available
5030 in the active IBI Data Queue or IBI Ring Pair, depending on the current operating mode:
5031 • In PIO Mode: The active IBI Data Queue is accessed via register IBI_PORT (Section 7.5.4).
5032 • The Secondary Controller Logic shall make the Broadcast CCC data available as a sequence of one or
5033 more IBI Status Descriptors, with each followed by IBI Data DWORDs according to the standard IBI
5034 handling defined in Section 6.9.1. The first IBI Data DWORD after the first such IBI Status Descriptor
5035 shall contain the Broadcast Address (7'h7E) in the first byte, the Command Code in the second byte,
5036 and subsequent bytes afterwards.
5037 • As necessary, the Secondary Controller Logic shall flow the data into multiple reports, each with its
5038 own IBI Status Descriptor, per the threshold setting in field IBI_DATA_SEGMENT_SIZE in register
5039 QUEUE_THLD_CTRL (Section 7.5.5). Field LAST_STATUS shall be set to 1'b0 for every IBI Status
5040 Descriptor except the last IBI Status Descriptor, where field LAST_STATUS shall be set to 1'b1 (i.e.,
5041 similar to a regular IBI with a split payload).
5042 • IN DMA Mode: The active IBI Ring Pair used is selected by field BCAST_CCC_IBI_RING in register
5043 STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1).
5044 • The selected Ring Bundle must be enabled and configured for use, and its IBI Ring Pair must also be
5045 initialized and ready to receive data per Section 6.6.1.
5046 • The Secondary Controller Logic shall make the Broadcast CCC data available as a sequence of one or
5047 more IBI Status Descriptors in the IBI Status Ring, with appropriately allocated chunks of data in the
5048 IBI Data Ring per Section 6.6.3. The first IBI Data DWORD shall contain the Broadcast Address
5049 (7'h7E) in the first byte, the Command Code in the second byte, and subsequent bytes afterwards.
5050 • As necessary, the Secondary Controller Logic shall flow the data into multiple reports, each with its
5051 own IBI Status Descriptor and set of Data Chunks, per the value of field CHUNK_SIZE in register
5052 IBI_SETUP (see Section 7.6.10.2). Field LAST_STATUS shall be set to 1'b0 for every IBI Status
5053 Descriptor except the last IBI Status Descriptor, where field LAST_STATUS shall be set to 1'b1 (i.e.,
5054 similar to a regular IBI with a split payload).
5055 Each IBI Status Descriptor for Broadcast CCC data shall have field STATUS_TYPE set to 3'b111 to
5056 distinguish it from other IBI Status Descriptor uses (see Section 8.6.7).

6.17.3.3 Simple Controller Role Request
5071 A Host Controller that supports the Minimal Standby Controller capabilities should also support the simple
5072 method of sending a Controller Role Request to the Active Controller of the I3C Bus defined in this
5073 section. This method involves reading from and writing to specific fields in the registers defined in
5074 Section 7.7.11. If the Host Controller supports this Simple Controller Role Request flow, then it shall
5075 indicate this capability with a value of 1'b1 in field SIMPLE_CRR_SUPPORT of register
5076 STBY_CR_CAPABILITIES (Section 7.7.11.3).
5077 Note:
5078 Although a Minimal Standby Controller (as defined in this I3C HCI Specification) is not required to
5079 support this flow, it is strongly recommended.
5080 The Controller Role Request shall be initiated when the Driver writes to field CR_REQUEST_SEND in
5081 register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1). Once the Driver writes a value of 1'b1 to this field, the
5082 Host Controller shall capture the request. After capturing the request, the Host Controller shall indicate the
5083 request status in field SIMPLE_CRR_STATUS in register STBY_CR_STATUS (see Section 7.7.11.4).
5084 Note:
5085 Field CR_REQUEST_SEND is a write-only bit. A pending Controller Role Request cannot be
5086 cancelled by the Driver, and the Host Controller shall only allow one pending request to be
5087 enqueued at a time. Writes to field CR_REQUEST_SEND shall have no effect if field
5088 SIMPLE_CRR_STATUS in register STBY_CR_STATUS currently has a value of 3'b001.
5089 The Secondary Controller Logic shall attempt to send the Controller Role Request at the earliest
5090 opportunity (i.e., after waiting for the I3C Bus to be idle for at least the Bus Available Condition, per the
5091 I3C Specification [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.3.2.2). The Driver may check on the status of the Controller
5092 Role Request by reading field SIMPLE_CRR_STATUS in register STBY_CR_STATUS (Section 7.7.11.4). The
5093 returned value indicates the status of the Secondary Controller Logic for this pending request, and should
5094 be used by the Driver to understand whether the Controller Role Request has been sent, and if so, whether
5095 the Active Controller ACKed or NACKed the Controller Role Request.
5096 When the Active Controller responds to this Controller Role Request, the Host Controller shall also trigger
5097 the CRR_RESPONSE_STAT interrupt in register STBY_CR_INTR_STATUS (Section 7.7.11.7). When this
5098 interrupt is triggered, field SIMPLE_CRR_STATUS shall have a valid value of 3'b010 or higher.
5099 Note:
5100 If a Controller Role Request was NACKed, then the Driver should use the value of field
5101 SIMPLE_CRR_STATUS to determine whether to send a subsequent Controller Role Request, for
5102 cases in which it is appropriate to do so. The Host Controller shall not prevent the Driver from
5103 sending subsequent Controller Role Requests after receiving a NACKed Controller Role Request,
5104 which might be followed by the DISEC CCC with the DISCR bit (i.e., the Active Controller disabling
5105 Controller Role Requests on the I3C Bus).
5106 Even if the Controller Role Request was ACKed, that is no guarantee that the Active Controller will
5107 always use the GETACCCR CCC to attempt to pass the Controller Role. The I3C Specification
5108 states that passing the Controller Role may happen either immediately, or at a later time.
5109 Additionally, the Active Controller might need to perform additional steps to synchronize this Host
5110 Controller’s Secondary Controller Logic with the current state of the I3C Bus and all known I3C
5111 Devices. In order to remain ready, the Host Controller should be primed to accept the Controller
5112 Role per Section 6.17.4 before the Driver sends the Controller Role Request.

6.17.4 Transition from Standby Controller Mode to Active Controller Mode
5113 In order to start the transition to Active Controller mode, the Host Controller in Standby Controller mode
5114 shall prepare the Secondary Controller Logic to accept the anticipated GETACCCR CCC from the Active
5115 Controller.
5116 The Host Controller becomes ready to accept the GETACCCR CCC according to the conditions below,
5117 using either of these two flows:
5118 • Direct Prime After Transition: If field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL
5119 (Section 7.7.11.1) was previously set to 1'b0, and the Driver subsequently writes the value 1'b1 to field
5120 ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT, then the Secondary Controller Logic shall become primed to accept the
5121 Controller Role.
5122 • Auto-Prime With Transition: The Secondary Controller Logic might have been previously primed to
5123 automatically accept the Controller Role upon transitioning into Standby Controller mode, if field
5124 PRIME_ACCEPT_GETACCCR was set to 1'b1 when the Host Controller accepted the special Command
5125 Descriptor in Active Controller Mode (per Section 6.17.2) and then successfully transitioned into
5126 Standby Controller mode.
5127 Note:
5128 The Driver may choose to initially follow the Auto Prime with Transition path, then write 1'b0 to field
5129 ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT to remove the primed status; and then subsequently write 1'b1 to field
5130 ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT to prime the Secondary Controller Logic again, at its discretion. However,
5131 for a limited-scope Host Controller (i.e., Minimal Secondary Controller) implementation, field
5132 ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT might not be writeable in Standby Controller mode.
5133 The Driver may explicitly request the Controller Role from the Active Controller by instructing the
5134 Secondary Controller Logic to send the Controller Role Request via the Simple Controller Role Request
5135 mechanism specified in Section 6.17.3.3. This may occur either before or after writing 1'b1 to field
5136 ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT; however, the typical flow expects the Secondary Controller Logic to be primed
5137 (i.e., ready to accept the GETACCCR CCC) before it sends the Controller Role Request.
5138 Note:
5139 Sending a Controller Role Request is not required to meet the conditions for readiness to accept
5140 the GETACCCR CCC. For certain use cases, the Active Controller might be configured to
5141 automatically send the GETACCCR CCC without having received a Controller Role Request. If a
5142 Controller Role Request is not sent, then the Secondary Controller Logic must wait until the Active
5143 Controller sends the GETACCCR CCC at its own discretion.
5144 If the Host Controller supports a Deep Sleep state for power management, then it shall automatically write
5145 a value of 1'b1 to field HANDOFF_DEEP_SLEEP in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1) to signal
5146 to the Active Controller that it might have missed important Broadcast messages (such as DEFTGTS and
5147 DEFGRPA CCCs) while in that state. This provides indication that the Active Controller should re-send Bus
5148 Configuration Broadcast CCCs, if such changes were recently made. Alternatively, software may choose to
5149 report the same Deep Sleep indication by writing to field HANDOFF_DEEP_SLEEP.
5150 The readiness to accept the GETACCCR CCC depends on several conditions, all of which must remain
5151 true:
5152 1. The Secondary Controller Logic has been initialized and configured as defined in Section 6.17.1.1.
5153 This includes setting field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL
5154 (Section 7.7.11.1) to a non-zero value. Note that this is supported for either initial role on
5155 the I3C Bus, so long as the Secondary Controller Logic is eventually enabled.
5156 2. The Bus Controller Logic has been configured.
5157 This includes setting field BUS_ENABLE in register HC_CONTROL (Section 7.4.2).
5158 3. The Host Controller has been configured with a valid Dynamic Address.

Public Release Edition

15-Feb-2023
5159 In register STBY_CR_DEVICE_ADDR (Section 7.7.11.2), field DYNAMIC_ADDR_VALID must
5160 be set to 1'b1 and field DYNAMIC_ADDR must be set to a Dynamic Address that is valid for
5161 an I3C Device.
5162 Note:
5163 If the Secondary Controller Logic receives a successful Target Reset action (i.e., RSTACT
5164 CCC followed by the Target Reset Pattern) that resets the Dynamic Address, as configured
5165 in register STBY_CR_CCC_CONFIG_RSTACT_PARAMS (Section 7.7.11.11), then the
5166 Secondary Controller Logic is required to revoke readiness to accept the Controller Role.
5167 4. The value 1'b1 has been written to field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL
5168 (Section 7.7.11.1) to signal readiness to accept the GETACCCR CCC.
5169 This sets the vector for the intended transition direction (i.e., the role that the Driver
5170 wishes the Host Controller to take). Software may read this register to verify that field
5171 ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT contains 1'b1.
5172 5. The Device has not received any incoming Broadcast DEFTGTS or DEFGRPA CCCs that have not yet
5173 been processed by software and had appropriate status cleared to indicate acceptance of the message
5174 data in these Broadcast CCCs.
5175 A. Field HANDOFF_DELAY_NACK in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1) indicates whether
5176 these Broadcast CCCs have been received by Secondary Controller Logic but not yet processed by
5177 software. Field HANDOFF_DELAY_NACK shall contain 1'b1 while that condition is false (i.e., is not
5178 met).
5179 • If the Secondary Controller Logic receives either of these Broadcast CCCs, then it shall
5180 automatically clear field HANDOFF_DEEP_SLEEP in register STBY_CR_CONTROL
5181 (Section 7.7.11.1) if that field was previously set, per Section 6.17.4.2.
5182 In this case, the Host Controller will capture the Broadcast CCC data and make
5183 it available to the Host via the active IBI Queue/Ring (per Section 6.17.3.2).
5184 • The Secondary Controller Logic shall not use the value of field HANDOFF_DEEP_SLEEP to
5185 determine whether to accept the Controller Role (i.e., the GETACCCR CCC).
5186 B. Software must clear this status by writing the value 1'b1 to field HANDOFF_DELAY_NACK (i.e.,
5187 write 1 to clear) in order to make this condition true. Software should not clear this condition until
5188 it has handled the Broadcast CCCs appropriately, per Section 6.17.4.1.
5189 • If the I3C Target Transaction Interface is supported and enabled, then software should verify
5190 that all received Request Descriptors for such Broadcast CCCs have been processed. Software
5191 might need to check this field again, in case the Active Controller subsequently sends any
5192 Broadcast DEFTGTS or DEFGRPA CCCs again.
5193 • If the I3C Target Transaction Interface is not supported or not enabled, then some other
5194 extended Secondary Controller Logic is required to handle the data messages in such
5195 Broadcast CCCs, and then clear this condition automatically (i.e., without software
5196 involvement).
5197 C. If the Active Controller repeatedly sends such Broadcast CCCs while software attempts to process
5198 them as they are received, then such activity might prevent this condition from remaining true, and
5199 this would hinder the Secondary Controller Logic from accepting the GETACCCR CCC. Note that
5200 the Host Controller in Standby Controller mode has no control over the Active Controller’s ability
5201 to continue sending such Broadcast CCCs.
5202 6. If an I3C Target Transaction Interface is supported and enabled, then the Device has not received any
5203 other incoming Write-Type transactions (either as Private Writes, Broadcast CCCs, or Direct CCCs)
5204 that have not yet been processed by software.
5205 A. This does not include the Broadcast DEFTGTS or DEFGRPA CCCs that are required to be
5206 captured by Secondary Controller Logic (as listed above, and in Section 6.17.3.2), although the
5207 method of handling them is similar. Field PENDING_RX_NACK in register STBY_CR_CONTROL
5208 (Section 7.7.11.1) indicates whether these transactions have been received by Secondary
5209 Controller Logic but not yet processed by software.

5210 B. Software must clear this status by writing the value 1'b1 to field PENDING_RX_NACK (i.e., write 1
5211 to clear) in order to make this condition true, per Section 6.17.4.1.
5212 Note:
5213 If an I3C Target Transaction Interface is not enabled (or is not supported), then such Write-Type
5214 transactions will not be received by software, and condition 6 above does not apply.
5215 Once all of the above conditions are true, for and as long as they remain true, the Secondary Controller
5216 Logic shall automatically accept the GETACCCR CCC once the Active Controller sends it, directed to this
5217 Host Controller’s Dynamic Address. If the Secondary Controller Logic accepts the GETACCCR CCC, then
5218 it shall return its own Dynamic Address and the correct Parity Bit at the appropriate time in the CCC
5219 framing (see the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.9.3.16).
5220 However, if any of the above conditions are not met, then the Secondary Controller Logic either will not
5221 receive the GETACCCR CCC (i.e., because it is not enabled), or else shall not accept the GETACCCR CCC,
5222 per Section 6.17.4.1.
5223 Note:
5224 Automatic acceptance of the GETACCCR CCC does not strictly require the I3C Target Transaction
5225 Interface to software for Read-Type or Write-Type transactions. However, successfully processing
5226 the Broadcast CCCs (such as DEFTGTS and DEFGRPA) requires either the I3C Target
5227 Transaction Interface to be supported and enabled, or an IBI Queue/Ring (per operating mode) to
5228 cache the data messages from such Broadcast CCCs and make them available to software, either
5229 before or after the transition to Active Controller mode.
5230 If the I3C Target Transaction Interface is supported and enabled, then such Broadcast CCCs shall
5231 appear as Write-Type transactions if sent by the Active Controller. Software should read these
5232 transactions according to the operating mode, and handle them in an appropriate manner.
5233 Following acceptance of the GETACCCR CCC, as indicated by the Active Controller driving the STOP
5234 condition, the Secondary Controller Logic shall participate in the Controller-to-Controller Handoff
5235 Procedure (see the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.7.2), activate the Bus Controller Logic (i.e.,
5236 enable SCL clock generation), and assert its Controller Role within the appropriate time, to prevent losing
5237 the Controller Role due to Error Type CE3 detection by the former Active Controller.
5238 If all of these events occur as indicated, then the Host Controller shall become the Active Controller of the
5239 I3C Bus, and shall transition into Active Controller mode. A successful transition shall trigger the
5240 STBY_CR_ACCEPT_OK_STAT interrupt, signaling that the Host Controller is now operating in Active
5241 Controller mode and that the Secondary Controller Logic is now idle.
5242 If there is an error during the GETACCCR CCC, or if the Active Controller does not indicate acceptance
5243 (i.e., by driving the STOP condition), then this shall trigger the STBY_CR_ACCEPT_ERR_STAT interrupt,
5244 signaling that the Host Controller is still operating in Standby Controller mode.
5245 As and when the Active Controller sends the GETACCCR CCC to this Host Controller’s Dynamic Address,
5246 and as the Secondary Controller Logic responds to that CCC, the Host Controller shall trigger one or more
5247 of the Table 10 interrupt events in register STBY_CR_INTR_STATUS (Section 7.7.11.7) to report successful
5248 transitions or failed transition attempts from Standby Controller mode to Active Controller mode.

5251 Note:
5252 The Table 10 interrupt events describe attempted transitions from Standby Controller mode to
5253 Active Controller mode. By contrast, the interrupt events in Table 9 describe attempted transitions
5254 from Active Controller mode to Standby Controller mode.
5255 If the interrupt event STBY_CR_ACCEPT_ERR_STAT is triggered for a failed or cancelled attempt,
5256 then this event shall not change the Secondary Controller Logic’s primed state, and the Secondary
5257 Controller Logic shall remain ready to accept any subsequent GETACCCR CCC that the Active
5258 Controller might send.
5259 If two or more of these interrupt events are triggered, then this reflects that the Active Controller has
5260 made multiple attempts to pass the Controller Role, and that these attempts ended in different
5261 outcomes. Since multiple events can be indicated by this register, if event
5262 STBY_CR_ACCEPT_OK_STAT plus any of the other events are triggered, and if field
5263 AC_CURRENT_OWN in register STBY_CR_STATUS contains the value 1'b1, then the successful
5264 transition was the most recent attempt, and the Host Controller has finally transitioned into Active
5265 Controller mode. To prevent past interrupt events from being confused with subsequent transitions
5266 to (and then from) Standby Controller mode, the software should clear any triggered interrupt
5267 events listed in Table 10 after it determines that the Host Controller has successfully transitioned
5268 into Active Controller mode.
5269 Software may monitor the transition status by reading field AC_CURRENT_OWN in register
5270 STBY_CR_STATUS (Section 7.7.11.4). If this field still contains the value 1'b0, then the Host Controller is
5271 still operating in Standby Controller mode. As long as a successful transition has not yet occurred, software
5272 may prevent a future transition (i.e., may revoke readiness to accept the GETACCCR CCC) by writing the
5273 value 1'b0 to field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1).

6.17.4.1  Conditions for Not Accepting the GETACCCR CCC
5277  If field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1) is set to 1'b0, and the
5278  Active Controller sends the GETACCCR CCC, then the Host Controller shall not accept (i.e., shall NACK)
5279  the CCC.
5280  This can happen under any or all of the following conditions:
5281  • The Host Controller enters Standby Controller mode, and was not initially primed to automatically accept
5282  the Controller Role (i.e., field PRIME_ACCEPT_GETACCCR was set to 1'b0);
5283  • The Host Controller initializes in Standby Controller mode with field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT set to 1'b0;
5284  or
• If field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT was set to 1'b1 when the Secondary Controller Logic was primed to accept
5285
5286  the Controller Role, but the Driver later wrote 1'b0 to the same field.
5287  Note:
5288  As noted in Section 6.17.4, these conditions are not completely exclusive: the current value of field
5289  ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT indicates whether the Secondary Controller Logic is primed to accept the
5290  Controller Role, and this status may be changed repeatedly by the Driver at its discretion.
The Secondary Controller Logic shall NACK the GETACCCR CCC if the Secondary Controller Logic
5291
5292  detects an attempt by the Active Controller to pass the Controller Role to the Host Controller while field
5293  ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT has a value of 1'b0; while field HANDOFF_DELAY_NACK has a value of 1'b1; or

5294 while field PENDING_RX_NACK has a value of 1'b1. In any of these events, the Host Controller shall also
5295 trigger the STBY_CR_ACCEPT_NACKED_STAT interrupt to signal that the Secondary Controller Logic did
5296 not accept the GETACCCR CCC that the Active Controller sent, and the Host Controller is still operating in
5297 Standby Controller mode.
5298 The Driver may subsequently process this interrupt, and it might decide to instruct the Secondary
5299 Controller Logic to accept any subsequent GETACCCR CCCs that the Active Controller might send, by
5300 priming the Secondary Controller Logic (if not already primed) and resolving any blocking conditions that
5301 prevented the NACK of this CCC. Alternately, the Driver may prime the Secondary Controller Logic at any
5302 time, and also resolve such blocking conditions proactively (i.e., in advance of receiving the interrupt) if it
5303 expects that the Active Controller might send the GETACCCR CCC.
5304 In either case, the Driver should take the following steps to resolve whatever blocking conditions might
5305 have arisen:
5306 • If field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT was previously set to 1'b0 (as mentioned above), then write a value of 1'b1
5307 to field ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT.
5308 • If the blocking condition indicated by field HANDOFF_DELAY_NACK with a value of 1'b1 was in effect,
5309 then first process all incoming Broadcast DEFTGTS or DEFGRPA CCCs per Section 6.17.4, and then
5310 write 1'b1 (i.e., write 1 to clear) to field HANDOFF_DELAY_NACK.
5311 • If the blocking condition indicated by field PENDING_RX_NACK with a value of 1'b1 was in effect, then
5312 first process or consume all other incoming Write-Type transactions per Section 6.17.4, and then write
5313 1'b1 (i.e., write 1 to clear) to field PENDING_RX_NACK.

6.17.4.2 Reporting Deep Sleep State Before Handoff
5315 As a part of preparing for the Controller Role Handoff Procedure, the Active Controller should check to see
5316 whether a Secondary Controller has reported that it has returned from a Deep Sleep state, and as a result
5317 might require resynchronization from the Active Controller (see the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at
5318 Section 5.1.7.1 and Section 5.1.9.3.15). The Active Controller can check for this status, using the
5319 GETSTATUS Format 2 CCC with Defining Byte value PRECR (i.e., 0x91).
5320 A Host Controller that supports Standby Controller mode shall allow the Deep Sleep state to be reported:
5321 either by the Driver, or based on internal logic (i.e., an automatic event triggered by power management
5322 state transitions, per Section 6.1.4.1). This state can be read or set (written) using field
5323 HANDOFF_DEEP_SLEEP in register STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1), subject to the following
5324 conditions:
5325 • The Host Controller shall automatically set field HANDOFF_DEEP_SLEEP to 1'b1 upon returning from any
5326 power management state in which there is a possibility that it could have missed any Bus Configuration
5327 activity (such as the Broadcast DEFTGTS and DEFGRPA CCCs) sent by the Active Controller.
5328 • The Driver may choose to set field HANDOFF_DEEP_SLEEP to 1'b1 to report this condition at any time.
5329 Regardless of the reason, setting field HANDOFF_DEEP_SLEEP to 1'b1 is ‘sticky’: the field shall remain set
5330 until any of the following occurs:
5331 • The Host Controller is reset; or
5332 • The Secondary Controller Logic receives at least one Broadcast DEFTGTS CCC (i.e., as the Active
5333 Controller attempts to resynchronize with the latest Bus Configuration data), which clears this field
5334 automatically; or
5335 • The Secondary Controller Logic accepts the GETACCCR CCC (per Section 6.17.4) and the Host
5336 Controller successfully transitions into Active Controller mode.
5337 The Secondary Controller Logic shall also use the current value of field HANDOFF_DEEP_SLEEP for
5338 automatic responses to the GETSTATUS Format 2 CCC with Defining Byte PRECR. For example, if field
5339 HANDOFF_DEEP_SLEEP contains 1'b1, then the Secondary Controller Logic shall populate Bit[0] of the
5340 LSB for the response of this CCC with 1'b1, indicating “Deep Sleep Detected” (see Section 5.1.9.3.15 of
5341 the I3C Specification [MIPI02]).
5342 Note:
5343 The Secondary Controller Logic shall automatically provide the LSB for the response to the
5344 GETSTATUS Format 2 CCC with Defining Byte PRECR. By default, the Secondary Controller Logic
5345 shall automatically provide a value of 0x00 for the MSB, because the MSB is reserved for vendor-
5346 specific use. If the implementer wishes to configure some other value to be provided for the vendor-
5347 specific MSB, then this can be configured using a vendor-specific register (i.e., via Extended
5348 Capabilities).
5349 The Active Controller shall determine whether this Host Controller (acting as a Secondary Controller)
5350 needs to be resynchronized. When determining whether to accept or refuse the Controller Role (i.e.,
5351 whether to ACK or NACK the GETACCCR CCC), the Secondary Controller shall not rely on seeing a
5352 value of 1'b1 in field HANDOFF_DEEP_SLEEP. Depending on the use case, it might be natural for the
5353 Secondary Controller Logic to accept the Controller Role after returning from Deep Sleep without
5354 resynchronization, as the Active Controller would have decided to send the GETACCCR CCC without
5355 sending any Bus Configuration CCCs (i.e., if no configuration changes needed to be transferred).
5356 Figure 40 illustrates the flow for rejecting (i.e., providing NACK for) the GETACCCR CCC due to lack of
5357 readiness.

6.18  Dead Bus Recovery
5358  The Host Controller may optionally support a Dead Bus Recovery Mechanism that allows the I3C Bus
5359  Controller Logic and optional I3C Secondary Controller Logic to either:
5360  • Recover from the Active Controller (i.e., another I3C Device) that might go unresponsive on the I3C Bus,
5361  and fail to transfer the Controller Role to this Host Controller;
• Connect to an existing I3C Bus and determine whether there is already an Active Controller that is
5362
5363  unresponsive (i.e., momentarily not ready to respond to a Hot-Join Request) or simply not present; or
5364  • Recover from either of situations above, by using the I3C defined Error Type DBR flow (per
Section 5.1.10.1.8 of the I3C Specification [MIPI02]) to take control (i.e., to claim the Controller Role)
5365
5366  of the I3C Bus.
5367  This mechanism provides additional tools to the Host system, in situations where the reliability and
5368  responsiveness of another Active Controller on the I3C Bus cannot be guaranteed, for use cases that rely on
5369  this Host system’s need to regain control of the I3C Bus in a well-defined manner, according to the Error
5370  Type DBR flow. This mechanism also interoperates with optional I3C Secondary Controller Logic for Host
5371  Controller implementations that also support Standby Controller mode and can initialize as either the
5372  Active Controller or a Secondary Controller (see Section 6.17.1).
5373  Figure 41 shows the high-level architecture of an I3C Host Controller subsystem that supports the Dead
5374  Bus Recovery Mechanism.

5379  • A mechanism that uses the optional I3C Error Type DBR flow for recovering an I3C Bus that does not

5381  • A limited START Request mechanism, which pulls SDA Low and uses a timer to test for SCL going

5383  • An optional IBI (In-Band Interrupt) Initiator with Address Arbitration mechanism, which drives a

5387  Controller) if no Active Controller is found to be both present and responsive:
5388  • Registers that can be written by the Driver, to configure the Dead Bus Recovery logic and trigger the
5389  mechanism;

7 Register Interface
5411 This Section of the Specification details the Register Set implemented by the Host Controller.
5412 The Register Set has several sections. The Capabilities and Operational registers (Section 7.3.1) are
5413 mandatory to implement, and for data transfer either the PIO Section or the Ring Headers Section is
5414 mandatory to implement.
5415 For Host Controllers that expose both PIO Mode and DMA Mode, the Driver shall select the current
5416 operating mode, and shall not use the register section associated with the other operating mode (the one that
5417 is not selected).
5418 The DAT and DCT Sections shall either be implemented either in the Register Map, or accessed from Host
5419 system memory. If the Host Controller does not implement the DAT and/or the DCT as internal registers,
5420 then the Driver shall allocate memory and provide the address in the Base Address registers that hold
5421 pointers for Device Context (see Section 7.4.19 and Section 7.4.20).
5422 All Vendor-Specific registers should be exposed in vendor-specific Extended Capability structures, as part
5423 of the Extended Capabilities list (see Section 7.7).
5424 The Host Controller shall ignore writes to Reserved fields and registers. The Host Controller Driver shall
5425 write the value 0 to all Reserved fields and registers. A Read from any Reserved field or register shall
5426 return the value 0.
5427 The Host Controller shall support Byte, Word, and DWORD accesses to all registers in the Register Map.
7.1 Register Memory Access Conventions
5428 In Memory Access columns in Section 7, the conventions shown in Table 11 are used.
5429 Table 11 Register Memory Access Conventions
Symbol Meaning Notes
R Read-Only Can only read from the register, cannot write to it
R/W Read/Write Can read from the register or write to it
Can read from the register
R/cW Read, conditional Write Writes are conditionally allowed, based on operating mode or
other current status
Can read from the register
R/W1C Read, Write 1 to Clear
To reset register value to its default value, write the value 1
W Write-Only Can only write to the register, read returns 0
7.2 PCI Configuration Registers
5430 Per the PCI Code and ID Assignment Specification [PCISIG01], compliance to this MIPI I3C Host
5431 Controller Interface Specification is indicated in the PCI header with Base Class equal to 0xCh, Sub Class
5432 equal to 0xAh, and Programming Interface equal to 0x0h. BAR0 configures decode for the HCI registers
5433 defined in the Register Map section. For more information refer to Section 9.2.1.1.

7.3 Register Map
5434 The Host Controller implements a defined Register Map (i.e., a standardized set of registers) for
5435 configuration and control. When using System Bus types that support direct memory access (see
5436 Section 9.1), the Host Controller may also optionally support Driver-allocated Host memory; see the
5437 maximal configuration shown in Figure 43.
5438 The Register Set is divided into the following sections:
5439 • Capability and Operational Registers (see Section 7.3.1) define software-discoverable Host Controller
5440 capabilities, allow software to limit these capabilities, control Host Controller behavior and current state,
5441 and define pointers to all other sections in the Register Map.
5442 Note:
5443 Capability and Operational Registers are the only registers in the Register Map whose offset
5444 from Base Address is static. The offset for all other registers in the Register Map are instead
5445 related to the particular Register Map section. These section base offsets might be read from
5446 the Capability and Operational Registers section, or from the Extended Capabilities registers
5447 in any Extended Capability structures that might be defined. Software shall evaluate the
5448 section base offset before accessing any register outside of the Capability and Operational
5449 Registers section.
5450 • Device Address Table (DAT) (see Section 7.3.3) stores Static and Dynamic Addresses and configuration
5451 information for some or all Devices controlled by the Host Controller. The DAT table is populated by
5452 software.
5453 Note:
5454 An index into the DAT is used for target Device identification in Command/Transfer
5455 Descriptors and the Host Controller shall use the index into the DAT to determine the Device’s
5456 Address from the indicated DAT entry for all Transfer Commands.
5457 • Device Characteristic Table (DCT) (see Section 7.3.3) is a transient table that provides temporary
5458 storage and captures the PID, DCR, BCR, and assigned Dynamic Address during the Dynamic Address
5459 Allocation procedure (i.e., the ENTDAA CCC), for software to read afterwards.
5460 • Optional Device Context in Driver-allocated Host system memory stores the DAT, the DCT, or both, if
5461 supported by the System Bus.
5462 • Ring Headers Descriptor and a set of Ring Headers (see Section 7.3.4) define the header structure for
5463 Rings. Rings are used to hold descriptors for DMA transfers for Commands, Transfers, and Events. This
5464 Specification permits multiple Ring Header instances.
5465 • PIO (Programmable I/O) (see Section 7.3.5) defines registers to allow Command, Transfer, and Event
5466 transmission using registers rather than Rings.
5467 • Extended Capabilities (see Section 7.3.2) define a linked list of capabilities, including vendor-specific
5468 capabilities, arranged as a linked list of Extended Capability structures.
5469 Note:
5470 Any features beyond those defined in this Specification would be implemented through vendor-
5471 specific Extended Capability structures.

5473 Although the Device Address Table (DAT) and Device Characteristics Table (DCT) are logically
5474 considered structures, from the software point of view they should be implemented as a set of registers for
5475 efficiency. If the system bus type supports direct memory access and the Host Controller includes DMA
5476 capability, then the Host Controller shall indicate whether the DAT and/or DCT are implemented as
5477 registers, or whether the Driver must allocate memory for all DAT entries and/or all DCT entries. This
5478 memory is referred to as the Device Context.
5479 If the Host Controller has multiple Bus Controller instances (per Section 7.7.4), then some or all of these
5480 register sections will exist for each Bus Controller instance.

7.3.1 Capabilities and Operation Registers
5481 Registers in the Capabilities and Operation Registers section are defined with offsets from the Register
5482 Map base Address of the current Bus Controller instance. The base Address of the first Bus Controller
5483 instance shall always be 0x0. Base Addresses of any additional Bus Controller instances in the same Host
5484 Controller are exposed by the registers in the Multi-Bus Instance Extended Capability Section (see
5485 Section 7.7.4).
5486 All other register sections that are associated with this I3C Bus Controller instance in the Host Controller
5487 may be placed at any offset relative to this base Address, as indicated by the pointers (i.e., section offset
5488 registers) within this register section (see Section 7.4):
5489 • Register DAT_SECTION_OFFSET (see Section 7.4.11) shall describe the DAT, whether it is implemented as
5490 registers in the Register Set, or required to be allocated by the Driver as Host system memory (as per
5491 Section 7.3.3 and Section 8.1).
5492 • Register DCT_SECTION_OFFSET (see Section 7.4.12) shall describe the DCT, whether it is implemented
5493 as registers in the Register Set, or required to be allocated by the Driver as Host system memory (as per
5494 Section 7.3.3 and Section 8.2).
5495 • If this I3C Bus Controller instance supports DMA Mode, then register RING_HEADERS_SECTION_OFFSET
5496 (see Section 7.4.13) shall provide the offset to the Ring Header Preamble at the start of the Ring Header
5497 Specific Registers section (see Section 7.3.4).
5498 • If this I3C Bus Controller instance supports PIO Mode, then register PIO_SECTION_OFFSET (see
5499 Section 7.4.14) shall provide the offset to the start of the Programmable I/O Registers section (see
5500 Section 7.3.5).
5501 • Register EXT_CAPS_SECTION_OFFSET (see Section 7.4.15) shall provide the offset to the start of the first
5502 Extended Capability structure (i.e., the beginning of the linked list of such structures; see Section 7.3.2).
5503 The definition of the Capabilities and Operation Registers section is specific to the HCI version indicated
5504 by register HCI_VERSION (i.e., the first DWORD register). Naturally, the Host Controller may define
5505 additional, vendor-specific registers in addition to the mandatory definitions.
5506 This version of the I3C HCI Specification defines the Capabilities and Operation Registers used in Active
5507 Controller mode, and that are generally used while the Host Controller is acting as Active Controller of the
5508 I3C Bus. Support for Target and Secondary Controller use models (i.e., for Standby Controller mode) is
5509 optional, and would require additional registers; this I3C HCI Specification defines certain Extended
5510 Capability structures for Standby Controller mode (see Section 6.17 and Section 7.7.11).

7.3.2  Extended Capabilities Registers
5513  Extended Capabilities are expressed as a list of vendor-specific registers. These registers shall be placed in
5514  a contiguous set of registers, and shall be treated as a linked list comprising one or more Extended
5515  Capability structures.
5516  In general, the Extended Capability structures that are defined in this I3C HCI Specification are optional for
5517  an I3C Host Controller; however, some exceptions are defined in order to expose support for certain
5518  optional features and capabilities.
5519  Additionally, certain optional features and capabilities might be subsequently defined in future I3C HCI
5520  Feature Specifications, which would extend the core Host Controller functionality defined in this I3C HCI
5521  Specification.
5522  Each Extended Capability structure has a defined length in DWORDs, and specifies a Capability ID
5523  defining the type of capability the structure describes. Note that the first register in each Extended
Capability structure must be an Extended Capability Header register (EXTCAP_HEADER, Section 7.7.1)

5540 of Extended Capability structures; however, some exceptions are defined for specific Capability IDs which

7.3.3 DAT and DCT Registers
5542 The Device Address Table (DAT) and Device Characteristic Table (DCT) shall be implemented either as a
5543 Register Set, or in Driver-allocated memory at an Address indicated with the Device Context pointer.
5544 When the DAT and/or DCT is implemented in a Register Set, the order of DWORDs in the structure is
5545 DW0 (comprising Bits[31:0]) first (lowest Address). All entries within the register set are contiguous.
5546 Example: For 2 DWORDs DAT entry size, if the DAT offset points at 0x400 for the first Device,
5547 then the lowest-order DWORD of the DAT (DW0, containing Device type, Static Address, etc.) is
5548 located at offset 0x400, and the next DWORD of the DAT (DW1, containing the Auto-Command
5549 configuration) is located at offset 0x404. The second Device is located at offsets 0x408 (DW0) and
5550 0x40C (DW1).
5551 When the DAT and/or DCT is implemented in Driver-allocated memory (per Section 6.2), the DWORDs
5552 appear with DW0 in the lowest Addresses. The Host Controller shall define the expected sizes for the tables
5553 based on the number of entries (i.e., field TABLE_SIZE). The Host Controller shall use the following
5554 partitioning for the Driver-allocated memory:
5555 • If only the DAT is implemented in Driver-allocated memory (i.e., not registers), then:
5556 • The first DAT entry shall start at offset 0x0; the second DAT entry shall start at offset 0x8; etc. This
5557 continues for all entries, as defined by field TABLE_SIZE in register DAT_SECTION_OFFSET (i.e., with 2
5558 DWORDs for each entry).
5559 • The Driver must allocate a region of memory that is large enough to hold all DAT entries.
5560 • If only the DCT is implemented in Driver-allocated memory (i.e., not registers), then:
Copyright © 2018–2023 MIPI Alliance, Inc. 189
Public Release Edition

Specification for I3C HCI Version 1.2
15-Feb-2023
5561 • The first DCT entry shall start at offset 0x0; the second DCT entry shall start at offset 0x10; etc. This
5562 continues for all entries, as defined by field TABLE_SIZE in register DCT_SECTION_OFFSET (i.e., with 4
5563 DWORDs for each entry).
5564 • The Driver must allocate a region of memory that is large enough to hold all DCT entries.
5565 • If both the DAT and DCT are implemented in Driver-allocated memory (i.e., not registers), then:
5566 • The DAT entries shall start at offset 0x0 (as above), with 2 DWORDs for each DAT entry, and continue
5567 through the last DAT entry (i.e., as defined by field TABLE_SIZE in register DAT_SECTION_OFFSET).
5568 • After the last DAT entry, the DCT entries shall start at offset (DAT_SECTION_OFFSET.TABLE_SIZE) * 8,
5569 with 4 DWORDs for each DCT entry, and continue through the last DCT entry (i.e., as defined by field
5570 TABLE_SIZE in register DCT_SECTION_OFFSET).
5571 • The Driver must allocate a region of memory that is large enough to hold all DAT and DCT entries.
5572 For detailed descriptions of the DAT and DCT data structures, see Section 8.1 and Section 8.2, respectively.
5573 Note:
5574 The TABLE_SIZE fields in registers DAT_SECTION_OFFSET and DCT_SECTION_OFFSET are read-
5575 only to the Host, and cannot be changed by the Driver. The Host Controller determines how many
5576 entries it uses for each such table that it expects the Driver to store in system memory.

7.4.2 Host Controller Control (HC_CONTROL) (BASE + 0x4)
5593 Host Controller Control register is used to manage the Host Controller and Controller Configuration.
5594 Table 18 Host Controller Control (HC_CONTROL) Register
Size Memory Reset
Field Name Description
[Bits] Access Value
1 BUS_ENABLE R/W 0x0 Host Controller Bus Enable
[31] Enables or disables the operation on the
I3C Bus by the Host Controller.
If the software sets this bit, then it also
confirms that initialization is done, and that
the Host Controller can use the
programmed register values (e.g.,
generation of SCL on IBI detection, etc.). If
this bit is not set, then the Host Controller
shall not generate SCL for incoming IBI.
Software may disable the Host Controller
bus operation while it is active, However:
• If a disable request occurs while
receiving IBI, the actual disabling will not
occur until reception of the IBI is
complete.
• If a disable request occurs while the Host
Controller still has additional Commands
queued for transfers, then the actual
disabling will not occur until transmission
of all queued Commands is complete
(i.e., until the Host Controller encounters
a Command with field TOC set to 1). The
Host Controller shall then return to the
Idle state (as indicated in register
PRESENT_STATE_DEBUG).
When the software reads the value 1'b0
from this field, this indicates that the Host
Controller bus operation disable operation
has completed.
Values:
• 1'b0: DISABLED: The Host Controller bus
operation is Disabled
• 1'b1: ENABLED: The Host Controller bus
operation is Enabled

Size Memory Reset
Field Name Description

1 RESUME R/W1C 0x0 Host Controller Resume
[30] This bit is used to resume Host Controller
operation following the Halt state.
The Host Controller enters the Halt state
(as indicated in register
PRESENT_STATE_DEBUG) as a result of
any type of error occurring in a transfer. The
error type is indicated by field ERR_STATUS
in the Response Descriptor (see
Section 8.5).
After the Host Controller has entered the
Halt state, software must write the value
1'b1 to the RESUME bit to resume operation
(i.e., write 1 to clear).
Values (when read):
• 1'b0: RUNNING: The Host Controller is
running
• 1'b1: SUSPENDED: The Host Controller
is suspended
1 ABORT R/W 0x0 Host Controller Abort
[29] When set to 1, this bit triggers the Host
Controller Abort operation which may abort
the currently issued transfer (see
Section 6.8.4).
In response to an ABORT request, the Host
Controller terminates the current
transaction on the I3C Bus at the nearest
opportunity (i.e., after the complete data
byte is transferred or received).
Usage and operational details vary, per the
current operating mode. (See
Section 6.8.4, Table 6)

7.4.3 Controller Device Address (CONTROLLER_DEVICE_ADDR) (BASE + 0x8)
5595 The Controller Device Address register is used to program the Host Controller’s Dynamic Address. In
5596 Active Controller mode, the software shall self-assign the Dynamic Address if it is the Primary Controller
5597 (i.e., before initiating its first Controller-to-Controller Handoff Procedure).
5598 Table 19 Controller Device Address (CONTROLLER_DEVICE_ADDR) Register
Size Memory Reset
Field Name Description
[Bits] Access Value
1 DYNAMIC_ADDR_VALID R/W 0x0 Dynamic Address is Valid
[31] This bit indicates whether or not the value in the
DYNAMIC_ADDR field is valid.
This bit must be set to 1'b1 before passing the
Controller Role to another Controller.
In Active Controller mode, the software shall set
this bit to 1'b1 as it self-assigns its Dynamic
Address. This requires the Host Controller to act
as the Primary Controller of the I3C Bus.
If operating as a Secondary Controller (i.e., in
Standby Controller mode), then the Host
Controller shall set this bit to 1'b1 when the
Active Controller assigns the Dynamic Address
(see Note below this table).
Values:
• 1'b0: The Dynamic Address field is not valid
• 1'b1: The Dynamic Address field is valid
8 RESERVED R 0x0 –
[30:23]
7 DYNAMIC_ADDR R/W 0x0 Device Dynamic Address
[22:16] This field is used to program the Host Controller
Device’s Dynamic Address in Active Controller
mode, before passing the Controller Role to
another Controller.
In Active Controller mode, the software shall
program the Dynamic Address as it self-assigns
its Dynamic Address.
If operating as a Secondary Controller, then the

7.4.5 Reset Control (RESET_CONTROL) (BASE + 0x10)
5607 Reset Control register is used to reset specific functional areas of Host Controller, including buffer resets.
5608 Table 21 Reset Control (RESET_CONTROL) Register
Size Memory Reset
Field Name Description
[Bits] Access Value
26 RESERVED – – –
[31:6]
1 IBI_QUEUE_RST R/W 0x0 IBI Queue Buffer Software Reset
[5] On software setting this bit to 1'b1, the IBI
Queues in the Controller shall be flushed. This
field shall be cleared automatically upon
completion of IBI Queue reset.
This field is valid for PIO Mode only.
1 RX_FIFO_RST R/W 0x0 Receive Queue Buffer Software Reset
[4] On software setting this bit to 1'b1, the Rx
Queues in the Controller shall be flushed. This
field shall be cleared automatically upon
completion of Rx Data Queue reset.
This field is valid for PIO Mode only.
1 TX_FIFO_RST R/W 0x0 Transmit Queue Buffer Software Reset
[3] On software setting this bit to 1'b1, the Tx
Queues in the Controller shall be flushed. This
field shall be cleared automatically upon Tx
Data Queue reset completion.
This field is valid for PIO Mode only.
1 RESP_QUEUE_RST R/W 0x0 Response Queue Software Reset
[2] On software setting this bit to 1'b1, the
Response Queues in the Controller shall be
flushed. This field shall be cleared
automatically upon Response Queue reset
completion.
This field is valid for PIO Mode only.
1 CMD_QUEUE_RST R/W 0x0 Command Queue Software Reset
[1] On software setting this bit to 1'b1, the
Command Queues in the Controller shall be
flushed. This field shall be cleared
automatically upon Command Queue reset
completion.
This field is valid for PIO Mode only.

Size Memory Reset
Field Name Description
[Bits] Access Value
1 SOFT_RST R/W 0x0 Core Software Reset
[0] On Driver setting this bit to 1'b1, the Host
Controller shall be reset and disabled. All
registers shall return to their reset values, and
the software shall re-initialize the Controller.
This field is cleared automatically upon Host
Controller reset completion.
This field also resets all Queues in the Host
Controller.
This field does not reset any Ring Headers in
the Host Controller.
Note:
Programming this field while it contains a
value of 1'b1 may result in undefined
behavior.

7.4.6 Present State (PRESENT_STATE) (BASE + 0x14)
5609 The Present State Register returns the Host Controller’s current state. State has two parts: this register
5610 which is mandatory, and an additional optional PRESENT_STATE_DEBUG register intended for debug
5611 purposes (see the Debug Capability registers in the Extended Capabilities list).
5612 Table 22 Present State (PRESENT_STATE) Register
Size Memory Reset
Field Name Description
[Bits] Access Value
29 RESERVED R 0x0 –
[31:3]
1 AC_CURRENT_OWN R 0x0 Active Controller
[2] This bit indicates whether or not the
Host Controller is presently the Active
Controller on the I3C Bus.
The Active Controller is the Controller-
capable Device on the I3C Bus that
owns the SCL line.
If Standby Controller mode is
supported, then this field is mirrored in
register STBY_CR_STATUS
(Section 7.7.11.4).
Values:
• 1'b0: NOT_BUS_OWNER: The Host
Controller is not the Active Controller,
and must request and acquire the
Controller Role before initiating any
transfer.
• 1'b1: BUS_OWNER: The Host
Controller is the Active Controller,
and as a result can initiate transfers.
Note:
Acting as a Secondary Controller
(i.e., value 1'b0) requires the
implementer to add I3C Secondary
Controller Logic, and also add
support for Standby Controller
mode as an Extended Capability.

7.4.7  Interrupt Status (INTR_STATUS) (BASE + 0x20)
5613  The Interrupt Status register reflects the status of outstanding interrupts relating to general Host Controller
5614  errors or other actions.
5615  The status fields are R/W1C (i.e., write 1 to clear).
5616  The bit fields in this register act as Status Bits, according to the interrupt register model described in
5617  Section 6.14. These bits will be set (i.e., the “Status bit set” action will occur) if the interrupt condition is
5618  detected, and if the corresponding bit in the Interrupt Status Enable Mask is set to 1'b1.

7.4.8  Interrupt Status Enable (INTR_STATUS_ENABLE) (BASE + 0x24)
5620  The Interrupt Status Enable register enables or disables reporting of outstanding interrupts.
5621  The bit fields in this register act as Interrupt Status Enable Mask bits, according to the interrupt register
5622  model described in Section 6.14. Writes to these fields shall enable or disable the visibility of an interrupt
5623  condition in the Status Register. The value of each field shall determine whether the interrupt condition will
5624  be passed to the Interrupt Signal Mask to result in an Interrupt trigger; and will also determine whether
5625  software sees the interrupt condition using polling (i.e., without using an interrupt service routine).

7.4.18 IBI Data Abort Control (IBI_DATA_ABORT_CTRL) (BASE + 0x5C)
5663 The IBI Data Abort Control register allows the Driver to configure the Host Controller’s monitoring logic
5664 for ongoing IBI data payload transfers. When enabled, the Driver may request the I3C Bus Controller Logic
5665 to abort (i.e., to forcibly stop) an ongoing In-Band Interrupt Request, if and when the Driver determines
5666 that the IBI Data Payload should no longer be allowed to continue (see Section 6.9.4).

• 1'b0: DISABLED: No IBI Data Abort

transfer immediately (i.e., 0 more Chunks).
• 2'd1–2'd3 (N): DELAYED: Abort the IBI data
payload transfer after N more Chunks (i.e., N
from 1 thru 3). If the the Target terminates the

then no abort is performed.

7.4.19 Device Context Base Address Low (DEV_CTX_BASE_LO) (BASE + 0x60)
5684 The Device Context Base Address Low register points to Driver-allocated memory containing Device
5685 Context (i.e., DAT and/or DCT) when either or both are provided in Host system memory (per
5686 Section 7.3.3).
5687 This register and the following one (i.e., DEV_CTX_BASE_HI) are only present for Host Controllers that
5688 support direct access to Host system memory through a Memory Access Engine (i.e., DMA engine). If a
5689 Host Controller does not support direct access to Host system memory, then these registers shall be read-
5690 only, and both the DAT and the DCT shall be implemented in registers.
5691 If the Host Controller also supports Scatter-Gather capability (as indicated in field SG_CAPABILITY_DC_EN
5692 of register HC_CAPABILITIES; see Section 7.4.4), then the appropriate Scatter-Gather register shall also be
5693 implemented as register DEV_CTX_SG (see Section 7.4.21).
5694 If either the DAT Section Offset (i.e., register DAT_SECTION_OFFSET, see Section 7.4.11) or the DCT
5695 Section Offset (i.e., register DCT_SECTION_OFFSET, see Section 7.4.12) indicate that the Host Controller
5696 does not implement table entries in registers (with field TABLE_OFFSET in either register having a value of
5697 12'h000), then the Driver must allocate enough System memory to contain the required number of entries.
5698 The total amount of memory for each section shall be the sum of the number of entries multiplied by the
5699 size of the entry. If both the DAT and the DCT are required, then the total size of allocated memory can be
5700 expressed as follows:
5701 sizeof ( DAT ) + sizeof( DCT )
5702 • If Scatter-Gather mode is not supported, then this must be a single contiguous allocation of physical
5703 memory, large enough to hold all table entries.
5704 • The Driver shall write the base address of this single allocation of memory into the Base Address
5705 registers.
5706 • If Scatter-Gather mode is supported, then this might be either a single contiguous allocation (as above),
5707 or it might consist of a series of individual chunks (i.e., smaller allocations) having a total size sufficient
5708 to hold all table entries described by an array of Memory Descriptor structures (see Section 8.7).
5709 • The Driver shall set field BLP of register DEV_CTX_SG to indicate whether it is providing a single
5710 allocation (as above) or an array of individual allocations.
5711 • For an array of individual allocations, the Driver shall write the address pointer for the array of
5712 Memory Descriptor structures into the Base Address registers, and shall write the size of this array into
5713 field LIST_SIZE of register DEV_CTX_SG.
5714 • Refer to Section 6.2.1 for more information on Scatter-Gather memory allocation.

[31:0] Lower 32 bits of pointer to physical memory
allocated for storing Device Context.
The Device Context is DWORD aligned, so the last
two Address bits will always be 2'b00.

7.5 PIO Mode Registers
5733 All PIO Mode registers are defined as relative offsets, starting from the location indicated by register
5734 PIO_SECTION_OFFSET (see Section 7.4.14), if PIO Mode is supported.
7.5.1 Command Queue Port (COMMAND_QUEUE_PORT) (PIO + 0x0)
5735 32-bit mailbox register COMMAND_QUEUE_PORT is a write-only register that the Driver uses to enqueue a
5736 Command Descriptor structure in a format that depends on the requested command type. All command
5737 types are defined in Section 8.4.
5738 When writing to this register to enqueue a Command Descriptor structure, the Driver must write DWORDs
5739 in the correct order, starting with the Least Significant DWORD (i.e., starting at bit 0) until the Most
5740 Significant DWORD. The Driver shall use this register to enqueue new commands, including Transfer
5741 Commands, per Section 6.8.1.
5742 For a 64-bit Command Descriptor, the two DWORDs are written in order, from lowest to highest (i.e.,
5743 DWORD 0 followed by DWORD 1).
5744 Upon receiving two DWORD writes to register COMMAND_QUEUE_PORT, the Host Controller shall
5745 enqueue the new Command Descriptor.
5746 Note:
5747 Usage of a Command Descriptor is defined in Section 6.7.
7.5.2 Response Queue Port (RESPONSE_QUEUE_PORT) (PIO + 0x4)
5748 32-bit mailbox register RESPONSE_QUEUE_PORT is a read-only register that the Driver uses to read a
5749 Response Descriptor structure (see Section 8.5) generated in the Response Queue, after a command that
5750 was previously processed by the Host Controller.
5751 Each DWORD read of this register shall consume (i.e., shall dequeue) one Response Descriptor from the
5752 Response Queue. The Driver shall read from this register to determine the status of commands, such as
5753 Transfer Commands, per Section 6.8.1.
5754 The Driver should not attempt to read from this register unless there is at least one Response Descriptor
5755 pending in the Response Queue. The Driver may receive a notification based on Queue Status indication, in
5756 the form of a PIO Interrupt (i.e., field RESP_READY_STAT in register PIO_INTR_STATUS; see Section 7.5.9).
222 Copyright © 2018–2023 MIPI Alliance, Inc.
Public Release Edition

Version 1.2   Specification for I3C HCI
15-Feb-2023
7.5.3  Transfer Data Port (XFER_DATA_PORT) (PIO + 0x8)
5757  32-bit mailbox register XFER_DATA_PORT is a 32-bit bi-directional data transfer register that is used both to
5758  read from the RX_DATA_PORT (which reads from the Rx Data Queue), and to write to the TX_DATA_PORT
5759  (which writes to the Tx Data Queue). In other words, registers RX_DATA_PORT and TX_DATA_PORT have
5760  the same offset, forming a single bi-directional port for transmitting or receiving Host Controller data for
5761  Transfer Commands per Section 6.8.1.
5762  • Read Operations: To receive data from the RX Buffer, the Driver shall read from register
5763  RX_DATA_PORT. Its reset value is undefined, and should be read based on Queue Status indication. The
5764  Host Controller may send a notification in the form of a PIO Interrupt.
5765  • Write Operations: To send data to the TX Buffer, the Driver shall write to register TX_DATA_PORT.
5766
Note:
5767  The ordering of bytes within the DWORDs that are written into the Tx Data Queue or read
5768  from the Rx Data Queue via this register shall use the current data byte ordering mode, per
5769  Section 6.8.3.

Controller shall only send the valid number of bytes
indicated in the DATA_LENGTH field of the Command
Descriptor.

7.5.4 IBI Port (IBI_PORT) (PIO + 0xC)
5772 32-bit mailbox register IBI_PORT is a read-only register the Driver uses to read DWORDs from the IBI
5773 Queue containing an IBI Status Descriptor (see Section 8.6) and any associated IBI Data, after an Interrupt
5774 Request (e.g., an In-Band Interrupt Request) was received by the Host Controller.
5775 When receiving an IBI, the Driver shall first read the IBI Status Descriptor, followed by consecutive
5776 DWORDs of IBI Data (as specified in Section 6.9.1). The Host Controller shall enqueue the IBI Status
5777 Descriptor as the first DWORD for the IBI event, followed by any DWORDs of data associated with that
5778 IBI event.
5779 Note:
5780 If the I3C HCI Auto-Command feature is used, then the IBI Data will include the data received via
5781 the auto-generated private read operation.
5782 The Driver should not attempt to read from this register unless there is at least one IBI Status Descriptor
5783 pending in the IBI Data Queue. The Driver may receive a notification based on Queue Status indication, in
5784 the form of a PIO Interrupt (i.e., field IBI_STATUS_THLD_STAT in register PIO_INTR_STATUS; see
5785 Section 7.5.9).

7.5.5 Queue Threshold Control (QUEUE_THLD_CTRL) (PIO + 0x10)
5787 The Queue Threshold Control register controls the interrupt trigger thresholds for the Command Queue, the
5788 Response Queue, and the IBI Queue. It also controls the maximum size of the IBI Data segment for each
5789 IBI Status Descriptor, for IBIs that have long payload data and require multiple IBI Status Descriptors (per
5790 Section 6.9.1).
5791 Note:
5792 It is assumed that the Host Controller has exactly one Command Queue, exactly one Response
5793 Queue, and exactly one IBI Queue.
5794 The specific reset values are indicative, and could be hardware implementation specific.

Size Memory Reset
