[Bits] Access Value
8 IBI_STATUS_THLD R/W 0x1 IBI Status Threshold
[31:24] Controls generation of the
IBI_STATUS_THLD_STAT interrupt, based on
the value of the IBI Queue’s outstanding IBI
Statuses.
Values:
• 0: Not valid, do not use
• 1–255 (N): Interrupt is generated when
the number of outstanding IBI Statuses is
equal to or greater than N.
Each IBI Status entry can represent either
the complete IBI payload (if the IBI payload
byte size <= 4 * IBI_DATA_SEGMENT_SIZE),
or a segment of the IBI payload (if the IBI
payload byte size >
4 * IBI_DATA_SEGMENT_SIZE).
8 IBI_DATA_SEGMENT_SIZE R/W 0x1 IBI Data Segment Size
[23:16] Controls the maximum size of IBI Data
segments, in DWORDs.
Supported Values:
• Minimum: 1 (1 DWORD = 4 Bytes)
• Maximum: 63 (63 DWORDs = 252
Bytes), provided that the configured IBI
Queue depth is >= 64.
In PIO Mode, this field allows the incoming
IBI Data to be sliced into multiple segments
generating status individually, to support cut-
through readout of a long IBI Payload Data.
When Asynchronous Timing Control Mode is
supported, this field should be set to a value
of 4 or more to allow the single data segment
to contain the entire Controller timestamp
value (i.e., both C_REF and C_C2).

5833 This register contains additional read-only parameters that describe the PIO Queues, including:

5841 Note:
5842 This register is new for this version of this I3C HCI Specification. The Driver shall try to read this
5843 register when initializing the Host Controller, to determine whether the Command Queue and
5844 Response Queue have different sizes, and whether the IBI Queue size is extended. In previous
5845 versions of this I3C HCI Specification, the Command Queue and Response Queue were required
5846 to have the same size, and the maximum IBI Queue size was limited to 255 DWORDs.
5847 If the IBI Queue size is extended, then this shall have no effect on how the Host Controller treats
5848 the value written to field IBI_STATUS_THLD in register QUEUE_THLD_CTRL.
5849 If this register is not present, or if the Host Controller returns a value of all zeros, then the Driver
5850 should assume that none of the additional options are supported, namely: the size of the Response
5851 Queue is the same as the size of the Command Queue, as reported by field CR_QUEUE_SIZE in
5852 register QUEUE_SIZE, and the IBI Queue size is not extended (i.e., is exactly the number of
5853 DWORDs reported by field IBI_STATUS_SIZE). This ensures that Drivers can remain compatible
5854 with existing implementations that conform to previous versions of this I3C HCI Specification. Note
5855 that such implementations will return values of all zeros for registers that are not present.

7.5.9  PIO Interrupt Status (PIO_INTR_STATUS) (PIO + 0x20)
5856  The PIO Interrupt Status register indicates the status of outstanding interrupts relating to the PIO Queues or
5857  other PIO events and errors.
5858  The status fields are either R/W1C (write 1 to clear), or else are cleared based on queue operations.
5859  The bit fields in this register act as Status Bits, according to the interrupt register model described in
5860  Section 6.14. The Host Controller shall set these bits (i.e., the “Status bit set” action will occur) if the
5861  interrupt condition is detected, and if the corresponding bit in the Interrupt Status Enable Mask is set to
5862  1'b1.

7.5.10  PIO Interrupt Status Enable (PIO_INTR_STATUS_ENABLE) (PIO + 0x24)
5864  The PIO Interrupt Status Enable register enables reporting of outstanding interrupts.
5865  The bit fields in this register act as Interrupt Status Enable Mask bits, according to the interrupt register
5866  model described in Section 6.14. Writes to these fields shall enable or disable the visibility of an interrupt
5867  condition in the Status Register. The value of each field shall determine whether the interrupt condition will
5868  be passed to the Interrupt Signal Mask to result in an Interrupt trigger; and will also determine whether
5869  software might see the interrupt condition using polling (i.e., without using an interrupt service routine).

7.5.13 PIO Control (PIO_CONTROL) (PIO + 0x30)
5881 The PIO Control register is used to control overall operation and status of the PIO Queues. It can be used to
5882 enable/disable access to the PIO Queues, control the execution of enqueued Command Descriptors, or abort
5883 (i.e., forcibly stop) a current Transfer Command.
5884 Note:
5885 The values written to this register and to register HC_CONTROL (Section 7.4.2) shall control overall
5886 Host Controller operation if PIO Mode is selected. Refer to Figure 11 in Section 6.5.1 for more
5887 details on the PIO initialization process.

current Command Descriptor, and hold any remaining

for operational details.
Software shall only toggle this bit if field ENABLE has

• 1'b1: PIO Queue Abort request
• 1'b0: PIO Queue Abort clear request (i.e., resume
processing)
1 RS R/W 0x0 PIO Run / Stop Request

Software may use this bit to dynamically pause

Descriptor.

• 1'b1: PIO Queue Start request

While access is disabled, software may not read from
or write to any PIO Queue registers.
Values:
• 1'b1: PIO Queues Enable request
• 1'b0: PIO Queues Disable request

7.6 Ring Headers Specific Registers
5889 The Host Controller has two transfer Modes: PIO Mode, and DMA Mode for transfers. In DMA Mode, the
5890 Host Controller exposes one or more Ring Headers which the Driver uses to allocate Ring-related memory.
5891 Rings are defined in Bundles of Command/Response Rings, and Event Rings.
5892 The number of Ring Bundles supported is defined by Host Controller, and may be limited by the Driver,
5893 with a maximum of eight Ring Bundles in total.
5894 All Ring-related registers appear in the Ring Headers section of the Register Map, beginning with register
5895 Ring Headers Preamble which defines how many Ring Bundles the Host Controller supports, and the size
5896 of the Ring Header Descriptor structure (expressed as a power of 2). The Preamble also allows the Driver
5897 to limit the number of Rings in use. This is followed by the Ring Header Offsets.
5898 The Ring Headers Preamble and Offsets registers are defined as relative offsets, starting from the location
5899 indicated by register RING_HEADERS_SECTION_OFFSET (see Section 7.4.13), if DMA Mode is supported.

7.6.10 Ring Header Descriptor (RH +)
5919 The following registers comprise one Ring Header Descriptor, and are defined for each Ring Bundle that
5920 the Host Controller supports. The starting offset of each Ring Header Descriptor is linked from registers
5921 RH0_OFFSET through RH7_OFFSET (see Section 7.6.2 through Section 7.6.9).
5922 Relative offsets of these registers are shown accordingly (i.e., from the starting offset of the corresponding
5923 Ring Header).
5924 The layout of registers within a Ring Header Descriptor is shown in Section 6.6.4.
7.6.10.1 CR Setup (CR_SETUP) (RH + 0x0)
5925 The Command/Response Ring Setup register provides the sizes of the Transfer Descriptor structures in the
5926 Command Ring, and the corresponding Response Descriptor structures in the Response Ring. This register
5927 also allows the Driver to set the overall size (i.e., number of entries) for both of these Rings.
5928 The Driver shall read fields XFER_STRUCT_SIZE and RESP_STRUCT_SIZE, and allocate physical memory
5929 buffers with sizes (in bytes) that are at least XFER_STRUCT_SIZE * RING_SIZE (for the Command Ring) and
5930 RESP_STRUCT_SIZE * RING_SIZE (for the Response Ring).
5931 • If either Ring does not use Scatter-Gather, or if Scatter-Gather is not supported (per Section 6.2.1), then
5932 the single memory buffer for the Ring shall be contiguous, and shall have a size sufficient to hold all
5933 structures in the Ring.
5934 If Scatter-Gather is supported and enabled for either Ring (per Section 6.2.1), then the Driver shall allocate
5935 an array of Memory Descriptor structures (see Section 8.7), and each shall be configured to point to an
5936 allocated memory buffer for that portion of the Ring. Note that each portion shall be a multiple of the
5937 Ring’s structure size, and the sum of these buffers (i.e., all the portions of the Ring) described by all such
5938 Memory Descriptors shall be sufficient to hold all structures in the Ring (i.e., the value of RING_SIZE,
5939 which applies to both Command and Response Rings).
5940 The Driver shall update field RING_SIZE before starting the Ring Bundle. See Section 6.6.1 for more details
5941 on Ring Bundle initialization.
5942 If the Driver sets RING_SIZE to 0, then the Host Controller shall consider the Command/Response Rings to
5943 be not allocated, and shall disable Command/Response processing for this Ring Bundle.

5945 Note:
5946 If fields XFER_STRUCT_SIZE and/or RESP_STRUCT_SIZE are larger than the minimum structure
5947 sizes (i.e., 20 bytes or 4 bytes, respectively) then the implementer has defined a larger structure
5948 size for a specific purpose, and the Driver must allocate sufficient memory in the Ring to
5949 accomodate the larger structure size. In this case, the use of such additional bytes in each
5950 structure shall be defined by the implementer, and the Driver must not assume that these additional
5951 bytes are available for general use. If larger structure sizes are used, then implementers should
5952 provide sizes that are DWORD-aligned, for optimal system performance.
5953 A value of 0 in field RING_SIZE effectively disables the Command/Response Ring processing for a
5954 particular Ring Bundle, and allows the Driver to enable processing for only the IBI Rings (i.e., in
5955 register IBI_SETUP) for this Ring Bundle. If the Command/Response Rings are enabled, then the
5956 minimum Ring size shall be 2 entries, although the smallest usable size might be somewhat greater
5957 (i.e., at least 4 entries) per the use case, since the size of a Ring is primarily limited by available
5958 Host system memory.

7.6.10.2 IBI Setup (IBI_SETUP) (RH + 0x4)
5959 The IBI Ring Setup register provides the sizes of the IBI Status Descriptor structures and the IBI Data
5960 Chunk, and the overall size of the IBI Ring.
5961 The Driver shall read the IBI_STATUS_STRUCT_SIZE field and allocate physical memory buffer(s) of at least
5962 (IBI_STATUS_STRUCT_SIZE * IBI_STATUS_RING_SIZE) bytes for the IBI Status Ring.
5963 Similarly, the Driver shall also allocate physical memory buffer(s) for the IBI Data Ring, based on the
5964 configured Data Chunk Size (i.e., field CHUNK_SIZE) and the number of Data Chunks (i.e., field
5965 CHUNK_COUNT).
5966 • If the either Ring does not use Scatter-Gather, or if Scatter-Gather is not supported per Section 6.2.1, then
5967 the single memory buffer for the Ring shall be contiguous, and shall have a size sufficient to hold all
5968 structures/chunks in the Ring.
5969 • If Scatter-Gather is supported and enabled for either Ring, per Section 6.2.1, then the Driver shall
5970 allocate an array of Memory Descriptor structures (see Section 8.7), and each shall be configured to point
5971 to an allocated memory buffer for that portion of the Ring. Note that each portion shall be a multiple of
5972 the Ring’s structure/chunk size, and the sum of these buffers (i.e., all the portions of the Ring) described
5973 by all such Memory Descriptors shall be sufficient to hold all structures/chunks in the Ring:
5974 • For the IBI Status Ring, this shall be determined by the value of field IBI_STATUS_RING_SIZE.
5975 • For the IBI Data Ring, this shall be determined by the value of field CHUNK_COUNT.
5976 The Driver shall update fields IBI_STATUS_RING_SIZE and CHUNK_COUNT before starting the Ring Bundle.
5977 See Section 6.6.1 for more details on Ring Bundle initialization.
5978 If the Driver sets IBI_STATUS_RING_SIZE and CHUNK_COUNT to 0, then the Host Controller shall consider
5979 the IBI Rings to be not allocated, and shall not serve any IBIs for this Ring Bundle.

7.6.10.5 Ring Interrupt Status Enable (RH_INTR_STATUS_ENABLE) (RH + 0x14)
5996 The Ring Interrupt Status Enable register controls reporting of outstanding interrupts, for specific Ring
5997 Bundle instances.
5998 The fields in this register act as Interrupt Status Enable Mask bits, according to the interrupt register model
5999 described in Section 6.14. Writes to these fields shall enable or disable the visibility of an interrupt
6000 condition in the Status Register. The value of each field shall determine whether the interrupt condition will
6001 be passed to the Interrupt Signal Mask to result in an Interrupt trigger; and will also determine whether
6002 software sees the interrupt condition using polling (i.e., without using an interrupt service routine).

| ----------- | ------- | ------------- | --- |
[2]

•  1'b1: Ring processing aborted per Section 6.6.6.
If the Ring is aborted, then it shall wait for Ring
Abort condition clearing and Enqueue Pointer Write
(Doorbell) in order to resume operation.
•

cleared (i.e., to resume operation)
| 1  RUNNING  | R  0x0  | Ring Running  |     |
| ----------- | ------- | ------------- | --- |
[1]
Values:
•  1'b1: Ring running
•  1'b0: Ring not running (stopped) If the Ring is not
running, then the Enqueue Pointer update shall not
trigger the processing of Transfer Commands for
the Command/Response Ring Pair.
| 1  ENABLED  | R  0x0  | Ring Enabled  |     |
| ----------- | ------- | ------------- | --- |
| [0]         |         | Values:       |     |
•  1'b1: Ring enabled
•  1'b0: Ring disabled
If the Ring is disabled, then no operation on the
Ring shall be possible.

7.6.10.9 Ring Control (RH_CONTROL) (RH + 0x24)
6017 The Ring Control register allows Ring status changes to be requested.
6018 Table 67 Ring Control (RH_CONTROL) Register
Size Memory Reset
Field Name Description
[Bits] Access Value
29 RESERVED – – –
[31:3]
1 ABORT R/W 0x0 Ring Abort Request
[2] Allows Driver to abort processing of current transfer
(at earliest opportunity) per Section 6.6.6. In the
ABORTED state, the Ring shall block processing of
any subsequent enqueued Transfer Descriptors
Values:
1'b1: Ring Abort operation request
1'b0: Ring Abort operation clear (i.e., resume
processing)
1 RS R/W 0x0 Ring Run / Stop Request
[1] If the Ring Bundle is running, then the RUNNING bit in
register RH_STATUS shall have the value 1'b1.
The Driver may use this bit to dynamically pause
operation of a given Ring Bundle. The Host Controller
shall stop the Ring Bundle gracefully at the first
possible opportunity (boundary).
The software Driver shall only toggle this bit if the
ENABLE field already has value 1'b1 (Ring Enable
requested).
Values:
1'b1: Ring Start request
1'b0: Ring Stop request
1 ENABLE R/W 0x0 Ring Enable Request
[0] If the Ring Bundle is enabled for hardware
processing, then the ENABLED bit in register
RH_STATUS shall have the value 1'b1.
A transition of this bit to 1'b1 (Enable) shall reset all
hardware internal pointers (if any).
Values:
1'b1: Ring Enable request
1'b0: Ring Disable request

7.7  Extended Capabilities Registers
Extended Capabilities are implemented as a linked list of Extended Capability structures (see Section 7.3.2)
6060
6061  Extended Capabilities registers are defined as relative offsets, starting from the location indicated by
6062  register EXT_CAPS_SECTION_OFFSET (see Section 7.4.15).
6063  Each Extended Capability structure represents one Extended Capability, as identified by the Extended
6064  Capability ID field. Table 82 lists the defined and reserved Extended Capability IDs. Further information
6065  for each defined Extended Capability ID appears below in this Section.
6066  Table 82 Extended Capability IDs
Extended Capability
Description  See Section

7.7.4  Multi-Bus Instance (ID = 0x03)
6094  This Section defines the two optional Capability-specific read-only registers that are available under
6095  Extended Capability ID 0x03, Multi-Bus Instance.
6096  This capability is only required for the first Bus Controller instance (the one that starts at absolute base
6097  Address 0x0, or BAR0 for PCIe).
6098  A Host Controller with the Multi-Bus Instance capability supports multiple I3C Buses (up to 15), with one
6099  instance of the HCI Register Set and one instance of I3C Bus Controller Logic for each I3C Bus, in a single
6100  hardware function (e.g. PCIe B/D/F). This approach makes it possible to build Host Controller hardware
6101  that supports multiple I3C Bus Controller instances, while keeping single-instance versions simple.
6102  For a Host Controller with Multi-Bus Instance functionality, each HCI entry point (i.e., HCI Register Set)
6103  describes one I3C Bus Controller instance. All register offsets defined for a given I3C Bus Controller
6104  Instance are relative to the HCI entry point for that particular I3C Bus instance.
7.7.4.1  Bus Controller Instance Count (+ 0x04)
6105  Number of additional I3C Bus Controller instances (i.e., number of HCI Register Sets – 1).

7.7.4.2 Bus Controller Instance Offset (+ 0x08 + 4*(INSTANCE_NUMBER-1))
6107 The Bus Controller Instance Offset is an array of registers. For each Bus Controller instance, the Offset
6108 register contains the offset from the primary/absolute HCI base (0x0) to the HCI Register Set for the
6109 implemented I3C Bus Controller instances.
6110 Example:
6111 Consider the case of a specific Host Controller implementation featuring Bus Instance Capability
6112 with:
6113 • Bus Controller instance 0 at offset 0x0
6114 Of course instance 0 must start at offset 0x0. The Multi-Bus Instance capability can skip
6115 this Offset.
6116 • Bus Controller instance 1 at offset 0x400
6117 HCI_VERSION for instance 1 is thus located at offset 0x400.
6118 • Bus Controller instance 2 at offset 0x1200
6119 HCI_VERSION for instance 2 is thus located at offset 0x1200.
6120 In this example, Bus Controller instance 0 features Multi-Bus instance capability with Instance
6121 Count equal to 2, Bus Controller instance 1 offset is 0x400, and Bus Controller instance 2 offset is
6122 0x1200. Optionally, Bus Controller instance 0 may be introduced, in which case the Instance Count
6123 equals 3 and Bus Controller instance 3 offset is 0x0.
6124 In the title of Table 89, the hash characters (“##”) represent the Bus Controller instance number.
6125 Table 89 Bus Controller Instance ## Offset (BUS_CTRL_INSTANCE_##_OFFSET) Register

Field Name Description
[Bits] Access Value

HCI_VERSION, or HCI entry point) for
an additional Bus Controller instance.
The number of Bus Controller
instances shall not exceed 15.

6126  This Section defines the optional Capability-specific registers available under Extended Capability ID
6127  0x0A, Target IBI Credit Counters. This capability includes a credit counting mechanism that allows
6128  individual I3C Targets to have individual credit counters for IBI payload data as well as associated Pending
6129  Read data (i.e., when used with Auto-Command, per Section 6.11). A Host Controller may support this
6130  Extended Capability; if so, then it shall implement the credit counting mechanism that manages whether
6131  individual I3C Targets are allowed to send IBI Requests on the I3C Bus, based on the credit counter for
6132  each I3C Target (see Section 6.9.5).
6133  This Extended Capability structure includes a Target Credit Table, consisting of an array of registers with
6134  one register for each Target. The size of the Target Credit Table array shall be the size of the DAT (i.e., the
6135  same  number  of  entries),  as  indicated  by  field  TABLE_SIZE  in  register TARGET_CREDIT_TABLE  (see
Section 7.7.5.1).

7.7.5.3 Target Credit Count (TARGET_CREDIT_##) (+ offset varies)
6151 This register serves two purposes:
6152 • The Driver may write to this register to update (i.e., either increment or decrement) the credit counter for
6153 a particular I3C Target; or
6154 • The Driver may read this register to get the current credit counter for a particular I3C Target.
6155 This register exists within an array in the Extended Capability structure, and the index corresponds with the
6156 same index in the DAT. Therefore, this array has the same number of entries as the DAT, and each Target
6157 that can raise IBI Requests will require both a DAT entry and a register in this array, with the same index.
6158 The first instance of this register is at offset 0x0C from the start of the Extended Capabilities structure.
6159 Note:
6160 In the title of Table 92, the hash characters (“##”) represent the array index.

7.7.6 Dead Bus Recovery (ID = 0x0B)
6162 This Section defines the optional Capability-specific registers available under Extended Capability ID
6163 0x0B, Dead Bus Recovery. This capability includes a Dead Bus Recovery Mechanism that uses the I3C-
6164 defined Error Type DBR, which is defined as an optional recovery procedure at Section 5.1.10.1.8 of the
6165 I3C Specification [MIPI02]. A Host Controller may support this Extended Capability; if so, then it shall
6166 implement support for Error Type DBR handling in its I3C Bus Controller Logic, and shall also implement
6167 sufficient other logic to test for the presence of a dead I3C Bus (i.e., when there is no Active Controller that
6168 responds to a START Request).
6169 The Dead Bus Recovery Mechanism is intended to operate on its own, and also in cooperation with an
6170 optional Extended Capability that supports Standby Controller mode (i.e., acting as a Secondary Controller
6171 on the I3C Bus). The implementer may choose whether the Extended Capability for Standby Controller
6172 mode is implemented either (a) according to this I3C HCI Specification (i.e., per Section 6.17 and
6173 Section 7.7.11), or (b) within another vendor-defined Extended Capability, as long as the Host Controller
6174 can join the I3C Bus as either an Active Controller or a Standby Controller.
6175 The possible options for testing the I3C Bus to determine whether there is already an Active Controller
6176 (i.e., one that is responsive and active) might vary, depending on whether support for Standby Controller
6177 mode is also present.
7.7.6.1 Dead Bus Recovery Engage (DBR_ENGAGE) (+ 0x04)
6178 The Dead Bus Recovery Engage register is a write-only register that engages the Dead Bus Recovery
6179 mechanism, and attempts to test the I3C Bus for an Active Controller (i.e., not this Host Controller) that is
6180 active and responsive. Software shall write to this register to configure the Dead Bus Recovery mechanism
6181 and arm it for engagement, i.e., when a suitable Internal Control Command is enqueued (per
6182 Section 8.4.2.8).

Dead Bus Recovery mechanism to test the
I3C Bus.
Values:
• 3'd0: SDA_QUICK_RELEASE: If the
Active Controller responds, then release
SDA and do not drive any bits in the
Arbitrable Address Header.
• 3'd1: USE_IBI_ADDRESS: If the Active
Controller responds, then drive the I3C
Address provided in field
DBR_IBI_ADDRESS.
• 3'd2: USE_HJ_ADDRESS: If the Active
Controller responds, then simulate a
Hot-Join Request.
• 3'd3: USE_CR_DEVICE_ADDR: Use valid
field DYNAMIC_ADDRESS in register
CONTROLLER_DEVICE_ADDR
(Section 7.4.3), if and only if that
Address field is valid.
• 3'd4: Use implementer-defined logic
(i.e., Secondary Bus Controller Logic for
Standby Controller mode) to test the
I3C Bus, which automatically chooses
the initial role per Section 6.17.1.
• All other values: Reserved for future
use.
If the chosen Address wins Arbitration,
then the Host Controller shall not provide a
data payload for the IBI.

6187 register HC_CONTROL (see Section 7.4.2) must be set to DISABLED before using the Dead Bus

6192 Controller mode (i.e., by setting field BUS_ENABLE in register HC_CONTROL to 1'b1) and it shall
6193 become the Active Controller, per the I3C Specification at Section 5.1.10.1.8 [MIPI02].

7.7.8 Scheduled Commands for Handler Type 1 (ID = 0x0D)
6220 This Section defines the Capability-specific registers available under Extended Capability ID 0x0D,
6221 Scheduled Commands for Handler Type 1 (Simple Table). The Scheduled Commands capability is an
6222 optional capability that allows the Host Controller to issue certain Transfer Commands on a programmed
6223 schedule (see Section 6.16) while operating in Active Controller mode. The Host Controller uses registers
6224 to define the Scheduled Commands data structure that contains Command Descriptors and other
6225 configuration parameters relating to this instance of Scheduled Commands capability and its logic within
6226 the Host Controller.
6227 Note:
6228 This Extended Capability structure only applies to Handler Type 1 (Simple Table), as defined in
6229 Section 6.16.2.
6230 The data structure shall contain, in the following order:
6231 • A SCHEDULE_CAPABILITIES register (Section 7.7.8.1) that indicates the basic timing parameters and
6232 clock resolution as well as the size of the table of unique entries that might be configured by software for
6233 unique Transfer Commands.
6234 • A SCHEDULE_TABLE_LAYOUT register (Section 7.7.8.2) that defines this structure for Handler Type 1,
6235 and describes the sizes and layout of the Schedule Table Entries (i.e., data structures) available to
6236 software.
6237 • A SCHEDULE_CONFIG register (Section 7.7.8.3) that contains run-time control over the operation of this
6238 instance of Scheduled Commands logic and the number of entries that are enabled for programmed
6239 execution.
6240 These first three registers are required, and shall serve as a descriptor for the Extended Capability structure
6241 residing at a fixed offset relative to the starting offset for the structure (i.e., the instance of
6242 EXTCAP_HEADER).
6243 After these entries, the data structure shall contain a contiguous set of Schedule Table Entries arranged in
6244 an array. Each such array entry shall consist of a set of the following registers, identified by index “##”:
6245 • Registers SCHEDULE_TABLE_##_MASK (Section 7.7.8.4) and SCHEDULE_TABLE_##_CONFIG
6246 (Section 7.7.8.5). These registers shall be used to indicate the specific clock ticks at which the specific
6247 Transfer Command shall be executed, as well as how often the Transfer Command shall be executed (i.e.,
6248 only execute on every N-th cycle of ticks, if supported).
6249 • Registers to contain one Command Descriptor (i.e., SCHEDULE_TABLE_##_COMMAND, Section 7.7.8.6)
6250 to be executed according to the criteria above. The Command Descriptor shall be stored in an appropriate
6251 number of registers for the Host Controller’s supported Command Descriptor format (see Section 6.7 and
6252 Section 8.4).
6253 In this section, the index for such Schedule Table Entries may be in the range between 0 and the value of
6254 field MAX_COUNT in register SCHEDULE_CAPABILITIES. For simple configurations, this Extended
6255 Capability structure may contain a fixed number (i.e., up to 16) of Schedule Table Entries. For more
6256 advanced configurations, this Extended Capability structure might be defined with other variants based on
6257 alternative use models. Field SCHED_HANDLER in register SCHEDULE_TABLE_LAYOUT defines the overall
6258 format of the table and its registers.
6259 Note:
6260 Subsequent text and register field tables assume a handler method value of 0x1, where each
6261 Schedule Table Entry contains one Command Descriptor.
6262 Since the size of the Command Descriptor depends on the supported Command Descriptor format, both
6263 software and the Host Controller’s Scheduled Commands logic must understand the correct relationship,
6264 based on the entry sizes indicated in register SCHEDULE_TABLE_LAYOUT, in order to determine the location
6265 and layout of the table. Note that the entry size for the Schedule Table Entries might be larger than the
6266 required size of the sum of registers for schedule configuration and for the Command Descriptor, in order

7.7.8.4 Schedule Table Entry Mask (SCHEDULE_TABLE_##_MASK) (+ offset P varies)
6306 This register defines the bit mask to be applied (using bitwise logical AND) to the schedule tick interval
6307 number when determining when to execute the Command Descriptor in the corresponding Command
6308 Descriptor entry.
6309 Since the location and size of the Schedule Table Entries within the Extended Capability structure can vary,
6310 the offset of each instance of this register might also vary. The following formula gives the offset in
6311 DWORDs within the Extended Capability structure relative to the array index for the entry, where the index
6312 can range from 0 to MAX_COUNT:
6313 Offset = (2 + ENTRY_BASE_OFFSET + (sizeof(ENTRY_SIZE) × INDEX))
6314 Note:
6315 Field MAX_COUNT is found in register SCHEDULE_CAPABILITIES for this Schedule Table
6316 (Section 7.7.8.1). Fields ENTRY_BASE_OFFSET and ENTRY_SIZE are found in register
6317 SCHEDULE_TABLE_LAYOUT for this Schedule Table (Section 7.7.8.2).
6318 For the lowest possible value of field ENTRY_BASE_OFFSET (i.e., 0x2), the first instance of this register
6319 (i.e., index 0 in the Schedule Table Entries array) will reside at relative offset 0x10 bytes from the start of
6320 the Extended Capability structure. Each subsequent instance of this register would start at a further offset
6321 increment based on the Schedule Table Entry size, as indicated by field ENTRY_SIZE (in register
6322 SCHEDULE_TABLE_LAYOUT).
6323 Note:
6324 In the title of Table 102, the hash characters (“##”) represent the Schedule Table entry index.

6326 If the Host Controller supports Scheduled Commands on every N-th opportunity, then this register’s field
6327 N_TICKS defines the value of N. If N is greater than 1, then the Host Controller shall only process the
6328 schedule on the N-th iteration (i.e., shall treat the schedule as empty for the first (N − 1) tick horizons).
6329 Since the location and size of the Schedule Table Entries within the Extended Capability structure can vary,
6330 the offset of each instance of this register might also vary. The following formula gives the offset in

6332 can vary from 0 to MAX_COUNT:
6333 Offset = ( 3 + ENTRY_BASE_OFFSET + ( sizeof(ENTRY_SIZE) × INDEX) )

7.7.8.6 Schedule Table Entry Command Descriptor
(SCHEDULE_TABLE_##_COMMAND) (P + 0x8, etc.)
6346 Each Schedule Table Entry shall include registers containing the command(s) to be executed at the
6347 scheduled time(s). The number of registers shall be appropriate to store one complete Command Descriptor
6348 in the format supported by the Host Controller, as indicated by field CMD_SIZE in register HC_CAPABILITIES
6349 (Section 7.4.4).
6350 Note:
6351 The Schedule Table Entry Command Descriptor registers shall apply to handler method 0x0, which
6352 includes a single Command Descriptor with the Schedule Table Entry. In order to support this
6353 handler method, the Host Controller’s Schedule Table Entries must have a structure size with a
6354 minimum size of 4 DWORDs.
6355 Since the location and size of the Schedule Table Entries within the Extended Capability structure can vary,
6356 the offset of each instance of this register might also vary. The following formulas give the offset in
6357 DWORDs within the Extended Capability structure relative to the array index for the entry, where the index
6358 can vary from 0 to MAX_COUNT:
6359 Offset of first DWORD = ( 4 + ENTRY_BASE_OFFSET + ( sizeof(ENTRY_SIZE) × INDEX ) )
6360 Offset of second DWORD = ( 5 + ENTRY_BASE_OFFSET + ( sizeof(ENTRY_SIZE) × INDEX ) )
6361 Etc.
6362 Note:
6363 Field MAX_COUNT is found in register SCHEDULE_CAPABILITIES for this Schedule Table
6364 (Section 7.7.8.1). Fields ENTRY_BASE_OFFSET and ENTRY_SIZE are found in register
6365 SCHEDULE_TABLE_LAYOUT for this Schedule Table (Section 7.7.8.2).
6366 Within each Schedule Table Entry starting at DWORD offset E, the Command Descriptor registers will
6367 start at DWORD E+2 (i.e., byte offset 0x8) and continue in order, to contain all DWORDs for the single
6368 Command Descriptor. Note that DWORDs E+0 and E+1 hold the other per-Entry registers (see
6369 Section 7.7.8.4 and Section 7.7.8.5).
6370 Each of these two contiguous registers shall hold one DWORD of the Command Descriptor:
6371 • DWORD E+2 shall hold the first quarter (i.e. the first DWORD, Bits[31:0]); and
6372 • DWORD E+3 shall hold the second quarter (i.e. the second DWORD, Bits[63:32]).
6373 For the lowest possible value of field ENTRY_BASE_OFFSET (i.e., 0x2), the first register for the first
6374 instance of a Command Descriptor (i.e., for array index 0 in the array of Schedule Table Entries) will reside
6375 at relative offset 0x18 bytes from the start of the Extended Capability structure. Each subsequent instance
6376 of this first register for a Command Descriptor would have an offset increment based on the size of the
6377 Schedule Table Entry, as indicated by field ENTRY_SIZE (in register SCHEDULE_TABLE_LAYOUT).
6378 The Command Descriptor is defined in Section 8.4.
6379 Note:
6380 The hash characters (“##”) represent the Schedule Table Entry index.
6381 After executing a Transfer Command from a Schedule Table Entry, the Host Controller shall generate an
6382 IBI Status Descriptor (see Section 8.6.5) followed by IBI Data Chunks (as appropriate for the Transfer
6383 Command) to indicate the status of executing the Transfer Command.
6384 In this IBI Status Descriptor:
6385 • Field STATUS_TYPE shall be set to 3'b010.
6386 • Field ERROR shall be set to 1'b0 if the Transfer Command completed successfully, or 1'b1 if there was an
6387 error. For an error, the Host Controller may continue with the next Schedule Table Entry at the
6388 appropriate time, or it may stop execution entirely and report an interrupt to the Host (via field
6389 HC_INTERNAL_ERR_STAT in register INTR_STATUS, Section 7.4.7).
Copyright © 2018–2023 MIPI Alliance, Inc. 303

6390 • Field IBI_ID shall be set to a value that indicates the Transfer Command was executed by Scheduled
6391 Commands logic with Handler Type 1. Bits[11:8] shall indicate the Schedule Table Entry index, and
6392 Bits[15:12] shall be set to 1'b0.

7.7.9 Scheduled Commands for Handler Type 2 (ID = 0x0E)
6393 This Section defines the Capability-specific registers available under Extended Capability ID 0x0E,
6394 Scheduled Commands for Handler Type 2 (Command Sequence). The Scheduled Commands capability is
6395 an optional capability that allows the Host Controller to issue certain Transfer Commands on a programmed
6396 schedule (see Section 6.16) while operating in Active Controller mode. The Host Controller uses registers
6397 to define the Scheduled Commands data structure that contains Command Descriptors and other
6398 configuration parameters relating to this instance of Scheduled Commands capability and its logic within
6399 the Host Controller.
6400 Note:
6401 This Extended Capability structure only applies to Handler Type 2 (Command Sequence), as
6402 defined in Section 6.16.3.
6403 The data structure shall contain, in the following order:
6404 • A SCHEDULE_CAPABILITIES register (Section 7.7.9.1) that indicates the basic timing parameters and
6405 clock resolution that software can configure for unique Transfer Commands.
6406 • A SCHEDULE_LAYOUT register (Section 7.7.9.2) that defines this structure for Handler Type 2, and
6407 describes the layout of the Schedule Sequence (i.e., data structure) available to software.
6408 • A SCHEDULE_CONFIG register (Section 7.7.9.3) that contains run-time control over the operation of this
6409 instance of Scheduled Commands logic.
6410 These first three registers are required, and shall serve as a descriptor for the Extended Capability structure
6411 residing at a fixed offset relative to the starting offset for the structure (i.e., the instance of
6412 EXTCAP_HEADER).
6413 After these, the data structure shall contain arrays of registers that define the indicated Target Device(s) that
6414 will be used to execute the Command Descriptors, and the Command Descriptors to be executed. Registers
6415 that are defined in arrays are identified by index “##”:
6416 • Register SCHEDULE_SEQ_MASK (Section 7.7.9.4) indicates the specific clock ticks that will activate the
6417 execution of the command sequence for all configured Targets.
6418 • Register SCHEDULE_SEQ_CONFIG (Section 7.7.9.5) indicates how often the sequence of Transfer
6419 Commands shall be executed (i.e., only execute on every N-th cycle of ticks, if supported), and also the
6420 mask of which specific fields in subsequent registers contain valid Targets that will be used for executing
6421 the command sequence.
6422 • If the Host Controller is in DMA Mode, then this register also holds the Ring Bundle ID for the IBI
6423 Ring Pair to be used for any IBI Status Descriptors and optional IBI Data Chunks that will be
6424 generated as a result of processing Transfer Commands.
6425 • Registers SCHEDULE_SEQ_TARGETS_## (Section 7.7.9.6), with index from 0–3, allow the Driver to
6426 configure the command sequence to execute on specific Targets. This array has a minimum size of 1
6427 register (i.e., up to 4 Targets) and a maximum size of 4 registers (i.e., up to 16 Targets). Note that the
6428 previous register SCHEDULE_SEQ_CONFIG will determine which fields in these registers are valid (i.e.,
6429 will be used during execution iterations).
6430 • An additional array of registers contains one or more SCHEDULE_SEQ_COMMAND_## Command
6431 Descriptors (Section 7.7.9.7), to be executed according to the criteria above. Each Command Descriptor
6432 shall be stored in an appropriate number of registers for the Host Controller’s supported Command
6433 Descriptor format (see Section 6.7 and Section 8.4). The minimum size of this array is 2 Command
6434 Descriptors, and the maximum size of this array is 8 Command Descriptors, as indicated by field
6435 CMD_SEQ_LENGTH in register SCHEDULE_LAYOUT.
6436 The implementer may determine the sizes of the arrays, based on the use case. Field SCHED_HANDLER in
6437 register SCHEDULE_LAYOUT defines the overall format of the table and its registers.
6438 Note:
6439 Subsequent text and register field tables assume a handler method value of 0x2, which defines this
6440 structure for a command sequence and allows multiple Targets to be configured for execution.

7.7.9.4 Schedule Sequence Mask (SCHEDULE_SEQ_MASK) (+ offset P varies)
6478 This register defines the bit mask to be applied (using bitwise logical AND) to the schedule tick interval
6479 number when determining when the Host Controller shall start iterating over its configured Target Devices
6480 and executing the Command Descriptor sequence for each Target.
6481 Since the location and size of the Schedule Sequence registers within the Extended Capability structure can
6482 vary, the offset of this register might also vary. The following formula gives the offset in DWORDs within
6483 the Extended Capability structure, relative to the start of the structure:
6484 Offset = (2 + SEQ_BASE_OFFSET)
6485 Note:
6486 Field SEQ_BASE_OFFSET is found in register SCHEDULE_LAYOUT for this Extended capability
6487 structure (Section 7.7.9.2).
6488 Subsequent registers are described with offsets relative to this register, where the offset of this
6489 register is listed as P.
6490 For the lowest possible value of field SEQ_BASE_OFFSET (i.e., 0x2), the first Schedule Sequence register
6491 will reside at relative offset 0x10 bytes from the start of the Extended Capability structure.

7.7.9.5 Schedule Sequence Config (SCHEDULE_SEQ_CONFIG) (P + 0x4)
6493 If the Host Controller supports Scheduled Commands on every N-th opportunity, then this register’s field
6494 N_TICKS defines the value of N. If N is greater than 1, then the Host Controller shall only process the
6495 schedule on the N -th iteration (i.e., shall treat the schedule as empty for the first (N − 1) tick horizons).
6496 This register also defines which Target fields in the subsequent array SCHEDULE_SEQ_TARGETS_##
6497 registers to treat as valid. If the mask bit corresponding to a given Target is set to 1'b1, then the Host
6498 Controller shall include that Target field in these subsequent registers.
6499 Within the Extended Capabilities structure, this register immediately follows register
6500 SCHEDULE_SEQ_MASK (i.e., at offset P + 0x4). Since the location and size of the Schedule Sequence
6501 registers within the Extended Capability structure can vary, the offset of this register might also vary. The
6502 following formula gives the offset in DWORDs within the Extended Capability structure, relative to the
6503 start of the structure:
6504 Offset = (3 + SEQ_BASE_OFFSET)
6505 Note:
6506 Field SEQ_BASE_OFFSET is found in register SCHEDULE_LAYOUT for this Extended capability
6507 structure (Section 7.7.9.2).

7.7.9.6 Schedule Sequence Targets (SCHEDULE_SEQ_TARGETS_##) (P + 0x8, etc.)
6509 This register array defines which Target Devices will be included when the Host Controller iterates over the
6510 bit mask of valid Targets (i.e., those that are set to 1'b1 in field TARGET_MASK in register
6511 SCHEDULE_SEQ_CONFIG, Section 7.7.9.4). Each such register has 4 fields, each of which holds either the
6512 Target’s Address (if Transfer Command Format 2 is supported) or the Target’s DAT index (if Transfer
6513 Command Format 1 is supported).
6514 This array has a minimum size of 1 register and a maximum size of 4 registers. Implementers shall support
6515 at least one register (for up to 4 Targets) and may support up to four registers (for 16 Targets):
6516 • Register SCHEDULE_SEQ_TARGETS_00 (required) shall contain fields for Targets 0–3.
6517 These Targets are enabled and disabled by Bits[19:16] in field TARGET_MASK.
6518 • Register SCHEDULE_SEQ_TARGETS_01 (optional) shall contain fields for Targets 4–7.
6519 These Targets are enabled and disabled by Bits[23:20] in field TARGET_MASK.
6520 • Register SCHEDULE_SEQ_TARGETS_02 (optional) shall contain fields for Targets 8–11.
6521 These Targets are enabled and disabled by Bits[27:24] in field TARGET_MASK.
6522 • Register SCHEDULE_SEQ_TARGETS_03 (optional) shall contain fields for Targets 12–15.
6523 These Targets are enabled and disabled by Bits[31:28] in field TARGET_MASK.
6524 Any SCHEDULE_SEQ_TARGETS registers that are not implemented shall be read-only, with zero values.
6525 Within the Extended Capabilities structure, the first register in this array immediately follows register
6526 SCHEDULE_SEQ_CONFIG (i.e., offset P + 0x8). Since the location and size of the Schedule Sequence
6527 registers within the Extended Capability structure can vary, the offset of these registers might also vary. The
6528 following formula gives the offset in DWORDs within the Extended Capability structure, relative to the
6529 start of the structure:
6530 Offset of first register = (4 + SEQ_BASE_OFFSET)
6531 Offset of second register = (5 + SEQ_BASE_OFFSET)
6532 Offset of third register = (6 + SEQ_BASE_OFFSET)
6533 Offset of fourth register = (7 + SEQ_BASE_OFFSET)
6534 Etc.
6535 Note:
6536 Field SEQ_BASE_OFFSET is found in register SCHEDULE_LAYOUT for this Extended capability
6537 structure (Section 7.7.9.2).
6538 Subsequent registers for the Command Descriptors will start at 4 DWORDs after the first register
6539 (i.e., starting at offset P + 0x18).
6540
6541 For the lowest possible value of field SEQ_BASE_OFFSET (i.e., 0x2), the first instance of this register (i.e.,
6542 for array index 0) will reside at relative offset 0x14 bytes from the start of the Extended Capability
6543 structure. Each subsequent instance shall reside immediately after the previous instance.
6544 Note:
6545 In the title of Table 109, the hash characters (“##”) represent the index for the array of these
6546 registers.

7.7.9.7 Schedule Sequence Command Descriptor (SCHEDULE_SEQ_COMMAND_##)
(P + 0x18, etc.)
6548 The Extended Capability structure shall include registers containing the Transfer Commands to be executed
6549 at the scheduled time(s). The number of registers shall be sufficient to store between 2 and 8 complete
6550 Command Descriptors (as defined by field CMD_SEQ_LENGTH), where each Command Descriptor contains
6551 a Transfer Command in the format supported by the Host Controller, as indicated by field CMD_SIZE in the
6552 HC_CAPABILITIES register (see Section 7.4.4).
6553 Since the location and size of the Schedule Sequence Entries within the Extended Capability structure can
6554 vary, the offset of each register in this array might also vary. Within the Extended Capabilities structure, the
6555 first register in this array immediately follows the array of four SCHEDULE_SEQ_TARGETS registers, (i.e.,
6556 starting at offset P + 0x18).
6557 The following formulas give the offset in DWORDs within the Extended Capability structure relative to the
6558 array index for the entry, where the index can vary from 0 to CMD_SEQ_LENGTH:
6559 Offset of first Command Descriptor, first DWORD = (8 + SEQ_BASE_OFFSET)
6560 Offset of first Command Descriptor, second DWORD = (9 + SEQ_BASE_OFFSET)
6561 Offset of second Command Descriptor, first DWORD = (10 + SEQ_BASE_OFFSET)
6562 Offset of second Command Descriptor, second DWORD = (11 + SEQ_BASE_OFFSET)
6563 Etc.
6564 Note:
6565 Fields CMD_SEQ_LENGTH and SEQ_BASE_OFFSET are found in register SCHEDULE_LAYOUT for
6566 this Schedule Sequence (Section 7.7.9.2).
6567 For the lowest possible value of field SEQ_BASE_OFFSET (i.e., 0x2), the first register for the first Command
6568 Descriptor in this sequence will reside at relative offset 0x28 bytes from the start of the Extended
6569 Capability structure.
6570 The Command Descriptor is defined in Section 8.4.
6571 For each set of registers that holds a Command Descriptor in the array, the Driver shall write either:
6572 • A Command Descriptor containing a valid Transfer Command as defined in Section 6.16.3:
6573 The value of field CMD_ATTR shall be valid (i.e., shall indicate either a Regular Data Transfer
6574 Command or an Immediate Data Transfer Command).
6575 The Transfer Command shall have either:
6576 • For Broadcast CCCs: A value of 0x0 in the field that indicates the Target (since the Host Controller
6577 ignores the Target field for Broadcast CCCs); or
6578 • For any other transfer types: A value of 0x1 in the field that indicates the Target, i.e., either the DAT
6579 index or the Target Address, depending on the supported Transfer Command Format (since the Host
6580 Controller will substitute the Target based on the specific iteration that it is currently executing).
6581 Or:
6582 • An invalid Command Descriptor to signal the end of the sequence.
6583 The value 0x7 shall be used in field CMD_ATTR to inform the Host Controller that the sequence of
6584 Transfer Commands has ended, so that the Host Controller will stop execution (i.e., will not process
6585 this Command Descriptor).
6586 Note:
6587 The Scheduled Commands logic does not support Command Descriptors with the Command
6588 type “Internal Control”.
6589 For each iteration of the Transfer Commands sequence, the Host Controller shall begin by executing the
6590 first Command Descriptor in this array with the indicated Target, then continue executing the next
6591 Command Descriptor in the sequence, until it either runs out of Command Descriptors, or encounters an
318 Copyright © 2018–2023 MIPI Alliance, Inc.
Public Release Edition

Version 1.2 Specification for I3C HCI
15-Feb-2023
6592 error caused by a failed Transfer Command, or sees the value of 0x7 in field CMD_ATTR which signals the
6593 end of the sequence.
6594 After executing each Transfer Command in the sequence, the Host Controller shall generate an IBI Status
6595 Descriptor (see Section 8.6.5), followed by IBI Data Chunks as appropriate for the particular Transfer
6596 Command to indicate the status of executing the Transfer Command.
6597 • Field STATUS_TYPE shall be set to 3'b010.
6598 • Field ERROR shall be set to 1'b0 if the Transfer Command completed successfully, or 1'b1 if there was an
6599 error.
6600 For an error, no subsequent Transfer Commands in the sequence shall be executed for this Target.
6601 The Host Controller may then either iterate to the next valid Target (if indicated), or else stop
6602 execution entirely and report an interrupt to the Host via field HC_INTERNAL_ERR_STAT.
6603 • Field IBI_ID shall be set to a value that indicates which Command Descriptor in the array was executed,
6604 and shall also indicate that the Transfer Command was executed by Scheduled Commands logic with
6605 Handler Type 2. Bits[11:8] shall indicate the array index, Bit[12] shall be set to 1'b1, and Bits[15:13]
6606 shall contain the 3-bit instance identifier, field HT2_INST_ID.

7.7.10 Scheduled Commands for Handler Type 3 (ID = 0x0F)
6607 This Section defines the Capability-specific registers available under Extended Capability ID 0x0F,
6608 Scheduled Commands for Handler Type 3 (Schedule Buffer). The Scheduled Commands capability is an
6609 optional capability that allows the Host Controller to issue certain Transfer Commands on a programmed
6610 schedule (see Section 6.16) while operating in Active Controller mode. The Host Controller uses registers
6611 to describe and point to Host system memory that contains Transfer Descriptors and other configuration
6612 parameters relating to this instance of Scheduled Commands capability and its logic within the Host
6613 Controller.
6614 Note:
6615 This Extended Capability structure only applies to Handler Type 3 (Schedule Buffer), as defined in
6616 Section 6.16.4.
6617 The data structure shall contain, in the following order:
6618 • A SCHEDULE_CAPABILITIES register (Section 7.7.10.1) that indicates the basic timing parameters and
6619 clock resolution that software can configure for unique Transfer Commands.
6620 • A SCHEDULE_LAYOUT register (Section 7.7.10.2) that defines this structure for Handler Type 3, and
6621 describes the layout of additional registers.
6622 • A SCHEDULE_CONFIG register (Section 7.7.10.3) that contains run-time control over the operation of this
6623 instance of Scheduled Commands logic.
6624 These first three registers are required, and shall serve as a descriptor for the Extended Capability structure,
6625 residing at a fixed offset relative to the starting offset for the structure (i.e., the instance of
6626 EXTCAP_HEADER).
6627 After these, the data structure shall contain additional registers that configure, point to, and describe the
6628 Schedule Buffer:
6629 • Register SCHEDULE_BUF_MASK (Section 7.7.10.4) indicates the specific clock ticks that will activate the
6630 execution of the command sequence in the Schedule Buffer.
6631 • Register SCHEDULE_BUF_CONFIG (Section 7.7.10.5) indicates how often the Transfer Commands in the
6632 Schedule Buffer shall be executed (i.e., only execute on every N-th cycle of ticks, if supported) and also
6633 where the Host Controller will return read data from Transfer Commands.
6634 • If the Host Controller is in DMA Mode, then this register also holds the Ring Bundle ID for the IBI
6635 Ring Pair to be used for any IBI Status Descriptors and optional IBI Data Chunks that will be
6636 generated as a result of processing Transfer Commands.
6637 • Registers SCHEDULE_BUF_DESCR (Section 7.7.10.6), SCHEDULE_BUF_BASE_LO (Section 7.7.10.7), and
6638 SCHEDULE_BUF_BASE_HI (Section 7.7.10.8) describe and point to the Host system memory that contains
6639 the Schedule Buffer (i.e., an array of Transfer Descriptors).
6640 • Note that a Host Controller that supports Handler Type 3 also implicitly supports Scatter-Gather
6641 capabilities for the Host system memory that holds the Schedule Buffer (per Section 6.2.1).
6642 Field SCHED_HANDLER in register SCHEDULE_LAYOUT defines the overall format of the table and its
6643 registers.
6644 Note:
6645 Subsequent text and register field tables assume a handler method value of 0x3, which defines this
6646 structure for a Schedule Buffer that software may populate with Transfer Descriptors.

6688 schedule on the N-th iteration (i.e., shall treat the schedule as empty for the first (N − 1) tick horizons).

7.7.10.9 Transfer Descriptors in Schedule Buffer
6747 The Schedule Buffer contains one or more Transfer Descriptors to be executed at the scheduled time. The
6748 Host must allocate a region of system memory that is large enough for the use case. The Schedule Buffer
6749 can hold up to 255 Transfer Descriptors, where each Transfer Descriptor contains a Transfer Command in
6750 the format supported by the Host Controller, as indicated by field CMD_SIZE in the HC_CAPABILITIES
6751 register (see Section 7.4.4).
6752 The Command Descriptor is defined in Section 8.4 and the Transfer Descriptor is defined in Section 8.3.
6753 Note:
6754 The size of the Transfer Descriptor used by Handler Type 3 is the same as the Transfer Descriptor
6755 size for supported Ring Bundles, as defined by field XFER_STRUCT_SIZE in register CR_SETUP
6756 (Section 7.6.10.1). DWORDs 0 and 1 contain the Command Descriptor, DWORD 2 contains the
6757 Data Buffer Descriptor fields, and DWORDS 3 and 4 contain the Data Buffer Pointer.
6758 For each Transfer Descriptor that holds a Command Descriptor in the array, the Driver shall provide either:
6759 • A Command Descriptor containing a valid Transfer Command as defined in Section 6.16.3:
6760 The value of field CMD_ATTR shall be valid (i.e., shall indicate either a Regular Data Transfer
6761 Command or an Immediate Data Transfer Command).
6762 The Transfer Command shall have either:
6763 • For Broadcast CCCs: A value of 0x0 in the field that indicates the Target (since the Host Controller
6764 ignores the Target field for Broadcast CCCs); or
6765 • For any other transfer types: A value of 0x1 in the field that indicates the Target, i.e., either the DAT
6766 index or the Target Address, depending on the supported Transfer Command Format (since the Host
6767 Controller will substitute the Target based on the specific iteration that it is currently executing).
6768 Or:
6769 • An invalid Command Descriptor to signal the end of the Schedule Buffer:
6770 The value 0x7 shall be used in field CMD_ATTR to inform the Host Controller that the valid Transfer
6771 Descriptors have ended, so that the Host Controller will stop execution (i.e., will not process this
6772 Transfer Descriptor).
6773 Note:
6774 The Scheduled Commands logic does not support Command Descriptors with the Command
6775 type “Internal Control”.
6776 At each opportunity to start execution, the Host Controller shall begin by processing the first Transfer
6777 Descriptor in this Schedule Buffer, then continue processing the next Transfer Descriptors, until it either
6778 runs out of valid Transfer Descriptors in the Schedule Buffer, or encounters an error caused by a failed
6779 Transfer Command, or sees the value of 0x7 in field CMD_ATTR which signals the end of valid Transfer
6780 Descriptors in the Schedule Buffer.
6781 Note:
6782 The Host Controller shall not execute the Schedule Buffer while field RESPONSE_STEERING and
6783 field EXECUTED (in register SCHEDULE_BUF_CONFIG) both contain 1'b1. Such values indicate that
6784 a previous execution of the Schedule Buffer generated read data, but the Host has not yet
6785 consumed it from the Data Buffer Descriptors. The Host must first consume this read data, and
6786 then clear field EXECUTED, before the Host Controller will resume execution of the Schedule Buffer.
6787 After executing each Transfer Command in the Schedule Buffer, the Host Controller shall generate an IBI
6788 Status Descriptor (see Section 8.6.5) followed by optional IBI Data Chunks with read data (as appropriate
6789 for the Transfer Command) to indicate the status of executing the Transfer Command, but only if field
6790 RESPONSE_STEERING has a value of 1'b0. If, on the other hand, the value of field RESPONSE_STEERING is
6791 1'b1, then the read data shall instead be written into the Data Buffer Descriptor for its Transfer Descriptor.
6792 Within each IBI Status Descriptor:
334 Copyright © 2018–2023 MIPI Alliance, Inc.
Public Release Edition

Version 1.2 Specification for I3C HCI
15-Feb-2023
6793 • Field STATUS_TYPE shall be set to 3'b010.
6794 • Field ERROR shall be set to 1'b0 if the Transfer Command completed successfully, or 1'b1 if there was an
6795 error.
6796 For an error, no subsequent Transfer Commands in the Schedule Buffer shall be executed. The Host
6797 Controller shall stop execution entirely and report an interrupt to the Host via field
6798 HC_INTERNAL_ERR_STAT.
6799 • Field IBI_ID shall be set to a value that indicates that one or more Transfer Commands were executed by
6800 Scheduled Commands logic with Handler Type 3. Bit[12] shall be set to 1'b1, and Bits[15:13] shall
6801 contain the 3-bit instance identifier, field HT3_INST_ID.
6802 Note:
6803 Since the Scheduled Commands logic does not know the actual number of valid Transfer
6804 Descriptors in the Schedule Buffer when it starts execution, it is possible for many IBI Status
6805 Descriptors (and optional IBI Data Chunks) to be generated, which the Host must consume in a
6806 timely manner. In situations when the Host does not consume these from either the IBI Port (in PIO
6807 Mode) or the configured IBI Ring Pair (in DMA Mode), and the Queue or Ring becomes full, the
6808 Host Controller must temporarily stall execution of Transfer Descriptors in the Schedule Buffer until
6809 the Host resolves the situation by consuming IBI Status Descriptors (and optional IBI Data Chunks,
6810 depending on the value of field RESPONSE_STEERING). If the stall becomes a timeout, then the
6811 Host Controller shall stop processing and report the error. Such conditions will be reported to the
6812 Host as interrupts; refer to fields HC_WARN_CMD_SEQ_STALL_STAT and
6813 HC_ERR_CMD_SEQ_TIMEOUT_STAT in register INTR_STATUS (see Section 7.4.7).
6814 At the end of execution, if field RESPONSE_STEERING in register SCHEDULE_BUF_CONFIG has a value of
6815 1'b1, then the Host Controller shall set field EXECUTED to 1'b1 and then prevent subsequent execution
6816 attempts until the Host clears field EXECUTED at a later time.

| 7.7.11                      | Standby Controller Mode (ID = 0x12)  |     |     |              |
6817  This  Section  defines  the  Capability-specific  registers  available  under  Extended  Capability  ID  0x12,
6818  Standby Controller mode. These registers define the capabilities of, and affect the configuration and control
6819  of, the Host Controller’s Secondary Controller Logic. This logic is activated while the Host Controller is
6820  operating in Standby Controller mode, i.e., is in a Secondary Controller role.
6821  For these registers, fields that the Host may change are indicated as either R/W or R/cW in the register
6822  field tables, and fields that are read-only to the Host are indicated as R. The intent and purpose of each field
6823  is described either in the register field tables, or in the subsections.
6824  Some configuration fields (indicated as R/cW, meaning Read, conditional Write) are only writeable while
6825  the Host Controller’s Secondary Controller Logic is inactive (i.e., disabled). R/cW fields are read-only
6826  from the Host while the Host Controller is operating in Standby Controller mode (i.e., while field
6827  STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register STBY_CR_CONTROL is set to a non-zero value; see Section 7.7.11.1).
6828  Many such fields defined as conditionally writeable are used for initial configuration, and might be
6829  returned  as  response  data  on  the  I3C  Bus  for  certain  standard  CCCs  or  during  Dynamic Address
6830  Assignment, thereby providing information to the Active Controller of the I3C Bus. Since this data
6831  provided to the Active Controller would be treated as a contract, any changes desired by Host software
6832  might not be visible to the Active Controller, as the Active Controller would rely on the data being
6833  transferred  during  Bus  Enumeration  or  any  phases  of  initial  configuration  (e.g.,  Dynamic Address
6834  Assignment with ENTDAA). The Host Controller shall block writes to such fields indicated as R/cW from
6835  the Host while the Secondary Controller Logic is enabled, in order to prevent a violation of contract or
6836  other errors that might arise from mismatched expectations or deviations from previously agreed behavior.
6837  Such fields may only be written from the Host while the Secondary Controller Logic is disabled, and would
6838  typically require the Host Controller to re-join the I3C Bus.
6839  Other register fields might be read-only to the Host, but are updated by the Secondary Controller Logic
6840  during the course of normal operation, as a result of changing conditions or new status based on I3C Bus
6841  activity (such as receiving certain CCCs with data messages or Defining Byte values). The register field
6842  tables in subsections below indicate these fields, along with any special considerations for implementers
6843  and software developers.

1 ACR_FSM_OP_SELECT R/W 0x1 Active Controller Select
[2] or Permits the Device to (1) Accept the
R/cW Controller Role while operating in
Standby Controller mode, and (2) Send
the GETACCCR CCC while operating in
Active Controller mode.
When read by software, this bit indicates
the desired state for the Host Controller
i.e., the “transition to” state). This bit
should be interpreted in combination with
field AC_CURRENT_OWN in register
PRESENT_STATE which reflects the
Controller Role (i.e., SCL Line driving
status).
Values for Active Controller mode:
• 1'b0: HANDOFF_READY_SEND: The
Host Controller is prepared to accept
a Command Descriptor for the
GETACCCR CCC from software. It
shall be accepted as long as all pre-
Handoff conditions remain true (see
Section 6.17.2).
• 1'b1: BUS_OWNER: The Host
Controller retains the Controller Role
and is not prepared to send a
GETACCCR CCC.
Values for Standby Controller mode:
• 1'b0: NOT_BUS_OWNER: The Host
Controller is not in transition to the
Active Controller state, and will not
accept the Controller Role.
• 1'b1: HANDOFF_READY_RECV: The
Host Controller is ready to accept the
Controller Role via the GETACCCR
CCC (see Section 6.17.4).
1 HANDOFF_DELAY_NACK R/W1C 0x0 Handoff Delay NACK
[1] Indicates whether the Device shall NACK
any attempt to receive the Controller
Role via GETACCCR CCC, due to being
busy processing a DEFTGTS CCC or
any DEFGRPA CCCs sent by the Active
Controller.
The Secondary Controller Logic shall
automatically set this bit to 1'b1 if it
detects any incoming Broadcast
DEFTGTS or DEFGRPA CCCs.
Software may clear this bit by writing the
value 1'b1 (i.e., write 1 to clear) after
processing these CCCs.
This bit is also used for automatic
response to GETSTATUS Format 2 CCC
with PRECR Defining Byte (see
Section 6.17.3.1.1).

7.7.11.2 Standby Controller Device Address (STBY_CR_DEVICE_ADDR) (+ 0x08)
6848 This register holds the Host Controller’s Dynamic Address and Static Address while operating in Standby
6849 Controller mode. The Secondary Controller Logic uses these fields to match incoming I3C tranasctions,
6850 and during Dynamic Address Assignment (see Section 6.17.1 and Section 6.17.3).

Size Memory Reset
Field Name Description
[Bits] Access Value
1 DYNAMIC_ADDR_VALID R 0x0 Dynamic Address is Valid
[31] Indicates whether or not the value in the
DYNAMIC_ADDR field is valid.
This bit is also visible from register
CONTROLLER_DEVICE_ADDR (Section 7.4.3). It
may be changed from that register, but only
while the Controller is operating in Active
Controller mode.
While operating in Standby Controller mode, the
Host Controller shall set this bit to 1'b1 when the
Primary Controller assigns the Dynamic Address
(i.e., during the ENTDAA or
SETDASA/SETAASA process).
Values:
• 1'b0: DYNAMIC_ADDR field is not valid
• 1'b1: DYNAMIC_ADDR field is valid
8 RESERVED R 0x0 –
[30:23]
7 DYNAMIC_ADDR R 0x0 Device Dynamic Address
[22:16] Contains the Host Controller Device’s Dynamic
Address. The Host Controller uses this I3C
Address to respond to I3C Transactions as a
Target or Secondary Controller.
This Dynamic Address is also visible from
register CONTROLLER_DEVICE_ADDR
(Section 7.4.3). It may be changed from that
register, but only while the Host Controller is
operating in Active Controller mode.
While operating in Standby Controller mode, the
Host Controller sets this field to the Address
assigned by the Primary Controller during
Dynamic Address Assignment (i.e., during the
ENTDAA or SETDASA/SETAASA procedure),
or by subsequent use of the SETNEWDA CCC.

1 STATIC_ADDR_VALID R/cW 0x0 Static Address is Valid
[15] Indicates whether or not the value in the
STATIC_ADDR field is valid.
While the Host Controller is configured for
Standby Controller mode, software may set this
bit to 1'b1 before enabling Secondary Controller
Bus operation in register STBY_CR_CONTROL
(i.e., before the SETDASA/SETAASA process).
This field is Read-Only while field
STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register
STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1) is not
zero.
Values:
• 1'b0: The Static Address field is not valid; the
Host Controller may only participate in
Dynamic Address Assignment with ENTDAA
(if implemented and enabled).
• 1'b1: The Static Address field is valid; the
Host Controller may respond to SETDASA
and/or SETAASA per the configuration in
register STBY_CR_CONTROL.
8 RESERVED R 0x0 –
[14:7]
7 STATIC_ADDR R/cW 0x0 Device Static Address
[6:0] This field contains the Host Controller Device’s
Static Address. If field STATIC_ADDR_VALID is
set to 1'b1, then the Host Controller shall use
this Static Address when responding to
SETDASA and/or SETAASA, if the relevant
fields in register STBY_CR_CONTROL are set.
While the Controller is configured for Standby
Controller mode, software may set this field to a
valid I3C Address before enabling Secondary
Controller Bus operation in register
STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1).
This field is Read-Only while field
STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register
STBY_CR_CONTROL (Section 7.7.11.1) is not
zero.
6852 Note:
6853 This register shall be used only when the Host Controller is operating in Standby Controller mode.
6854 Register CONTROLLER_DEVICE_ADDR is intended for use in Active Controller mode.
6855 Use of a Static Address in Secondary Controller operation requires prior configuration on the
6856 Primary Controller of the I3C Bus. For most use cases, Dynamic Address Assignment with the
6857 ENTDAA CCC is the recommended option.

6871 Requests must be supported if Dynamic Address Assignment with ENTDAA is supported.

6873 Logic, as this is the defined mechanism for a Secondary Controller to request the Controller Role
6874 from the Active Controller of the I3C Bus. Field SIMPLE_CRR_SUPPORT should have a value of
6875 1'b1, except for special use cases where the Host Controller never sends a Controller Role

1 HJ_REQ_STATUS R 0x0 Hot-Join Request Status
[8] Indicates the status of a pending or
attempted Hot-Join Request, if the
Driver had previously written 2'b11 to
field STBY_CR_ENABLE_INIT in register
STBY_CR_CONTROL to make such a

[7:5] Status
Indicates the status of a pending or
attempted Controller Role Request, if
the Driver had previously written to field
CR_REQUEST_SEND in register
STBY_CR_CONTROL to make such a
request (see Section 6.17.3.3).
Values:
• 3'b000: No pending request. This is
the default reset value.
• 3'b001: The request is pending, but
has not yet been attempted due to
Bus Available Condition.
• 3'b010: The request was attempted,
but was NACKed by the Active
Controller.
• 3'b011: The request was attempted,
but the Active Controller NACKed it
and sent the DISEC CCC with the
DISCR bit set to disable further
Controller Role Requests.
• 3'b100: The request was attempted
and the Active Controller ACKed it.
All other values: Reserved for future
use.

7.7.11.7 Standby Controller Interrupt Status (STBY_CR_INTR_STATUS) (+ 0x20)
6886 This register reflects the status of outstanding interrupts relating to Standby Controller mode and the related
6887 I3C Secondary Controller Logic. This includes:
6888 • Outstanding interrupts relating to Standby Controller mode operations, and
6889 • Outstanding interrupts relating to transitions between Active Controller mode and Standby Controller
6890 mode (and vice versa).
6891 The status fields are indicated as either:
6892 • R/W1C (i.e., Write 1 to Clear) if cleared by software. R/W1C is used for original interrupt sources.
6893 Or
6894 • R (i.e., read only) if cleared by hardware based on other operations to the interrupt register sets.
6895 The bit fields in this register act as Status Bits, according to the interrupt register model described in
6896 Section 6.14.
6897 These bits shall be set (i.e., the “Status bit set” action will occur) if the associated interrupt status or event is
6898 detected. The interrupt events or status in this register shall only be enabled for reporting (i.e., for assertion
6899 via trigger to register STBY_CR_INTR_SIGNAL_EN) under any of the following conditions:
6900 • If the Host Controller is operating in Active Controller mode and is preparing to transition into Standby
6901 Controller mode (see Section 6.17.2);
6902 • If the Host Controller is operating in Standby Controller mode as a Secondary Controller role on the I3C
6903 Bus (see Section 6.17.3).
6904 If an I3C Target Transaction Interface to Software is supported and enabled, then certain interrupt
6905 conditions shall also be reported for Write-Type transfers that are sent by the Active Controller of the
6906 I3C Bus but which the I3C Secondary Controller Logic did not autonomously service (see
6907 Section 6.17.3);
6908 • If the Host Controller is preparing to transition into Active Controller mode, and is ready to accept the
6909 Controller Role from the Active Controller (see Section 6.17.4); or
6910 • If the Host Controller has just passed the Controller Role to another Controller-capable Device (i.e., a
6911 Secondary Controller) but the new Active Controller did not assert its Controller Role (i.e., an Error Type
6912 CE3 condition occurred), so the Host Controller was forced to reclaim the Controller Role and resume
6913 operation in Active Controller mode.
6914 If the Host Controller is operating in Active Controller mode and is not preparing to pass the Controller
6915 Role to any indicated Controller-capable Device (i.e., to a Secondary Controller on the I3C Bus), then the
6916 interrupt events or status in this register shall be not be enabled for reporting in this register.

8 Data Structures
6948 This Section describes several data structures used by the Host Controller.
6949 Note:
6950 Some of these data structures are implemented as HCI Registers, and as a result do not appear in
6951 the memory that the software Driver allocates.
8.1 Device Address Table (DAT)
6952 The DAT table stores the Device Addresses of Target Devices attached to the I3C Bus, plus several control
6953 and information fields per Device. The DAT may be either implemented as part of the HCI Register Set
6954 (i.e., may be implemented via regular registers) or placed in Driver-allocated memory as part of Device
6955 Context (see Section 6.3.3). In this section the DAT is presented in structure form for easier understanding.
6956 When used for Transfer Commands and automatic response to I3C Bus conditions, the DAT must contain
6957 one entry for each attached Target Device with an assigned Dynamic Address. A DAT entry must also be
6958 allocated for each assigned Group Address, if supported (see Section 6.4.3).
6959 Each entry in the DAT has the structure shown in Table 130. For Command types that require DAT table
6960 entries, DAT table entries are indexed by the Command’s DEV_INDEX field. Register DAT_SECTION_OFFSET
6961 (see Section 7.4.11) in the Capabilities registers section (see Section 7.3.1) indicates the offset to the DAT
6962 and the number of entries in the DAT.
6963 The DAT is populated by software, and hardware uses it during the Dynamic Address Assignment
6964 procedure. Per-Device prioritization of IBIs from Target Devices can be set via Driver software control
6965 over the Dynamic Address Arbitration procedure.
6966 Note:
6967 If the DAT is placed in Driver-allocated memory, then software should use the Internal Control
6968 Command with sub-command 0x3 for Device Context Update (see Section 8.4.2.3) to inform the
6969 Host Controller of any changes to DAT entries, as and when such changes are written by software.
6970 Each valid DAT entry contains the Device’s Static Address (if applicable) and its Dynamic Address (if
6971 configured). This specification supports 7-bit Target Device Addresses. If the Device is addressed via
6972 Dynamic Address, then the Static Address shall not be used. The Static Address shall only be used for I3C
6973 Target Devices that support Dynamic Address Assignment with the SETDASA CCC, and for I2C Target
6974 Devices (which must always have Static Addresses).
6975 The size of each DAT entry is 2 DWORDs.

8.1.1 DAT Usage for Transfer Commands
6980 The DAT entry’s scope of usage requires software to assign (i.e., to allocate) DAT entries for all known
6981 Target Devices that will be used for Transfer Commands.
6982 • Every Target Device shall have its own DAT entry for Transfer Commands.
6983 Software shall include an index into the DAT table for all Transfer Commands that address a specific
6984 Target Device by its Dynamic Address, or for Write-Type Transfer Commands that address a Group
6985 Address (if configured and supported).
6986 Broadcast CCCs do not use DAT entries, per Section 6.7.
6987 Additionally, most commands used for Dynamic Address Assignment also require DAT entries for all target
6988 Devices that are found, or are expected to be found. Specifically, the Address Assignment Commands (see
6989 Section 8.4.1) require DAT entries for the ENTDAA and SETDASA CCCs.
6990 Note:
6991 This puts an upper limit of 32 possible unique I3C Addresses, including the sum of assigned
6992 Dynamic Addresses and Group Addresses, on an I3C Bus that is used with an I3C Controller that
6993 complies with this I3C HCI Specification. If additional I3C Addresses are assigned, then such I3C
6994 Devices cannot all be addressed simultaneously by such an I3C Controller. Note that this upper
6995 limit might be reduced for Host Controller implementations that implement a smaller DAT (e.g., a
6996 reduced number of DAT entries as a Register Set).
8.1.2 DAT Addressing and Parity Bit
6997 Software shall provide the Dynamic Address and Parity Bit, written into field DYNAMIC_ADDRESS of a
6998 particular DAT entry before using it. This field must be written before any use of an Address Assignment
6999 Command, or any Transfer Command. The Dynamic Address shall be written into Bits[22:16], and the
7000 Parity Bit shall be written into Bit[23].
7001 Any DAT entry with a Dynamic Address of 7'h00 shall be considered to be disabled by the Host Controller,
7002 and shall not be valid for Transfer Commands. Such a DAT entry shall also not be matched for any
7003 incoming IBIs, as this Dynamic Address is a reserved I3C Address, per the I3C Specification [MIPI02] at
7004 Section 5.1.2.2.5.
7005 The Parity Bit is used for Dynamic Address Assignment with the ENTDAA CCC, per the I3C Specification
7006 [MIPI02] at Section 5.1.4.2. The Parity Bit shall be calculated using an inverse XOR of the Dynamic
7007 Address:
7008 PARITY = ~XOR( ADDR[6:0] )
7009 Software shall calculate the Parity Bit, and the Host Controller may choose to either use the Parity Bit
7010 written into Bit[23], or else ignore Bit[23] and calculate the Parity Bit directly from the Dynamic Address
7011 (i.e., from Bits[22:16]).
7012 Note:
7013 The implementer may determine whether the Host Controller will use the provided value for the
7014 Parity Bit in Bit[23], or automatically calculate the correct Parity Bit value based on the Dynamic
7015 Address alone.

8.2  Device Characteristic Table (DCT)
7016  The DCT table captures the Device Characteristics (PID, BCR, and DCR) and assigned Dynamic Address
7017  of each Device on the I3C Bus that participates in the Dynamic Address Allocation (ENTDAA) procedure.
7018  The DCT table is considered to be either part of the HCI Register Set (i.e., implemented as regular
registers), or else placed in Driver-allocated memory as part of Device Context (see Section 6.3.3). In this
7019
7020  section it is presented in structure form for easier understanding.
7021  Note:
7022  If the DCT is placed in Driver-allocated memory, then the Driver should not write to the DCT entries.
7023  Register DCT_SECTION_OFFSET (see Section 7.4.12), located in the Capabilities registers section (see
Section 7.3.1), indicates the offset to the DCT and the number of entries in the DCT.
7024
7025  The DCT contains one entry for each Device, and each entry has the structure shown in Table 131.

8.3 Transfer Descriptor
7027 Note:
7028 This section applies only for Host Controller implementations that implement DMA Mode, and thus
7029 connect to a System Bus that supports memory-mapped IO and DMA.
7030 The Transfer Descriptor is a structure put on Command/Response Rings in order to perform the transfer.
7031 The Transfer Descriptor is composed of a single Command Descriptor structure, and either a Data Buffer
7032 Pointer or an array of Data Buffer Pointers:
7033 • If the buffer for a requested transfer is organized as a single block of contiguous physical memory, then
7034 the Data Buffer Pointer within the Transfer Descriptor points directly to that memory block. Its field BLP
7035 shall have a value of 1'b0.
7036 • For Scatter-Gather Buffers, which are composed of multiple, usually smaller, non-contiguous blocks of
7037 physical memory, the array of Data Buffer Pointers is used. A list of multiple Data Buffer Pointers is
7038 provided, with each Data Buffer Pointer pointing to a separate memory blocks. The Data Buffer Pointer
7039 within the Transfer Descriptor shall act as a Data Buffer List Pointer that points to the array of Memory
7040 Descriptor structures (see Section 8.7), and its field BLP shall have a value of 1'b1.
7041 The Transfer Descriptor is a minimum of 5 DWORDs in size: 2 DWORDs for the Command Descriptor per
7042 Section 6.7, and 3 DWORDs for the Data Buffer Descriptor (including its Data Buffer Pointer), per
7043 Section 8.3.1.
7044 Note:
7045 The first DWORD (i.e., DW0) of the Transfer Descriptor is always the low DWORD of the Command
7046 Descriptor. Per Section 7.6.10.1, an implementer may define a larger Transfer Descriptor size,
7047 indicated in field XFER_STRUCT_SIZE of register CR_SETUP. If so, then the first 2 DWORDs shall
7048 consist of the Command Descriptor, the next 3 DWORDs shall consist of the Data Buffer
7049 Descriptor, and any additional DWORDs may be used for vendor-specific extensions.
7050 Figure 49 shows one example of Scatter-Gather Buffers (i.e., using an array of Data Buffer Pointers), and
7051 one example of contiguous memory transfers (i.e., using just a single Data Buffer Pointer).
